sections.heading: What Access catalogs is for
sections.body: "Access and retailer catalogs" holds the shared dropdown lists used across the dashboard: access roles, site types, retailer packs, size bands, recommendation categories, subscription plans, and domain ownership. A panel called "What these catalogs control" explains what each list affects. Each list opens as its own section at /admin/access-catalogs/[section], and the "Back to Access catalogs" link takes you back to the main page. Each list is a table with a search box ("Search by name or code"), row actions, and an add button at the top. Rows marked "Shared" are shared rows, which a platform super admin edits.

sections.heading: Search and move through a list
sections.body: Type in the "Search by name or code" box above a table to narrow the rows. If nothing matches you will see "[No rows match your search]". Longer lists are split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages, where the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed.

sections.heading: Edit, deactivate, or remove a row
sections.body: Each row has an "Actions" column with icon buttons. 1) Click "Edit" to change the row. 2) Change the fields. 3) Save, or click "Cancel" to leave without saving. "Deactivate" turns a row off, and "Remove" deletes it. If a removal does not go through, you will see "Remove failed". Rows marked "Shared" or "Shared with every tenant" are edited by a platform super admin.

sections.heading: Access roles
sections.body: In "Access roles", click "Add role" to open "Add access role". Each role has a "Code", a "Label", and a "Location scope" ("None", "Assigned locations", or "All locations"). A role can also open the admin menu, which shows as "Opens the admin menu". The role table shows "Admin menu", "Locations", and "Scope" columns. The "Platform super admin" role stays limited to the shared catalog. You will see "The access role was added." or "The access role was updated." after saving.

sections.heading: Site types and retailer packs
sections.body: "Site types" lists the organization site type. A shop is RETAIL. To add one, click "Add site type". A retailer pack belongs to a site type: shops use RETAIL, then a pack such as gas station or liquor store. 1) Open "Retailer packs". 2) Click "Add type" to open "Add retailer pack". 3) Choose the "Site type" and fill in the code and label. 4) Save. Existing packs can be changed with "Edit retailer pack". Messages like "The retailer pack was added." confirm the save.

sections.heading: Size bands
sections.body: Each size band belongs to one retailer type. Gas uses single, mid, and enterprise, and other packs start with one standard band. 1) Open "Size bands" and click "Add band". 2) Choose the "Retailer type". 3) Fill in the "Minimum locations" and "Maximum locations". 4) Save. A blank upper limit (shown as "No limit") means no maximum.

sections.heading: Recommendation categories
sections.body: These are the card kinds for the morning list. A new kind is a row here, and the card status list stays fixed. 1) Open "Recommendation categories" and click "Add category". 2) Fill in the fields, such as "Code", "Label", "Module", and "Sort order". 3) Click "Update category" when editing, or save when adding. Use "Active" to show whether a category is in use.

sections.heading: Subscription plans and domain ownership
sections.body: "Subscription plans" supplies the plan names on the onboarding form and on each tenant's subscription panel. Click "Add plan" to add one. Basic, Professional, and Enterprise stay in the shared list. "Domain ownership" supplies the choices on a new onboarding request and on Get Started. Click "Add ownership" to add one. The three built-in choices stay in the shared list. In both lists, the saved value is the code, so choose it carefully.

sections.heading: Rules and tips
sections.body: Pick the organization before adding a row for that tenant. Shared rows stay available to every organization. The code is what gets stored, and the label is the name people see. "Sort order" sets the position in the list. After saving you will see a confirmation such as "The site type was added." If saving fails, "Could not save" appears. Use "Cancel" to close a form without saving.

sections.heading: What the Batch Job Dashboard is for
sections.body: The "Batch Job Dashboard" at /admin/batch-jobs shows how background (batch) jobs are doing. At the top are count cards: "Total executions", "Completed", "Failed" and "Running". Below them is the "Job executions" list with filters, plus side panels for "Running now", "Recent failures" and "Configured jobs". The "Retail file run" panel lets you run a retail sample or an uploaded file right away. Use the reload button ("Reload") to refresh the data.

sections.heading: Read the summary counts
sections.body: The cards at the top give a quick health check: "Total executions" is all runs, "Completed" is runs that finished, "Failed" is runs that failed, and "Running" is runs in progress now. Use them to see at a glance whether anything needs attention. If "Failed" is above zero, check "Recent failures" or filter the list by status.

sections.heading: Search and filter job executions
sections.body: In the "Job executions" section, you can narrow the list. 1) Type part of a job's name in the "Job name" box (it shows "Contains…"). 2) Pick a value in "Status", or leave "All statuses". 3) Select "Filter" (the "Apply filters" button). The list updates to match. If nothing matches you will see "No job executions found" or "No executions found".

sections.heading: Browse pages and reload
sections.body: The list shows its rows in pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" (also labeled "Previous Page" and "Next Page") to move between pages. The line with "Page" and "Showing" tells you where you are in the list. Select "Reload" to fetch the latest data. If the refresh does not work, you will see "Failed to reload batch jobs".

sections.heading: Open an execution's details
sections.body: Each row in "Job executions" shows "Job", "Status", "Started", "Ended", "Exit" and "Detail". 1) In the "Detail" column, select "View" ("View execution detail"). 2) Wait while "Loading full execution details…" appears. 3) Read "Status", "Exit code", "Started", "Ended", "Created", "Last updated", "Exit message" and "Raw payload". 4) Select "Close" when finished. The exit message is useful for understanding why a job failed.

sections.heading: Running now, recent failures and configured jobs
sections.body: "Running now" lists jobs that are in progress at the moment. "Recent failures" lists jobs that failed lately; if there are none it says "No failed jobs". "Configured jobs" lists the jobs that are set up, or says "No configured jobs returned" when the list is empty. Use these panels for a quick view without filtering the main list.

sections.heading: If the dashboard is empty or shows a connection notice
sections.body: If you see "Backend batch-job APIs not reachable yet", the batch-job services that feed this page are not available yet. The notice says the dashboard will populate automatically once those admin services are live. Try "Reload" later. Nothing needs to be set up on this page.

sections.heading: Run a bundled retail sample
sections.body: The "Retail file run" panel lets you run a sample now without waiting for the night job. It does not open a customer connection. 1) Choose a "Shop pack": Gas sample (register and fuel), Liquor sample (register only), Dunkin sample (register only), 7-Eleven sample (register only), Restaurant sample (register only) or Clinic sample (register only). 2) Optionally fill in "Tenant id" and "Business date". 3) Turn on "Save to retail tables" if you want the results saved. 4) Select "Run bundled sample". If it fails you will see "The sample run did not finish".

sections.heading: Upload a register file and run it
sections.body: To run your own data, use the file part of "Retail file run". 1) Choose the "Shop pack". 2) Under "Register file", pick your file. 3) For the gas pack, also pick a "Fuel file"; other packs do not need one. 4) Optionally set "Tenant id", "Business date" and "Save to retail tables". 5) Select "Upload and run". If a file is missing you will see "Choose a register file" or "Choose a fuel file for a gas pack". If the run fails you will see "The uploaded file run did not finish".

sections.heading: Rules and options for file runs
sections.body: Files must be CSV (.csv). A fuel file is required only for the gas pack. "Tenant id" is the website tenant ID; if you leave it blank, the tenant you are signed in with is used. "Save to retail tables" controls whether results are saved to the retail tables. The run starts only when you select "Run bundled sample" or "Upload and run". The filters in "Job executions" apply when you select "Filter".

sections.heading: What the Billing Area is for
sections.body: The Billing Area shows who pays the platform, what the subscription covers, and the charge ledger. It is for the platform super admin only, and it is not ticket revenue. The main page is "Platform billing" (with a "Back to Admin" button); open an organization from it to see its websites and billing scope. "Charge search" is a separate page for finding charges and billing changes across every organization, with a "Back to Platform billing" button. Each organization has an "Organization billing" page, and each website (tenant) has its own billing card with a charge switch. If a billing link is out of date or the record was removed, you see "This organization is no longer available" or "This tenant is no longer available" with a button to go back.

sections.heading: Search for an organization on Platform billing
sections.body: On "Platform billing", type in the "Search billing" box, which accepts an organization, website, email, customer, subscription, or invoice, then click "Search". Each result shows the Organization, Scope, Amount, Status, Stripe customer, Last payment, Next period, and Covered websites. Click a result to open that organization's billing page. If nothing matches you see "No billing records match this search." When there are many results, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom; the page shows which page you are on and what is being shown.

sections.heading: Export the portfolio
sections.body: On "Platform billing", click "Export portfolio" to download the billing portfolio report. If the report cannot be produced you see "Billing report is unavailable". The search you typed in the "Search billing" box is next to this button on the same page.

sections.heading: Find charges with Charge search
sections.body: Open "Search charges and history" on Platform billing, or go to the "Charge search" page. 1) In "Find", type an organization name or number, an email, or a Stripe id (starting in_, sub_, pi_, or cus_). 2) Optionally narrow by "Website id" (exact), "Fee" ("All fees", "Event site", "Retail locations", or "Organization fee"), "Plan", "Status", the "From" date, and "Amount from ($)" and "Amount to ($)". 3) Pick an "Order": "Newest first", "Oldest first", "Largest amount first", or "Smallest amount first". 4) Click "Search". Click "Clear filters" to reset. The "Charges" tab lists charges; the "Change history" tab lists billing changes, and it cannot be searched by a Stripe id, so search by organization or website there. If nothing matches you see "No charges match this search." or "No billing changes match this search."

sections.heading: Open a charge's details
sections.body: In the "Charges" list, click a charge (its button is labeled "Open the charge details") to open "Charge details". The panel shows items such as Invoice, Subscription, Payment, Event, Organization id, Period start, and Failure reason when there is one. A charge marked "Paid later" was an invoice paid after it was first issued. You can use "Open in Stripe", "Open the organization billing page", or "Open the website billing page". The panel also lists "Ledger rows of this invoice" and "Latest billing changes for this fee". Click "Close" to return to the list.

sections.heading: Export matching charges
sections.body: On "Charge search", set your filters, then click "Export matching charges" (hover text: "Export every charge that matches"). It exports every charge that matches your current search, not just the ones on screen. If it does not work you see "The export failed."

sections.heading: Review an organization's billing
sections.body: The "Organization billing" page shows the organization's "Billing scope", "Monthly amount", "Status", "Stripe customer", and "Contact email". Under "Websites" it lists each website with its "Tenant id" and a "Billing" link. Use "Open charge switch" on a website to go to that website's billing card. If no websites are linked you see "No websites are linked to this organization." Use "Back to Platform Billing" to return.

sections.heading: Choose how an organization is billed
sections.body: On an organization in Tenant Management, the "Billing scope" card sets how it pays. 1) Choose "Bill the organization once" (one subscription for the organization) or "Bill each website separately" (each website stays complimentary until its own charge switch is turned on). 2) Check the "Monthly amount". 3) Click "Save billing scope". The change is only kept after you save; if it fails you see "Could not save billing scope". "Open billing area" on the card takes you to the billing pages.

sections.heading: Set up a website's platform billing
sections.body: A website's billing card is titled "Platform billing". It has "Status", "Catalog plan" (or "No catalog plan"), "Custom fee USD (blank uses the catalog)", "Review-by date (reminder only)", "Grace days", and the "Charge switch". Only a platform super admin can change platform billing. The review-by date is only a reminder and does not start a charge. If the website's plan is free or demo, the switch stays off and Stripe is not called. If an organization portfolio charge covers the website, clear that portfolio fee before charging the website on its own. Use "Turn the charge switch on" or "Turn the charge switch off" to change it.

sections.heading: What turning charging on does
sections.body: Turning the charge switch on does not charge the card by itself; the card shows "Billing saved. Turning the switch on does not charge the card by itself." Once charging is allowed, use a pay link. Paid admin tools are locked until the platform fee is paid, while the site itself stays online. Unpaid grace days lock paid admin tools and leave the site online. When the switch is off, the card says "Switch is off. Stripe is not called." A website covered by its organization shows that the organization subscription is the one that is paid and canceled.

sections.heading: Pay, manage payment methods, and cancel
sections.body: The billing card has these buttons: "Pay monthly", "Pay once", "Payment methods", "Update location count", "Cancel at period end", and "Cancel now". Pay opens Stripe Checkout with a card or a US bank account; bank debit appears when ACH Direct Debit is active on the Stripe account. "Cancel at period end" shows "The subscription will cancel at the end of the period." "Cancel now" ends it immediately, the card becomes Complimentary, and "Pay monthly" starts a new subscription. If a request fails you see "Request failed".

sections.heading: Include locations and update the count
sections.body: The billing card lists "Locations counted in the location fee". For each location use "Include this location" or "Remove this location"; excluded ones show "Not included". The count is active locations marked included, but a custom flat fee uses quantity 1. Including or removing a location only saves the choice ("Location inclusion saved"). To change the Stripe quantity, click "Update location count" afterward. If the page says to ask the platform team to include or remove a location, you cannot change it yourself on that screen. A failure shows "Could not update the location".

sections.heading: See a website's charges
sections.body: The "Charges" table on a website's billing card lists that website's platform charges. Filter with "Fee" ("All fees", "Event site", "Retail locations"), "Status" ("All statuses"), and "From". Use "Open in charge search" to see the same charges in Charge search, or open "Change history" for billing changes. Messages: "Loading charges…", "Charges could not be loaded.", "No charges match these filters.", or "No platform charges are recorded for this website yet." A row may say "This invoice was paid later."

sections.heading: What the Bulk Email page is for
sections.body: The page titled "Bulk Email Management" (subtitle: "Send bulk emails to your members and subscribers") is where you send one announcement to many people. It is at /admin/bulk-email. The page shows two cards: "Promotional Emails for Events" and "Newsletter Emails". Each card lists what you can do with it. Bulk Email is for the one-time send. Official sender addresses for your organization are added on the separate Email Addresses page (/admin/tenant-email-addresses).

sections.heading: Promotional emails for events
sections.body: The "Promotional Emails for Events" card is described as "Create and send promotional emails for specific events". It lists these abilities: create event-specific email templates, send test emails before bulk sending, send to all members or specific groups, and track email history and delivery status. Use it when you want to promote a particular event to your people.

sections.heading: Newsletter emails
sections.body: The "Newsletter Emails" card is described as "Create and send newsletter emails with news and updates". It lists the ability to create newsletter email templates. Use it for regular news and updates to your members and subscribers.

sections.heading: Creating email templates
sections.body: Both cards mention templates. The promotional card lets you create event-specific email templates. The newsletter card lets you create newsletter email templates. Look in the card that matches the kind of email you want to write, then start from a template for that type.

sections.heading: Testing and sending to your audience
sections.body: The promotional card says you can send test emails before bulk sending. It also says you can send to all members or to specific groups. A good order is: 1) prepare the email from a template, 2) send a test to check it, 3) choose all members or a specific group, 4) send it.

sections.heading: Tracking email history and delivery status
sections.body: The promotional card says you can track email history and delivery status. Use this after a send to check what was sent and whether it was delivered.

sections.heading: Where sender addresses are set up
sections.body: Bulk Email is where you send an announcement. It is not where you define your organization's inbox. Add official sender addresses on the Email Addresses page (/admin/tenant-email-addresses). That page is not a campaign tool, so use Bulk Email for the send itself.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Check-In Analytics page (Admin > Check-In Analytics) shows check-in rates and attendee history for events in this tenant, so you can compare who has arrived with who bought a ticket. When you first open it, a "Getting Started" message asks you to pick an event to view analytics and history. Once an event is chosen, you see summary figures ("Total Tickets", "Checked In", "Check-In Rate", "Total Guests"), a "Check-Ins by Hour" section, and a "Check-In History" list. You can narrow the data by date range and export it with "Export CSV".

sections.heading: Find and choose an event
sections.body: Use the event search area ("Search Events") to find the event you want. 1) Type your search and use "Search By" to pick "Title", "Caption", "Start Date" or "End Date". 2) Optionally set "Admission" to "All", "Free" or "Paid". 3) Optionally change "Sort" to "Date (Earliest)", "Date (Latest)", "Title (A-Z)", "Title (Z-A)", "ID (Newest)" or "ID (Oldest)". 4) Pick the event from the results. If nothing matches you will see "No events found matching your search criteria.", and before you search it says "Enter search criteria to find events." Results show details such as the location.

sections.heading: Read the summary figures
sections.body: After an event is selected, the top of the page shows four figures: "Total Tickets", "Checked In", "Check-In Rate" and "Total Guests". Together they show how many people have arrived compared with how many tickets were bought. While data loads you see "Loading analytics...". If something goes wrong, the message "Failed to load analytics" appears.

sections.heading: Filter by date range
sections.body: Use the date range controls to limit the data shown. You can type dates in the "From:" and "To:" boxes (format mm/dd/yyyy), or click a quick option: "Last 7 Days", "Last 30 Days", "Last 90 Days", "Last 6 Months", "Last Year" or "All Time". The "Getting Started" message notes that you can filter by date range for the chosen event.

sections.heading: See check-ins by hour
sections.body: The "Check-Ins by Hour" section shows when during the day attendees arrived. Use it to spot busy arrival times for the selected event and date range.

sections.heading: Browse and search check-in history
sections.body: The "Check-In History" list has the columns "Transaction ID", "Name", "Email", "Quantity", "Check-In Time" and "Guests Checked In". 1) Type in the box "Search by name, email, or ID..." to find a specific person or transaction. 2) Click the clear button ("Clear check-in search") to remove your search. 3) Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. While loading you see "Loading check-in history..."; if there is nothing you see "No check-ins found for this event."; and if it fails you see "Failed to load check-in history".

sections.heading: Export to CSV
sections.body: Click "Export CSV" (the button also shows the tooltip "Export to CSV") to download the check-in data as a CSV file, which you can open in a spreadsheet. The "Getting Started" message says you can export the data after choosing an event and optionally a date range.

sections.heading: Messages you may see
sections.body: "Loading analytics..." means the page is fetching data; wait a moment. "Failed to load analytics" or "Failed to load check-in history" means the data could not be retrieved, so try again or reselect the event. "Failed to load events" appears if the event search fails. "No check-ins found for this event." means no check-ins match the event and date range, so try a wider range such as "All Time".

sections.heading: What the Event Analytics page is for
sections.body: The Event Analytics page (Event Analytics Dashboard) shows attendance and ticket activity across events so you can compare how events performed. At the top, the description reads "View comprehensive event analytics, registration trends, and performance metrics." Summary figures are labeled "Total Events", "Total Registrations", "Active Events" and "Reports Generated". Below them are a "Quick Actions" area with four buttons and a set of cards: "Event Analytics Dashboard", "Registration Management", "Event Management", "Create New Event", "Event Settings" and "Reports & Exports".

sections.heading: Reading the summary figures
sections.body: Four figures sit at the top of the page. "Total Events" counts events, "Total Registrations" counts sign-ups, "Active Events" counts events that are currently active, and "Reports Generated" counts reports that have been produced. Use them for a quick view of how busy your events are before looking at the detail cards.

sections.heading: Using Quick Actions
sections.body: The "Quick Actions" area has four buttons: "Create New Event", "View Analytics", "Manage Registrations" and "Export Data". Click the one that matches what you want to do. Each one is a shortcut to the same tools described in the cards lower on the page.

sections.heading: Viewing analytics for all events
sections.body: The "Event Analytics Dashboard" card describes "View comprehensive analytics, registration trends, and guest statistics for all events." It covers "Registration trends", "Capacity utilization", "Guest analytics" and "Special requirements summary". To open it, click "View Analytics" in "Quick Actions" or use the card. Use these views to compare events with each other.

sections.heading: Managing registrations
sections.body: The "Registration Management" card is for managing all event registrations, viewing attendee details, and exporting data. It lists "View all registrations", "Search and filter", "Export to CSV" and "Manage attendee status". To get there, click "Manage Registrations" in "Quick Actions" or use the card. Use the search and filter options to find specific attendees or registrations.

sections.heading: Creating and managing events
sections.body: The "Event Management" card is for creating, editing and managing events, and viewing all events in the system. It lists "Create new events", "Edit existing events", "Cancel events" and "Event listings". The "Create New Event" card gives quick access to create a new event with "Event details", "Pricing setup", "Capacity management" and "Registration settings". To start, click "Create New Event" in "Quick Actions" or on its card.

sections.heading: Exporting data and reports
sections.body: To export, click "Export Data" in "Quick Actions". The "Reports & Exports" card is for generating detailed reports and exporting data for analysis. It lists "Custom reports", "Data exports", "Analytics reports" and "Registration summaries". Registrations can also be exported with "Export to CSV", which is listed under "Registration Management".

sections.heading: Event settings
sections.body: The "Event Settings" card is for configuring global event settings and preferences. It covers "Default settings", "Email templates", "Registration rules" and "System preferences". Use it for options that apply to all events, rather than to one event.

sections.heading: What the Event Analytics page is for
sections.body: The Event Analytics page (Event Management Dashboard) gives you an overview of all events and registrations. It shows summary figures at the top, then charts and lists such as "Registration Trends", "Guest Age Groups", "Guest Relationships", "Special Requirements", "Top Events by Attendance" and "Recent Registrations". When the page is opened for a single event, it reads "Manage registrations and analytics for this event" and "Registration and attendance overview for this event." The "View All Registrations" button and the "Previous Page" button are in the page header area. You will find it at /admin/events/dashboard.

sections.heading: Reading the summary figures
sections.body: Four headline figures are shown: "Total Attendees", "Total Guests", "Capacity Utilization" and "Active Events". Use them for a quick view of how busy your events are. If the data cannot be loaded, an error message starting with "Error fetching dashboard data" may appear.

sections.heading: Viewing registration trends
sections.body: The "Registration Trends" section shows how registrations change over time. Choose the time range you want: "Last 7 days", "Last 30 days" or "Last 90 days". Pick a shorter range to see recent activity or a longer one to see the bigger picture.

sections.heading: Understanding guest breakdowns
sections.body: Three sections describe the guests who registered. "Guest Age Groups" shows the age mix of guests. "Guest Relationships" shows how guests relate to the attendee who registered them. "Special Requirements" summarizes any special needs that were reported. Use these to plan your events.

sections.heading: Checking top events by attendance
sections.body: The "Top Events by Attendance" section lists the events with the most attendees. Use it to see which events are most popular compared with the others.

sections.heading: Browsing recent registrations
sections.body: The "Recent Registrations" table has the columns "Name", "Email", "Event", "Registration Date", "Status" and "Guests". To move through the list, use "Previous" and "Next" below the table. The page number and a "Showing" count tell you where you are. If nothing matches, you will see "No registrations found".

sections.heading: Exporting registrations to CSV
sections.body: Click "Export CSV" in the "Recent Registrations" section to download the registration data as a CSV file. You can open the file in a spreadsheet program. Use it for reports or to share the list.

sections.heading: Opening all registrations and going back
sections.body: Click "View All Registrations" to see the full list of registrations. Use the "Previous Page" button to go back to where you came from. There is also a "Next Page" button where it appears.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: "Registration Management" shows who signed up for events, including guests, for this tenant (website). Use it for the attendee list rather than sales totals. At the top, "Back to Admin" returns you to the main admin, and shortcut buttons lead to "Manage Events", "Manage Usage", "Event Analytics Dashboard" and "Communication Center". When you first open the page you see "Search for an Event"; once an event is chosen you get a list of attendees with search, a status filter, "Export CSV", and an "Event Registration Analytics" summary.

sections.heading: Find an event
sections.body: The page asks you to search for an event by Event ID, Event Name, or Date Range. 1) Under "Search By", pick "Event ID", "Event Name" or "Date Range". 2) Type in "Enter Event ID" or "Enter Event Name", or fill "Start Date" and "End Date". 3) Click "View Registrations" (the search button is also labeled "Search Events"). If the search fails, an error message about searching events appears.

sections.heading: Pick from recent events
sections.body: Instead of searching, use "Or select from recent events (max 50)". Open the "Select an event..." list and choose an event to load its registrations. To switch to another event later, use "Change Event...".

sections.heading: Search and filter attendees
sections.body: Once an event is loaded, you can narrow the attendee list. Choose "Search by Name", "Search by Email" or "Search by Event ID" and type in the box ("Enter name to search...", "Enter email to search..." or "Enter Event ID..."). Use the status dropdown to show "All Statuses", "Registered", "Pending", "Cancelled" or "Waitlisted". If nothing matches, you see "No registrations found".

sections.heading: Read the attendee list and totals
sections.body: The list has the columns "Attendee", "Contact", "Status" and "Actions". Above it, "Event Registration Analytics" shows "People Registered", "Total Guests" and "Total Attendees". Use "Previous Page" and "Next Page" (or "Previous" and "Next") at the bottom to move between pages; "Page" and "Showing" tell you where you are.

sections.heading: View attendee details
sections.body: In a row's Actions, click "View Details" to open "Attendee Details". It shows "Personal Information" (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone), "Event Information" (including Registration Date), and any Special Requirements, Dietary Restrictions and Accessibility Needs. It also shows the "Emergency Contact" with Contact Name, Contact Phone and Relationship. Click "Close" when done.

sections.heading: Edit a registration
sections.body: 1) In a row's Actions, click "Edit" to open "Edit Attendee Registration". 2) Change the fields. "First Name *", "Last Name *" and "Email *" are required. You can also change "Registration Status", special requirements, dietary restrictions, accessibility needs, the emergency contact (the relationship box suggests examples like Spouse, Parent, Friend), and "Notes" under "Additional Notes". 3) Under "Guest Management", set "Total Number of Guests" and "Guests Checked In". 4) Click "Save Changes" (it shows "Saving..." while working), or "Cancel" to discard. If saving fails you see "Failed to update attendee registration. Please try again."

sections.heading: Delete a registration
sections.body: 1) In a row's Actions, click "Delete Registration" (the trash action). 2) Read the warning: "This action cannot be undone and will permanently remove the registration data." 3) Confirm with "Delete Registration"; it shows "Deleting..." while working. If it fails, you see "Failed to delete attendee registration. Please try again." If you only want to mark someone as not coming, consider changing the status to "Cancelled" via "Edit" instead.

sections.heading: Export registrations to CSV
sections.body: With an event loaded, click "Export CSV" to download the registrations as a spreadsheet-style file. The export includes details such as Registration ID, Registration Date, Total Guests, special requirements, dietary restrictions, accessibility needs and emergency contact information. If it fails, you see "Failed to export CSV. Please try again."

sections.heading: Rules and tips
sections.body: You must pick an event before any registrations show. The recent-events list holds at most 50 events. First name, last name and email are required when editing. Changes in the edit window only apply after "Save Changes", while deleting is permanent once confirmed. Use "Back to Manage Events" or "Event Analytics" to move to related pages.

sections.heading: Overview of Event Sponsors
sections.body: Event Sponsors holds the sponsor names and logos that can be attached to events. The main page (Event Sponsors list) is headed "Global Sponsors" and shows a table of sponsors with the columns "Sponsor Name", "Type", "Company", "Priority" and "Status". Above the table are a search box ("Search sponsors..."), the filters "All Types" and "All Status", and the "Add Sponsor" button. Below the table are "Previous" and "Next" page buttons. Opening a single sponsor takes you to its own "Edit Sponsor" page, with a "Back to Sponsors" link to return to the list. The list notes that you can add or disassociate sponsors with any events, but to do that you go to the corresponding event page.

sections.heading: Search, filter and browse sponsors
sections.body: 1) Type in the "Search sponsors..." box to narrow the list. 2) Use the "All Types" filter to show one sponsor type and the "All Status" filter to show only "Active" or "Inactive" sponsors. 3) Click "Clear sponsor search" to empty the search box. Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; the page number and a "Showing" count appear below the table. If nothing matches, you see "No sponsors found".

sections.heading: Preview sponsor details from the list
sections.body: Hover over a row in the list (the hint reads "Hover to view full details") to see a "Sponsor Details" popup. It shows the sponsor's name, type, company, tagline, description, email, phone, website, priority, whether it is active, plus "Image text" and "Search text". This lets you check a sponsor without opening it.

sections.heading: Add a sponsor
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Sponsor" to open the "Add Event Sponsor" form. 2) Fill in the required fields: "Sponsor Name *", "Type *" (choose from "Select sponsor type", for example Community Partner, Media Partner or Food & Beverage) and "Priority Ranking *" (1 = highest priority). 3) Optionally add "Company Name", "Contact Email", "Contact Phone", "Website URL", "Tagline" (max 500 characters), "Description" and the "Social links" (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok URLs). 4) Tick "Active Sponsor" if the sponsor should be active. 5) Click "Create Sponsor". You see "Sponsor created successfully". If you leave out the name or type, you are told "Sponsor name is required" or "Sponsor type is required". Use "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Upload banner, logo and hero images
sections.body: The sponsor form has three image areas: "Banner poster", "Logo" and "Hero image". The banner poster is what visitors see on the sponsor page and on event sponsor cards; the logo is saved with the sponsor but visitors do not see it. In each area, click to upload or drag and drop an image (PNG, JPG, GIF up to 10MB), then use "Upload" if shown. To replace an image, upload another one ("Change banner poster", "Change hero image"), or click "Remove image" to take it away. When adding a new sponsor, the image uploads after the sponsor is created. If you see "Sponsor created, but image upload failed. Edit the sponsor to upload images.", open the sponsor and upload the images again. Non-image files or files over 10MB are rejected.

sections.heading: Edit a sponsor
sections.body: 1) Open a sponsor from the list to reach the "Edit Sponsor" page, or use the edit option on the sponsor's row, which opens "Edit Event Sponsor". 2) Change any fields under "Sponsor details" (name, type, company, priority, contact details, website, "Active Sponsor", description, tagline and social links). 3) Click "Update Sponsor". You see "Sponsor updated successfully". Use "Cancel" to leave without saving, or "Back to Sponsors" to return to the list.

sections.heading: Manage a sponsor's media gallery
sections.body: A sponsor's page includes a "Media Gallery" with the sponsor's media files. If it is empty you see "No media files found for this sponsor."; use "Upload Media" (or "Upload More Media") to add files. On each item, "Edit Priority" changes its priority ranking (it must be 0 or higher) and "Save" confirms it. The edit option ("Edit Media Details") opens fields for "Title *", "Description", "Alt Text", "Priority Ranking", "Start Displaying From Date" and "Featured Video URL". Under "Media Properties" you can tick options such as "Public", "Event Flyer", "Official Doc", "Hero Image", "Active Hero", "Featured Video", "Home Page Hero", "Featured Event" and "Live Event". Click "Save Changes" to apply.

sections.heading: Delete a sponsor or media file
sections.body: To delete a sponsor, use the delete option on its row in the list. A "Delete Sponsor" confirmation appears; click "Delete" to confirm, and you see "Sponsor deleted successfully". To remove a media file from the Media Gallery, choose "Delete media file", then confirm with "Delete" in the "Delete Media File" box ("Are you sure you want to delete this media file?"). To remove only an image on the sponsor form, use "Remove image" instead.

sections.heading: Rules and limits
sections.body: "Sponsor Name *", "Type *" and "Priority Ranking *" are required for a sponsor; the priority number cannot be below 0, and 1 is the highest priority. The tagline is limited to 500 characters. Images must be image files up to 10MB (PNG, JPG, GIF). Creating, updating and deleting a sponsor take effect when you click the matching button ("Create Sponsor", "Update Sponsor", "Delete"). Editing a priority from a media item or ranking editor takes effect when you click "Save". Linking sponsors to events is done from the corresponding event page.

sections.heading: Overview: what is in Events Analytics
sections.body: The main Event Analytics page shows summary cards ("Total Events", "Total Registrations", "Active Events", "Reports Generated"), a "Quick Actions" area ("Create New Event", "View Analytics", "Manage Registrations", "Export Data"), and cards such as "Event Analytics Dashboard", "Registration Management", "Event Management", "Event Settings" and "Reports & Exports". Each event also has its own pages, with a set of tiles for the tools of that event: "Manage Media Files", "Manage Ticket Types", "Manage Discount Codes", "Manage Tickets", "Check-In Analytics", "Sales Analytics", "Manual Payments", "Featured Performers", "Event Contacts", "Event Sponsors", "Event Emails", "Program Directors" and "Event Day Agenda". Use the search box above the tiles ("Search event tools by name, such as performers, sponsors, or agenda.") to find a tool quickly. Most of the event tool pages have a "Back to Event" button that returns you to the event. The same event pages also show the event's ID, title, dates and time at the top of the ticket, discount code and media pages so you can confirm which event you are working on.

sections.heading: Create or edit an event
sections.body: Use "Create New Event" to start a new event, or open an event's edit page to change it. Fill in the fields marked with *: "Title *", "Event Type *", "Start Date *", "End Date *", "Promotion Start Date *", "Start Time *", "End Time *", "Timezone *" and "Admission Type *" ("Free" or "Ticketed"). Optional fields include "Caption", "Description", "Location", "Directions to Venue", "Capacity" and "Max Guests Per Attendee". Dates must be typed as MM/DD/YYYY (for example 09/14/2025) or picked with the calendar icon. Switches such as "Active", "Allow Guests", "Require Guest Approval", "Enable Guest Pricing", "Registration Required", "Sports Event", "Competition Event", "Live Event" and "Featured Event" turn features on or off. Use "Reset" to undo your changes on the form, or "Cancel" to leave without saving. If saving fails you will see "Failed to update event".

sections.heading: Event form rules and limits
sections.body: Title can be up to 250 characters, "Caption" up to 450, "Description" up to 900, and "Directions to Venue" up to 580. Dates must be in MM/DD/YYYY format and must be today or later. The end date cannot be before the start date, the promotion start date cannot be after the event start date, and the end time must be after the start time. If guests are allowed, "Max Guests Per Attendee" must be greater than 0. In the Description box, leave a blank line (press Enter twice) to start a new paragraph on the event page. Each message appears next to the field when a rule is not met.

sections.heading: Payment, fundraiser and external link settings
sections.body: In the event form, the "Payment Configuration" section has "Payment Flow Mode *" with three choices: "Stripe Only" (all payments through Stripe checkout), "Manual Only (Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, etc.)" and "Hybrid (Both Stripe and Manual)". "Enable Manual Payment" only works when you choose "Manual Only" or "Hybrid". Under "Fundraiser & Charity Configuration" you can tick "Is Fundraiser Event" and "Is Charity Event"; for these events the zero-fee provider is set to Givebutter automatically. The "Givebutter Campaign ID" field is optional; if left empty, the default campaign from your provider settings is used, but setting one per event is recommended for tracking. You can also tick "Use external registration URL" or "Use external ticket purchase URL" and enter the full vendor link, which opens in a new browser tab; the ticket link needs Admission Type set to "Ticketed".

sections.heading: Recurring events and email header image
sections.body: In the event form, tick "Make this event recurring" to repeat the event. Choose a "Recurrence Pattern *", pick the weekdays ("On days of week *") or "On day of month *" when asked, and set an "End Condition *": "End on date" (maximum 5 years from the start date) or "End after occurrences" (maximum 1000). A preview shows the first 10 dates. The "Email Header Image" section lets you click or drag and drop a picture (JPEG, PNG or GIF, up to 10MB) that appears at the top of ticket confirmation emails. The "From Email" field lets you choose from verified, active email addresses; if the list is empty, an administrator must add addresses first.

sections.heading: Manage event contacts and event emails
sections.body: Open the "Event Contacts" or "Event Emails" tile to see a table with a search box ("🔍 Search contacts..." or "Search emails..."); click the clear button to reset the search. To add one, 1) click "Add Contact" or "Add Email", 2) fill in the form, 3) click "Create Contact" or "Create Email". A contact needs "Name *" and "Phone *"; "Email" is optional. An email entry needs "Email Address *". Use the edit action on a row to change it ("Update Contact" / "Update Email"), or the delete action and confirm "Delete" to remove it. Column headings such as "Name" and "Email Address" can be used for sorting. Each change shows a success message such as "Contact created successfully".

sections.heading: Manage featured performers
sections.body: Open "Featured Performers" to see the performers list with columns like "Name", "Stage Name", "Role", "Headliner", "Order", "Email" and "Active", plus a search box. To add one, 1) click "Add Performer", 2) fill in "Name *" (the only required field), 3) click "Create Performer". Other fields include "Stage Name", "Role", "Performance Order", "Performance Duration (minutes)", "Is Headliner", "Bio", contact details, "Website URL", "Nationality", "Date of Birth", "Priority Ranking", "Is Active" and social links (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, TikTok). In the "Images" area you can upload a "Portrait Image", a "Performance Image" and "Gallery Images". Use the edit action ("Update Performer") to change a performer or the delete action to remove one after confirming.

sections.heading: Manage program directors
sections.body: Open "Program Directors" to see a searchable list with "Name" and "Bio" columns. To add one, 1) click "Add Program Director", 2) enter "Name *" (required), 3) optionally add a "Bio" and a profile photo, 4) click "Create Program Director". For the photo, use "Upload Profile Photo" or enter a "Photo URL". To change a director, use the edit action and click "Update Program Director". To remove one, use the delete action and confirm "Delete".

sections.heading: Assign and manage event sponsors
sections.body: The "Event Sponsors" page lists sponsors already on this event ("Sponsor Name", "Type", "Company", "Contact Email", "Active", "Assigned Date") and, below it, "Available Sponsors to Assign". To assign one, 1) find it in the available list (use "Search available sponsors..."), 2) click "Assign", 3) confirm with "Assign Sponsor". To change an existing assignment use the edit action then "Update Assignment"; to take a sponsor off the event use "Remove Sponsor" and confirm "Remove". Click "Create New Sponsor" to add a new one that is assigned to this event right away: "Sponsor Name *", "Type *" and "Priority Ranking *" (1 = highest) are required, and the tagline can be up to 500 characters. You can also add contact details, social links and a "Logo Image", "Hero Image" and "Banner Image". Use "Edit" in the available list to change a sponsor itself ("Update Sponsor"). Assignments apply to this event only.

sections.heading: Upload media for an event
sections.body: Open "Manage Media Files" for the event, then use the upload form ("Upload Media Files for Event"). 1) Drag files onto the drop area or click "Browse Files" (images, videos, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel and SVG files are accepted). 2) Enter a "Title *" and choose a "Start Displaying From Date *". 3) Tick the options that apply, such as "Event Flyer", "Official Document", "Hero Image", "Active Hero Image", "Featured Event Image", "Live Event Image", "Home Page Hero Image" or "Public". 4) Click the upload button. A title, a start date and at least one file are all required. Tips on the page: hero images work best at 800×1200px (2:3), WebP preferred and under 300KB; featured event images at 1920×1080px (16:9) and under 500KB. Success shows "Upload successful!".

sections.heading: Find, edit and delete media
sections.body: Uploaded files appear under "Uploaded Media Files", and "Official Documents" are listed separately. Use "Show only Event Flyers" to narrow the list, and "Previous" / "Next" to move between pages. In the full list ("Media Files for Event") you can use "Search by Title", "Go to Serial #" (a number of 1 or more) and "Go to Image". Mouse over the Title or Type columns for full details, and click the × button to close the details box. To change an item, click the edit action, update "Title", "Description", "Alt Text", "Display Order", "Featured Video URL", "Start Displaying From" and the media options, then click "Save Changes". For home page hero images you can set how long the image shows ("Minutes" and "Seconds"); leaving it empty uses the default of 8 seconds. To delete, click the delete action and confirm; the message says this cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Manage ticket types
sections.body: Open "Manage Ticket Types" to see a list with "Name", "Price", "Service Fee", "Available", "Active" and "Actions". Hover over the Name, Price or Available columns for more detail. To add one, 1) click "Add New Ticket Type", 2) fill in "Name", "Code", "Description", price and "Available Quantity", and choose "Service Fee Included" if it applies, 3) click "Create Ticket Type". Name, code and description are required, the price and available quantity must be greater than zero, and a name or code already used on this event is rejected. Use "Edit" to change a ticket type ("Edit Ticket Type"). A ticket type may not be deletable right away; instead, edit it and untick "Active" to make it inactive. "Delete" asks you to confirm with "Confirm Delete".

sections.heading: Review sold tickets, resend emails and refund
sections.body: "Manage Tickets" shows totals ("Total Tickets Sold", "Total Amount", "Net Amount", "By Status"), a "Ticket Type Breakdown" with remaining quantities and a sales progress bar, and a "Tickets Sold" table ("Name", "Email", "Quantity", "Total", "Date", "Status"). To find a purchase, type in "Search by email", "Transaction ID" or "Name" and click "Search"; use "Previous" and "Next" for more pages. Hover over a Name or similar column to see full ticket details. On a row, "Resend Email" sends the ticket email again (it shows "Sending..." then "Sent!"). To refund, 1) click "Refund", 2) choose a reason from "Select refund reason:" ("Duplicate purchase", "Customer request", "Event canceled" or "Payment error"), 3) click "Process Refund". A reason is required, and refunded rows show "Refunded". A refund fails if no Stripe payment is found for the ticket.

sections.heading: Manage discount codes
sections.body: Open "Manage Discount Codes" to see a table with "Code", "Type", "Value", "Uses", "Active" and "Actions". You must be logged in to view this page. To add a code, 1) click "Add New Discount Code", 2) enter "Discount Code *" or click "Generate Code", 3) choose "Discount Type *" ("Percentage (%)" or "Fixed Amount ($)") and enter "Discount Value *", 4) optionally add a "Description" and "Maximum Uses" (empty or 0 means unlimited), 5) keep "Active (Available for use)" ticked if it should be usable, then save. Use the edit action ("Edit Discount Code") to change a code. To remove one, use delete and click "Confirm Delete"; this cannot be undone.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Executive Committee Management" page lets you manage the officers (leaders, not squad players) shown on the public site, including their name, title, order, and photo. It is at /admin/executive-committee. The main area is a list of members with the columns "Member", "Title & Department", and "Actions". Above the list you will find the search box, a "Status" filter, a "Sort" menu, and the "Add Member" button. Hover over the Member or Title & Department columns to see a tooltip with more details.

sections.heading: Search, filter and sort members
sections.body: Use the "Search team members" box to find a member. Pick what to search with the "Search by" menu: "First name", "Last name", "Title", "Email", "Department", "Designation", or "Member ID". The "Status" menu has "All", "Active only", and "Inactive only". The "Sort" menu offers "Priority (low first)", "Priority (high first)", "Last name (A–Z)", "Last name (Z–A)", "First name (A–Z)", "First name (Z–A)", "Title (A–Z)", and "Title (Z–A)". Use "Clear member search" to empty the search box. If nothing matches, you will see "No members found".

sections.heading: Add a new member
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Member". 2) In the "Add New Team Member" window, fill in the fields. "First Name *", "Last Name *", and "Title *" are marked as required. 3) Click "Create Member". You will see "Team member saved successfully!" when it works. Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving. If saving fails, you will see "Failed to save member".

sections.heading: Member form fields
sections.body: The form has "First Name *", "Last Name *", "Title *", "Designation", "Department", "Join Date", "Priority Order", "Email", and "Bio" (placeholder: "Brief biography of the team member..."). It also has "Image Background" and "Image Style" fields, and link fields "LinkedIn URL", "Twitter URL", and "Website URL". The "Active member" option marks whether the member is active, which is what the "Status" filter uses. "Priority Order" relates to the "Priority" sort options in the list.

sections.heading: Add expertise areas
sections.body: In the "Expertise" section of the form, add areas one by one. Examples: Leadership, Strategic Planning, Finance, Marketing, Team Building. 1) Type an area in the box (for example, "e.g., Leadership"). 2) Click "Add Expertise". 3) To remove one, use the "Remove expertise item" button next to it. Each expertise area is stored as a separate item.

sections.heading: View or edit a member
sections.body: In the "Actions" column of a member's row, click "View details" to open "View Team Member" with the member's information, such as contact links, expertise, status, priority order, bio, and join date. Click "Edit" in that window, or use "Edit member" on the row, to open "Edit Team Member". Change the fields and save. Use "Close" to leave the view window.

sections.heading: Upload or change a profile image
sections.body: 1) On a member's row, click "Upload profile image". 2) In the "Upload Profile Image" window, click "Click to upload" or "Select Image" and choose a picture. 3) Check the preview; use "Change" to pick another or "Remove" to clear it. 4) Click "Upload Image". The window accepts image files up to 10MB (PNG, JPG, GIF). You will see "Profile image uploaded successfully!" when it works. If a member saves but the image fails, you can upload the image later.

sections.heading: Profile image guidelines
sections.body: The page shows "Profile Image Guidelines" for best results. Dimensions: 800×1000px (4:5 aspect ratio). Format: JPG or WebP. File size: under 200KB. Keep the face centered in the upper 60%, with a clean, professional background, even lighting, and a professional, approachable expression. The 4:5 ratio keeps card heights consistent and avoids stretched images in the "Our Team" section. The upload window itself accepts larger files (up to 10MB), but the guidelines are the recommended specs.

sections.heading: Delete a member
sections.body: 1) On the member's row, click "Delete member". 2) In the "Confirm Deletion" window, read the message "Are you sure you want to delete the team member:" followed by the name. 3) Click "Confirm Delete" to remove them, or "Cancel" to keep them. This action cannot be undone. If it fails, you will see "Failed to delete member. Please try again."

sections.heading: Browsing the list and pages
sections.body: The list shows a "Showing" summary and is split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. If there are no members, you will see "No team members yet" with a prompt to add your first member. If a page has nothing, it shows "No rows on this page." Empty details show as "Not specified", "Not provided", "No designation", or "No department". If loading fails or takes too long (over 15 seconds), you will see an error message.

sections.heading: Overview of Focus Groups
sections.body: Focus Groups are discussion circles and the events attached to them, such as committees. The main page, "Manage Focus Groups", lists the focus groups for the tenant you have selected, with the columns "Name", "Slug", "Active" and "Actions". Use "New Group" to create one. Each row has icons for "Edit Focus Group", "Manage Events", "Manage Members" and "Delete Focus Group". A search box and "Previous" / "Next" page buttons sit around the list.

sections.heading: Search and browse the list
sections.body: On "Manage Focus Groups", type in the search box ("Search name, image text, or search text") to narrow the list. To clear the search, use the "Clear focus group search" button. If nothing matches, you see "No focus groups found". The "Active" column shows "YES" for active groups. When there are many groups, use "Previous" and "Next" under the list; the footer shows "Showing" the count of focus groups and the current "Page".

sections.heading: Create a new focus group
sections.body: 1) Click "New Group" on the "Manage Focus Groups" page. 2) Fill in "Name *" and "Slug *", which are required. 3) Optionally add a "Description", choose a "Cover Image", and tick "Active". 4) Click "Create Focus Group". Use "Cancel" to leave without saving. If the name or slug is already used by another focus group, you will see a message asking you to choose a different one.

sections.heading: Required fields and slug rules
sections.body: "Name *" and "Slug *" are required; leaving them blank shows "Name is required" or "Slug is required". The slug may contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, for example career-guidance. Otherwise you will see "Slug must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens". Each focus group needs its own unique name and slug.

sections.heading: Upload or replace the cover image
sections.body: The "Cover Image" area is shown on the new and edit pages, and visitors see this cover on the focus group. Click to upload or drag and drop a picture. PNG, JPG, or GIF files up to 10MB are accepted, and 800×480 is recommended. On the new page, the image uploads after the focus group is created; if that upload fails you will be told the group was created and you can upload the image on the edit page. To replace a cover, upload another image; use "Remove image" to take it away. Wrong file types show "Invalid File Type" and oversized files show "File Too Large".

sections.heading: Edit a focus group
sections.body: 1) On the list, click "Edit Focus Group" on the group's row. 2) Change "Name", "Slug", "Description", "Announcements" (public announcements shown on the focus group page), or "Meeting schedule" (for example, Every Saturday 10am at Kerala Center). 3) Tick or untick "Active" and "Show member gallery publicly" as needed. 4) Update the "Cover Image" if you want. 5) Click "Save Focus Group". The edit page also shows the group's associated events.

sections.heading: Delete a focus group
sections.body: On the list, click "Delete Focus Group" on the group's row. A confirmation, "Delete focus group?", appears. Confirm with "Delete Focus Group", or choose "Cancel" to keep it. If it fails, you see "Failed to delete focus group".

sections.heading: Link and unlink events
sections.body: Click "Manage Events" on a group's row to see "Linked Events". To add one, use "Link New Event": search by title ("Search by Title") or by ID ("Search by ID"), then click "Link" next to the event. To remove a link, click "Unlink" on the event's row; the event itself is not mentioned as deleted. The edit page also has "Associated Events" with "Upcoming Events" and "Past Events" tabs showing title, start date, end date and status. An event already linked to the group cannot be linked again.

sections.heading: Add and manage members
sections.body: Click "Manage Members" on a group's row to see the "Members" list with first name, last name, email, role, status and actions. To add someone: 1) Click "Add Member". 2) Search for a registered user by name or email and select them. 3) Choose a "Role" and "Status". 4) Click the "Add member" button. The user must already have a profile. Use "Refresh list" to reload the list, and "View user profile" to open a member's profile.

sections.heading: Roles, status, update and remove members
sections.body: Roles available are MEMBER (regular), ORGANISER (contact organiser), EXECUTIVE (contact organiser), LEAD and ADMIN. Use ORGANISER or EXECUTIVE for Contact Organisers on the public page. Status can be ACTIVE, PENDING or INACTIVE; ACTIVE means they count as current members. To change a member, adjust "Role" or "Status" in their row and click "Update member". To take someone out, click "Remove member" and confirm "Remove this member from the focus group?".

sections.heading: Overview of Gallery Albums
sections.body: Gallery Albums lets you group public photos into albums shown on the gallery page. The main page (Admin Dashboard > Gallery > Albums) is titled "Gallery Albums" and lists your albums with a search box, a visibility filter, a sort menu and page buttons. Each album row has three actions: "Manage Media", "Edit Album" and "Delete Album". The "Create New Album" button at the top starts a new album. Editing an album opens a page titled "Edit Album", and managing media opens a page titled "Media" for that album. If you see a message "Select a tenant in the admin bar", pick a website (tenant) in the admin bar first.

sections.heading: Create a new album
sections.body: 1) On the "Gallery Albums" page click "Create New Album". 2) Enter a "Title *" (required) in the box marked "Enter album title". 3) Optionally add a "Description", a "Cover Image URL" (can be set later when adding media), and a "Display Order" (lower values appear first in the gallery; default is 0). 4) Choose "Public — visible in gallery" or "Private — hidden from public gallery". 5) Optionally pick a "Category", then click "Create Album". Use "Cancel" to close the form without saving. If something goes wrong, an "Error creating album" message appears with "Technical details" you can open.

sections.heading: Search, filter and sort albums
sections.body: Use the "Search by field" menu to choose what to search: "All", "Title", "Description", "Image text", "Search text" or "Album ID". When you choose Album ID, the search box asks for a numeric album ID. Type in the "Search albums" box, and use "Clear album search" to reset it. The visibility filter has "All Visibility", "Public" and "Private". The "Sort" menu offers "Display order (asc)", "Display order (desc)", "Title (A–Z)", "Title (Z–A)", "Newest first", "Oldest first" and "Recently updated". If nothing matches you see "No albums found" with the hint "Try adjusting your search filters."

sections.heading: Reading the album list and paging
sections.body: Each album shows whether it is "Visible on the public gallery" or "Hidden from the public gallery", and its gallery category. Albums without a category show "Uncategorized". When the list is long, use "Previous Page" and "Next Page" at the bottom; the list also shows "Showing" with the current page. If you have no albums yet, you see "Get started by creating a new album." If the list can't load, you see "Error loading albums".

sections.heading: Edit an album
sections.body: 1) On the album list click "Edit Album" on the album's row (or on the media page). 2) Change the "Title *", "Description", "Display Order", "Visibility" ("Public — visible in gallery" or "Private — hidden from public gallery") or "Category". 3) Click "Save Changes". Private albums stay in the admin but are hidden on the public site. Nothing is saved until you click "Save Changes". If saving fails, an "Error updating album" message appears.

sections.heading: Set the album cover
sections.body: The cover is what visitors see on gallery cards and album listings. In the "Cover Image" section of the edit page, click "Click to upload" or drag and drop an image (PNG, JPG, GIF up to 10MB). A preview appears, and "Cover image saved to the album." confirms it. To replace it, upload another image. If you type a cover URL manually, it is saved when you click "Save Changes". You can also use "Set as Cover Image" on an image in the album's media page. Errors such as "Invalid File Type", "File Too Large" or "Upload Failed" explain what to fix.

sections.heading: Upload photos and files to an album
sections.body: On the album list click "Manage Media" on the album. In the "Upload Media" section: 1) Enter a "Title *" (required). 2) Choose a "Start Displaying From Date *" (required). 3) Optionally add "Description", "Alt Text" and "Display Order", and tick "Make media public (visible in gallery)". 4) Drag and drop files, or click "Browse Files" or "Upload Folder". 5) Confirm with "Upload files" when asked "Upload the selected files to this album?" Accepted files are images, videos, PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, Excel and SVG files. At least one file is required; otherwise you see "No files to upload".

sections.heading: Add YouTube videos
sections.body: In the media page use the "Add YouTube video" section. 1) Enter a "YouTube URL *" and a video title (and optionally a description). 2) Click "Add another URL" to add more videos, or "Remove" to drop one. 3) Tick "Make videos public (visible in this album)" if wanted. 4) Click "Add videos to album". The videos are saved as gallery items together with uploaded photos and files. You see "YouTube video added to this album." on success, or "Add a YouTube URL and a title." if something is missing.

sections.heading: Edit, remove or delete media in an album
sections.body: Each media item on the media page has these actions: "Set as Cover Image" (images only), "Edit Media" (then "Save Changes"), "Remove from Album" and "Delete Media". "Remove from Album" takes the file out of the album but it stays in the library. "Delete Media" removes the file permanently from the library and from this album, after you confirm. Use "Previous Page" and "Next Page" to move through the list. If there are no files you see "No media files yet".

sections.heading: Delete an album
sections.body: 1) Click "Delete Album" on the album's row in the list (or on the edit page). 2) Read the confirmation, then click "Confirm delete" to proceed, or "Cancel" to stop. Deleting cannot be undone. Media files in the album are not deleted, but they are removed from the album. If it fails, you see "Failed to delete album".

sections.heading: Rules and limits
sections.body: A title is required for albums and for uploaded media, and uploads also need a "Start Displaying From Date" and at least one file. Cover images must be PNG, JPG or GIF and smaller than 10MB. Lower display order numbers appear first in the gallery; the default is 0. Creating, deleting, uploading and removing media take effect when you confirm the action; album detail changes on the edit page take effect when you click "Save Changes". Only public albums are visible on the public gallery.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Use the "Gallery YouTube videos" page to manage the YouTube videos that appear in the gallery. Each URL is shown as a thumbnail in the Videos section of the MOSC redesign gallery. The page shows a list of video rows, each with "YouTube URL", "Title" and "Details" fields and a "Show this video in the gallery" option. Below the rows are the "Add Another URL" and "Save gallery videos" buttons. The page is at /admin/gallery-youtube-videos. The videos belong to the tenant (website) you are working in.

sections.heading: Add a video
sections.body: To add a YouTube video to the gallery: 1) Click "Add Another URL" to get a new row. 2) Paste the video link into "YouTube URL". 3) Fill in "Title" and "Details" if you want them. 4) Make sure "Show this video in the gallery" is ticked if you want it visible. 5) Click "Save gallery videos". The video is not stored until you save.

sections.heading: Edit a video
sections.body: To change an existing video, find its row and edit the "YouTube URL", "Title" or "Details" text. Then click "Save gallery videos" to keep your changes. While the page is opening you may see "Loading gallery videos..." until the existing rows appear.

sections.heading: Hide or show a video without deleting it
sections.body: Each row has a "Show this video in the gallery" option. Leave it unticked (inactive) to hide that video without deleting it, or tick it to show the video again. After changing it, click "Save gallery videos". Only active videos appear in the gallery Videos section.

sections.heading: Remove a video
sections.body: To delete a video, click "Remove" on its row. If you only want to hide the video for now, untick "Show this video in the gallery" instead, which keeps the row for later use. If the removal fails, you will see "Could not remove a gallery video."

sections.heading: Saving and messages
sections.body: Click "Save gallery videos" to save all your rows. When it works you will see "Gallery videos saved. Active videos appear in the MOSC gallery Videos section." If something goes wrong you may see "Could not save a gallery video." or "Could not load gallery videos." Try again, and check the URL and fields if a save keeps failing.

sections.heading: What the Gas Station area is for
sections.body: The Gas Station area of the admin dashboard is made up of five pages: the main Gas Station page, "Access", "Compare", "Integrations" and "Stations". The main page is the starting point for the group. The other four are sub-pages in the same area. This guide only covers what can be confirmed about these pages. Buttons, fields and limits on each page are not described here because they were not available when this guide was written.

sections.heading: Opening the main Gas Station page
sections.body: To start, open the Gas Station page from the admin dashboard. It is the entry page for this group and sits at the top level of the Gas Station area. From there, go to the Access, Compare, Integrations or Stations page. You can also open any of those pages directly by their address. If the page sends you to another page, you have opened the Gas Station area from its starting point.

sections.heading: Stations page
sections.body: The Stations page is where gas stations are handled. Open it from the Gas Station area. Use the buttons and lists shown on the page itself to view or work with stations. Which actions you see may depend on your role.

sections.heading: Access page
sections.body: The Access page belongs to the Gas Station area and is about access to it. Open it from the Gas Station area to see its options. If you cannot see the page or some of its actions, your role may not include them. Follow the labels shown on the page.

sections.heading: Compare page
sections.body: The Compare page is part of the Gas Station area. Open it to see the comparison options it offers. Use the controls on the page itself to choose what you want to compare. The exact options are shown on the page.

sections.heading: Integrations page
sections.body: The Integrations page is part of the Gas Station area. Open it to see the integrations available for gas stations. Use the labels and buttons on the page to review or change them. If a setting does not seem to save, check the page for a Save button or message.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Global Contacts" page (Event Contacts in the admin area) lists shared contacts with a name, phone number, and email. A note on the page says you can add or disassociate these items with any events, and that you should go to the corresponding event page to manage the associated entities. The page has a search box ("Search contacts..."), an "All Events" filter, an "Add Contact" button, and the list of contacts with page controls ("Previous" and "Next") below. Each contact row has Edit and Delete actions. When no contacts are available, the list shows "No contacts found".

sections.heading: View a contact's full details
sections.body: Hover over a contact in the list to see a details popup (the hint "Hover to view full details" appears on the row). The popup is titled "Contact Details" and shows the contact's Name, Phone, Email, and Event. Use it when the list does not show everything at a glance.

sections.heading: Search for contacts
sections.body: 1) Click the search box showing "Search contacts...". 2) Type part of the contact's details. 3) The list updates to show matching contacts. To start over, use the "Clear contact search" button next to the box. If nothing matches, you will see "No contacts found" and "[No contacts match your criteria]".

sections.heading: Filter contacts by event
sections.body: Use the event dropdown, which starts on "All Events", to narrow the list to contacts linked to a particular event. Choose "All Events" again to see every contact. If the events fail to load, an error beginning "Failed to load events:" is shown.

sections.heading: Add a contact
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Contact" at the top of the page. 2) In the "Add Event Contact" window, fill in "Name *" and "Phone *", which are required. 3) Optionally enter "Email". 4) Optionally pick an event under "Event (Optional)"; leave "No Event (Global)" selected to keep the contact global. 5) Click "Create Contact". You will see "Contact created successfully". Use "Cancel" to close the window without saving.

sections.heading: Edit a contact
sections.body: 1) Find the contact in the list and use its edit action to open the "Edit Event Contact" window. 2) Change the "Name *", "Phone *", "Email", or "Event (Optional)" fields. 3) Click "Update Contact". You will see "Contact updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Delete a contact
sections.body: 1) Use the delete action on the contact's row. 2) A "Delete Contact" confirmation appears. 3) Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to keep the contact. After deleting, you will see "Contact deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Move between pages
sections.body: When there are many contacts, the list is split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" (also labeled "Previous Page" and "Next Page") below the list to move between pages. The page shows a "Showing" count and the current "Page" number to help you see where you are.

sections.heading: Required fields and messages
sections.body: "Name *" and "Phone *" are required when adding or editing a contact; "Email" and "Event (Optional)" are optional. Changes are saved when you click "Create Contact" or "Update Contact", and deleting happens after you confirm "Delete". If the list cannot be loaded, you will see "Failed to load contacts". For managing which contacts are attached to an event, use the corresponding event page as the on-screen note says.

sections.heading: Overview of Global Directors
sections.body: Global Directors are shared program directors that can be attached to many events. The main page (titled "Global Program Directors") shows a searchable, paged list of directors with an "Add Director" button. Each director opens in its own edit page ("Edit Director") with details, an "Images" upload area and an "Overview" list of uploaded media. The page notes that you can add or disassociate these items with events, but you should go to the corresponding event page to manage those associations.

sections.heading: Search and browse directors
sections.body: Type in the "Search directors..." box to filter the list. To clear your search, use the "Clear director search" button. While data loads you will see "Loading program directors...", and if nothing matches you will see "No directors found" with "[No directors match your criteria]". Use "Previous" and "Next" (or the "Previous Page" and "Next Page" buttons) to move between pages; the list shows "Showing" counts and the current "Page".

sections.heading: View director details by hovering
sections.body: Hover over a director in the list ("Hover to view full details") to see a "Director Details" popup. It shows the director's "Name", "Bio", "Photo URL" and "Event". Use this to check a record quickly without opening it.

sections.heading: Add a director
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Director". 2) In the "Add Global Program Director" window, enter the "Name *" (required). 3) Optionally choose an event under "Event (Optional)", or leave it as "No Event (Global)". 4) Optionally enter a "Photo URL (Optional)" and a "Bio". 5) Click "Create Director". You will see "Program director created successfully". If the name is empty you will see "Name is required". Use "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Edit a director
sections.body: From the list, use the edit action on a director to open the "Edit Global Program Director" window. Change the "Name *", "Event (Optional)", "Photo URL (Optional)" or "Bio", then click "Update Director". You will see "Program director updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving. You can also open the director's full edit page, which has a "Back to Directors" link at the top, the same "Name *" and "Bio" fields, and an "Update Director" button that shows "Director updated successfully".

sections.heading: Delete a director
sections.body: Use the delete action on a director in the list to open the "Delete Program Director" confirmation. Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to keep the director. After deleting, you will see "Program director deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Upload director images
sections.body: On a director's edit page, use the "Images" section to upload several photos. You can drag and drop images or click "Click to upload" to browse. Only image files are accepted (PNG, JPG, GIF and similar), up to 10MB each. Use "Upload" to send a selected image, or "Remove" to discard a selection before uploading. After upload you will see "Image uploaded successfully", and all images appear in the "Overview" section below. The first/current picture may be labeled "Primary photo". Errors include "Please select an image file (JPEG, PNG, GIF, etc.)" and "File size must be less than 10MB".

sections.heading: Edit or delete uploaded media
sections.body: In the "Overview" list on a director's edit page, use the edit icon ("Edit media details") on a file to open "Edit Media Details". You can change "Title *", "Description", "Alt Text", "Priority Ranking" and "Start Displaying From Date", plus "Featured Video URL" and "Media Properties" checkboxes such as "Public", "Event Flyer", "Official Doc", "Hero Image", "Active Hero", "Featured Video", "Home Page Hero", "Featured Event" and "Live Event". Click "Save Changes" to apply, or "Cancel". To remove a file, use the delete icon ("Delete media file") and confirm with "Delete". "Edit Priority" lets you change a file's display order. Use "Previous" and "Next" to page through files.

sections.heading: Required fields and limits
sections.body: "Name *" is required when creating or updating a director; "Photo URL (Optional)", "Bio" and the event are optional. A director with "No Event (Global)" is not tied to a specific event. Images must be image files up to 10MB. Media "Title *" is required when editing media details. If something fails you may see messages such as "Failed to load program directors", "Failed to load events:", "Failed to update media:" or "Failed to delete media:"; try again.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Global Emails" page (/admin/event-emails) lists shared email addresses that can be reused on events. This is not the organization sender inbox and not Bulk Email. At the top you will find a search box ("Search emails...") and an "Add Email" button. Below is the list of emails with page controls ("Previous" and "Next"). The page notes that you can add or disassociate these items with any events, and that you should go to the corresponding event page to manage the associated entities.

sections.heading: View full details of an email
