sections.body: Hover over a row in the list (the hint says "Hover to view full details") to open an "Email Details" tooltip. It shows the "Email" address and the "Event" title it is linked to. Use this to quickly see which event an address belongs to without opening anything.

sections.heading: Search emails
sections.body: 1) Click the "Search emails..." box. 2) Type part of an email address. 3) The list updates to show matching emails. To start over, use the "Clear email search" button in the search box. If nothing matches, you will see "No emails found" with "[No emails match your criteria]".

sections.heading: Add a global email
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Email". 2) In the "Add Global Event Email" window, fill in "Email Address *" (placeholder "Enter email address"). 3) Click "Create Email". You will see "Email created successfully" when it is saved. If you leave the field empty, you will see "Email is required". Click "Cancel" to close the window without saving.

sections.heading: Edit an email
sections.body: 1) Find the email in the list. 2) Use its edit action on the row to open the "Edit Global Event Email" window. 3) Change "Email Address *". 4) Click "Update Email". You will see "Email updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Delete an email
sections.body: 1) Find the email in the list. 2) Use the "Delete Email" action on its row. 3) In the confirmation, click "Delete" to confirm. You will see "Email deleted successfully" when it is removed.

sections.heading: Browse through pages
sections.body: When there are many emails, the list is split into pages. Use "Next" (or "Next Page") and "Previous" (or "Previous Page") to move between pages. The footer shows "Page" and "Showing" counts so you know where you are in the list.

sections.heading: Rules and messages
sections.body: "Email Address *" is required; saving without it shows "Email is required". Creating, updating and deleting take effect when you confirm the action ("Create Email", "Update Email", "Delete"). While the list is loading you will see "Loading emails...", and if it cannot be loaded you will see "Failed to load emails". To manage how emails are associated with events, go to the corresponding event page.

sections.heading: Overview of Global Performers
sections.body: Global Performers are shared performers that can be attached to many events. The main page (Global Performers) shows a searchable, paged list with a "Search performers..." box, an "All Events" filter and an "Add Performer" button. List columns include "Name", "Stage Name", "Role", "Event", "Headliner" and "Order". Each row has actions to edit and delete. Opening a performer goes to its own "Edit Performer" page, which has the details form, an "Images" area and an "Overview" section. A note on the list page says you can add or disassociate these items with events, but should go to the corresponding event page to manage those associations.

sections.heading: Search and filter performers
sections.body: Type in the "Search performers..." box to find performers by name, stage name or role. To clear the search, use the "Clear performer search" button. Use the "All Events" dropdown to narrow the list to one event. If nothing matches, you see "No performers found" and "[No performers match your criteria]".

sections.heading: View details and move between pages
sections.body: Hover over a row to see a "Performer Details" tooltip. It shows name, stage name, role, bio, email, phone, website, headliner, active, order and event. When the list has more than one page, use "Previous" and "Next" (or the "Previous Page" and "Next Page" buttons). The footer shows the current "Page" and a "Showing" count.

sections.heading: Add a performer
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Performer". The "Add Featured Performer" form opens. 2) Optionally choose an "Event (Optional)"; leave it as "No Event (Global)" for a shared performer. 3) Fill in "Name *" (required). You can also fill in "Stage Name", "Role", "Performance Order", "Performance Duration (minutes)", "Is Headliner", "Bio", "Performance Description", "Contact Email", "Contact Phone", "Website", "Social Media Links" and "Special Requirements". 4) Enter social media links separated by commas. 5) Click "Create Performer". You see "Performer created successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Edit a performer
sections.body: On the list, use the edit action on a row to open the "Edit Featured Performer" form. Change the fields and click "Update Performer". You see "Performer updated successfully". You can also open the performer's own page, titled "Edit Performer". It has "Name *", "Stage Name", "Role", "Performance Order", "Performance Duration (minutes)", "Is Headliner", "Active", "Bio", "Performance Description", "Email", "Phone", "Website URL" and Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and YouTube URL fields. Click "Update Performer" to save; a "Changes Saved" message appears, and you click "Got it" to close it. Use "Back to Performers" to return to the list.

sections.heading: Delete a performer
sections.body: 1) On the list, use the delete action on the performer's row. 2) A "Delete Performer" confirmation opens. 3) Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to keep the performer. After deleting you see "Performer deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Upload performer images
sections.body: On the "Edit Performer" page, the "Images" section lets you upload multiple images per type. Drag and drop images or click "Click to upload" to browse. Click "Upload" to send a chosen image, or "Remove" to discard it before saving. Uploaded images appear in the "Overview" section below, and you see "Image uploaded successfully".

sections.heading: Edit or delete a performer's media files
sections.body: Media files for a performer appear in a paged list, or "No media files found for this performer." if there are none. Use "Edit media details" on a file to open "Edit Media Details". There you can change "Title *", "Description", "Alt Text", "Priority Ranking" and "Start Displaying From Date". You can also set "Media Properties" such as "Public", "Event Flyer", "Official Doc", "Hero Image", "Active Hero", "Featured Video", "Home Page Hero", "Featured Event" and "Live Event". Add a "Featured Video URL" if needed, then click "Save Changes". Use "Edit Priority" to change the display priority. Use "Delete media file" and confirm with "Delete" to remove a file.

sections.heading: Rules and limits
sections.body: "Name *" is required for a performer, and media "Title *" is required. Priority ranking must be 0 or higher. Image uploads accept image files only (PNG, JPG, GIF and similar) up to 10MB. Larger files or non-image files are rejected with a message. Changes in the add and edit forms are saved only when you click "Create Performer" or "Update Performer". Deleting asks for confirmation first.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Use Homepage Cache when you have changed heroes, events, or sections and the public homepage still looks old. The page shows a list headed "Cache records", with one row per tenant (website). Each row shows the "Tenant ID", the "Cache version", and an "Action" column with a button to refresh that tenant's cache. Above the list are search and sort controls, a "Reload from database" button, and Previous/Next page controls. The page is at /admin/homepage-cache.

sections.heading: Reading the cache records list
sections.body: Each row in "Cache records" is one tenant's settings. "Tenant ID" is the website's tenant ID. "Cache version" is the stored homepage cache version number for that tenant. When the cache is refreshed for a tenant, the version shown for it is the one to look at. The list shows "Showing" followed by the range of records you are viewing.

sections.heading: Refresh a tenant's homepage cache
sections.body: To make the public homepage pick up your latest changes, refresh that tenant's cache. 1) Find the tenant's row in "Cache records". 2) Click "Refresh cache records" in the "Action" column (hover text: "Refresh cache records for this tenant"). 3) The button shows "Refreshing…" while it works. If it does not work, the message "Failed to refresh cache" appears, so try again.

sections.heading: Search by Tenant ID or Settings ID
sections.body: Use the "Search cache records" area to narrow the list. The Tenant ID typeahead filters by organization, tenant ID, or domain. If you leave it empty, the list uses your default tenant context. The "Settings ID" box takes an exact numeric id (placeholder "Exact numeric id") if you know the specific settings record.

sections.heading: Sort the list
sections.body: Use the "Sort" dropdown to change the order of rows. The choices are "Tenant ID (A–Z)", "Tenant ID (Z–A)", and "Updated (newest)". Pick "Updated (newest)" to see the most recently changed records first.

sections.heading: Move between pages
sections.body: When there are many records, use "Previous" and "Next" below the list to move between pages. The current "Page" number and the "Showing" range tell you where you are. The arrow buttons labeled "Previous Page" and "Next Page" do the same.

sections.heading: Reload the list from the database
sections.body: Click "Reload from database" (hover text: "Reload data from database") to fetch the latest list of records. This reloads the list you see. It is separate from the "Refresh cache records" button in each row, which refreshes that tenant's cache.

sections.heading: Empty list and error messages
sections.body: If you see "No cache records found" or "No tenant settings found. Create tenant settings first or adjust Tenant ID filter.", the current filter matches nothing or no tenant settings exist yet. Clear or change the Tenant ID filter and try again. The message "Tenant setting not found" means the tenant's settings could not be located. "Failed to refresh cache" means the refresh did not complete.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Use the "Homepage YouTube live" page (/admin/homepage-youtube-live) to set the live or featured YouTube video shown in the player on the MOSC redesign homepage. The page is a single form that applies to this tenant (website), described on screen as the homepage YouTube live stream override for this tenant. When the page opens it shows "Loading the current override..." and then fills the form with what is currently saved. The form has the fields "YouTube URL", "Title", "Description", "Show this URL on the homepage", "Starts" and "Ends", and a "Save YouTube URL" button.

sections.heading: How the override and the automatic stream work
sections.body: While the override is active and has not passed its end time, your URL is shown on the homepage player. This includes the time before the start time, when the video still shows as Upcoming. After the end time passes, or when the form is empty or turned off, the homepage goes back to the automatic Devalokam Aramana stream.

sections.heading: Set a YouTube video on the homepage
sections.body: 1) Open the page and wait for the current settings to load. 2) Type or paste the link in "YouTube URL". 3) Optionally fill in "Title" and "Description". 4) Make sure "Show this URL on the homepage" is turned on. 5) Click "Save YouTube URL". After saving you will see "Homepage YouTube URL saved. It replaces the automatic stream until the end time passes."

sections.heading: Schedule when the video appears
sections.body: Use "Starts" and "Ends" to time the override; both are optional. A future start time still shows the video as Upcoming, rather than hiding it. After the "Ends" time, the automatic stream is used again. The end time must be after the start time. Click "Save YouTube URL" to store the schedule.

sections.heading: Turn the override off
sections.body: To go back to the automatic Devalokam Aramana stream before the end time, clear the "Show this URL on the homepage" option and click "Save YouTube URL". An empty form or a turned-off override also makes the homepage use the automatic stream. Otherwise the override stops by itself once the "Ends" time passes.

sections.heading: Rules and error messages
sections.body: A YouTube URL is required while the override is active; otherwise you see "A YouTube URL is required while the override is active." The link must be a youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com, or youtu.be address, or you see "Enter a youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com, or youtu.be URL." If the end is not after the start you see "End time must be after the start time." Nothing is saved until you click "Save YouTube URL".

sections.heading: If loading or saving fails
sections.body: If the current settings cannot be loaded, the page shows "Could not load the YouTube override." If saving fails, you see "Could not save the YouTube override." Check your entries against the rules and try "Save YouTube URL" again.

sections.heading: Overview of the Leagues page
sections.body: The Leagues page (Admin > Leagues) is where you manage league seasons, their clubs, match results, and standings for a sports-team site. The main screen is a list of leagues with the columns "Name", "Season", "Status", "Published", "Homepage" and "Tenant". Use the "Create New League" button to start a new one, and the row action "View details" to open an existing league. Inside a league you will find the sections "League details", "Clubs", "Results" and "Standings". Use "Back to leagues" to return to the list, or "Back to Admin" to leave the page.

sections.heading: Browse and open leagues
sections.body: The list shows "Loading leagues…" while it loads. If nothing exists yet you will see "No leagues found. Create a league to get started." Each row shows the league name, season, status, whether it is published, whether it shows on the homepage, and its tenant (the website it belongs to). To open a league, use the "View details" action on its row. Use "Back to leagues" to go back to the list.

sections.heading: Create a new league
sections.body: 1) On the Leagues list, click "Create New League". 2) Under "League details", fill in "League name" and, if you like, "Season label" (for example "Spring 2026"), "Homepage order" and "Description". 3) Choose a "Status" and a "Standings source" (see the related sections). 4) Click the save button ("Save league") to store it. Use "Back to leagues" if you want to leave without saving.

sections.heading: Edit league details, status and visibility
sections.body: Open a league and change the fields under "League details": "League name", "Season label", "Homepage order", "Description". "Status" can be "Draft", "Upcoming", "Active" or "Completed". Tick "Published" to make the league visible, and "Show on homepage" to feature it on the homepage; "Homepage order" sets its position there. Click "Save league" to keep your changes.

sections.heading: Add and remove clubs
sections.body: In the "Clubs" section, the table lists "Club name", "Role" and "Actions". When empty it says "No clubs yet. Add the first club below." 1) Type the name in the club name box (for example "Capital United"). 2) Tick "This club" if it is your own club; other clubs are shown as "Opponent". 3) Click "Add club". To remove a club, use "Delete" in its row.

sections.heading: Add and remove match results
sections.body: The "Results" section lists matches with "Home", "Score", "Away" and "Played". When empty it says "No results yet. Add a match below." 1) Under "Add result", pick the "Home club" ("Select home") and the "Away club" ("Select away"). 2) Choose the match status: "Scheduled", "Postponed" or "Cancelled" are among the options. 3) Enter "Home score" and "Away score" and the "Played at" date. 4) Click "Add result". To delete a match, use "Remove result" on its row. Add clubs first so they can be selected.

sections.heading: Standings: calculated or manual
sections.body: Set "Standings source" in "League details" to "Calculated" or "Manual". The "Standings" section shows "Pos", "Club" and "Pts" columns; until clubs and results exist it says "Standings will appear after clubs and results are added." To enter your own table, click "Copy calculated" to fill it from the calculated standings, edit the values, then click "Save manual table". Remember to click "Save league" if you change the standings source.

sections.heading: Delete a league
sections.body: Open the league and click "Delete league". A confirmation asks: "Delete this league and its related clubs, matches, and standings?" Confirming removes the league together with its clubs, matches and standings, so only do it when you are sure.

sections.heading: Events overview
sections.body: The Events pages let you manage one event at a time and see event-wide reports and settings. Open an event to reach its main page (Event Details plus a "Management Options" list), and from there go to its media, competitions, ticket types, sponsors, performers, program directors, and manual payments. Other pages for the same event cover the day agenda, contacts, emails, tickets sold, and competition catalog, days, registrations, results, and settings. Two pages are not tied to a single event: "Event Reports & Exports" and "Event Settings". Most event sub-pages have a "Back to Event" button at the top to return to the event's main page.

sections.heading: Open an event and reach its sections
sections.body: The event's main page shows "Event Details" (Start Date, Time, Location, Capacity, Admission, Status, Description). Click "Edit Event" at the top, or "Edit Event Details" under "Management Options", to change those details. The other buttons under "Management Options" are "Event Media", "Competitions", "Ticket Types", "Event Sponsors", "Performers", "Program Directors", and "Manual Payments". Use "Back to Manage Events" to return to the list of events. If you see "Event Not Found", the event could not be loaded or you may not have permission to view it.

sections.heading: Add, edit, or delete day agenda items
sections.body: Open the "Event Day Agenda" page for the event to see timed program items in a list with the columns Order, Date, Time, Program, Published, and Image. To add one: 1) click "Add Agenda Item" 2) fill in "Title *" and "Start time *" (other fields: "Description", "Date (optional)", "End time", "Sort order") 3) tick "Published on event page" if it should show publicly 4) save. Use the "Edit Agenda Item" or "Delete Agenda Item" icons on a row to change or remove an item. Overlapping times are allowed. If the list is empty you will see "No agenda items yet".

sections.heading: Add pictures to agenda items and the agenda flyer
sections.body: In the agenda item form, under "Agenda item image", click "Click to upload an image" (PNG, JPG, or WEBP up to 10MB), or use "Or pick existing event media" to choose a picture already attached to the event. Once an image is set you can use "Replace image" or "Remove image". Separately, the "Agenda Flyer" panel holds one full-day schedule image for the event; it is different from the Event Flyer and from the small pictures on agenda rows. Use "Upload Agenda Flyer", "Replace Agenda Flyer", or "Remove Agenda Flyer" (JPEG, PNG, or WEBP). Removing the flyer only detaches it from the event; the file stays in media.

sections.heading: Manage event contacts and emails
sections.body: "Event Contacts" lists Name, Phone, Email, and Actions; "Event Emails" lists Email Address and Actions. Use the search box ("Search contacts..." or "Search emails...") and the Previous/Next buttons to find rows. To add an existing one, scroll to "Available Contacts to Add" or "Available Emails to Add" (with their own search box) and click "Add" on the row. To create a new one: 1) click "Add Contact" or "Add Email" 2) fill in the form (contacts need "Name *" and "Phone *"; email is optional there; emails need "Email Address *") 3) click "Create Contact" or "Create Email". Row icons are "Edit", "Disassociate" (removes it from this event only), and "Delete" (permanently deletes it, after a confirmation).

sections.heading: Manage performers and program directors
sections.body: The "Featured Performers" and "Program Directors" pages work the same way as contacts: search the list, add from the "Available ... to Add" section with "Add", or create new with "Add Performer" or "Add Program Director". A performer form has "Name *" plus optional fields such as Stage Name, Performance Order, Performance Duration (minutes), Is Headliner, Bio, contact details, social links, and images (Portrait, Performance, Gallery). A program director form has "Name *", a bio, and a photo ("Photo URL (Optional)" or "Upload Profile Photo"). Row icons are Edit, Upload (banners for this event), View Media, Disassociate (remove from this event only), and Delete (permanent, after confirming). Hover over a name to see full details in a tooltip.

sections.heading: Assign and manage event sponsors
sections.body: The "Event Sponsors" page shows sponsors assigned to this event; assignments here apply to this event only. To assign an existing sponsor, find it under "Available Sponsors to Assign" and click "Assign", then confirm in "Assign Sponsor to Event". To make a new one, click "Create New Sponsor", fill in "Sponsor Name *", "Type *", and "Priority Ranking *" (1 = highest priority), and optionally company, contact details, tagline (max 500 characters), description, social links, and Logo, Hero, and Banner images; it is then created and assigned to the event. Row icons include Edit, Upload (banners for this event), View Media, Disassociate (remove from this event), and Delete. Delete permanently removes the sponsor from all events.

sections.heading: Manage event media
sections.body: The event media list ("Media Files for Event") shows uploaded files. Click "Upload New Media" to add one. Use "Search by Title" or "Go to Serial #" with "Go to Image" to find an item, and use the Previous/Next buttons to page through. Hover over an image to see full details; click the × button to close the tooltip. The "Edit Media" icon opens "Media Properties" with Title, Description, Alt Text, "Start Displaying From Date" (leave empty to display immediately), "Featured Video URL", and checkboxes such as Public, Event Flyer, Agenda Flyer, Official Doc, Hero Image, Active Hero, Featured Video, Home Page Hero, Featured Event Image, and Live Event Image. Click "Save Changes" to keep edits. "Delete Media" asks you to confirm and cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Work with competitions
sections.body: Competitions have several pages. "Competitions catalog" lists the contests; use "Add competition" (a new-competition page) to create one and the edit page to change one, with "Back to list" to return. "Competition settings" covers scoring, eligibility, and how results appear on the public event page; after saving settings, open the catalog to add age groups or categories. "Schedule days" sets competition days that appear on public competition pages and can be attached to individual contests. "Registrations" shows who signed up for each competition so you can confirm or review them. "Results" is where you enter and publish placements once judging is complete. Hover over the question mark on the catalog and results pages for more details.

sections.heading: View tickets sold and ticket types
sections.body: The "Tickets Sold" page shows the event's ticket transactions. At the top you see "Total Tickets Sold", "Total Amount", "Net Amount", and a "By Status" breakdown, followed by a "Ticket Type Breakdown" with total quantity, sold, remaining, min/max per order, service fee, sales progress, and sale start and end. To find a purchase, type in "Search by email", "Transaction ID", or "Search by name" and click "Search"; use Previous/Next to page. The list columns include Quantity, Total, Date, and Status. The "Ticket Types" page for the event shows prices, inventory, and availability. If it shows "Unable to Connect to Backend", try again later.

sections.heading: Create reports and exports
sections.body: Open "Event Reports & Exports" to generate data for analysis. Under "Quick Actions" use "Export All Registrations", "Generate Analytics Report", or "Export to Excel". For a tailored report, use the "Custom Report Builder": 1) pick a "Report Type" (Registration Data, Event Performance, Guest Demographics, or Analytics Summary) 2) choose a "Date Range" (Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, Last year, or Custom range) 3) choose a "Format" (CSV, Excel, or PDF) 4) set the "Event Filter" (All Events, Free Events Only, Paid Events Only, or Specific Event) 5) click "Generate Custom Report". Report cards such as Registration Summary and Email Campaign Results have "Generate" and "Download" buttons.

sections.heading: Change global event settings
sections.body: "Event Settings" applies to event management and registration across your tenant's events. In "Email Settings" enter the "Default Confirmation Email Template" and the "Reminder Email Template". In "Registration Settings" choose the "Default Registration Status" (Pending Approval, Automatically Registered, or Waitlisted), set "Maximum Guests Per Registration", "Default Event Capacity", and "Registration Deadline (days before event)", and use the checkboxes to require admin approval or enable the waitlist when events are full. In "System Settings" choose a Timezone (Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific) and turn QR code generation and analytics and reporting on or off. Click "Save Settings" to keep your changes.

sections.heading: Rules, limits, and what removes what
sections.body: Required fields are marked with *: agenda items need a title and start time; contacts need a name and phone; emails need an email address; performers, program directors, and sponsors need a name (sponsors also need a type and priority ranking). Agenda item pictures must be image files up to 10MB (PNG, JPG, or WEBP); the agenda flyer accepts JPEG, PNG, or WEBP. Adding a duplicate contact, email, performer, or program director to the same event is rejected. "Disassociate" only removes the item from this event, while "Delete" or "Delete Permanently" removes it for good (for sponsors, from all events) after you confirm. Deleting media cannot be undone.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Use the New Event page (/admin/events/new) to set up a new event for your website. It is one long form. It starts with the title and description, then dates and times, location, admission type, payment settings, fundraiser options, guest options, the email header image, and the "Make this event recurring" option. At the bottom are the "Reset" and "Cancel" buttons and the create button, labelled "Create Event". A help note near the top says to mouse over it for tips about the page. Fields marked with * are required.

sections.heading: Enter the title, caption, description and event type
sections.body: 1) Type the "Title *" (required, up to 250 characters). 2) Optionally add a "Caption" (up to 450 characters). 3) Optionally add a "Description" (up to 900 characters). To start a new paragraph on the event's display page, leave a completely blank line by pressing Enter twice. 4) Pick an "Event Type *" from the "Select event type" list. The "Active" and "Live Event" checkboxes are also on the form.

sections.heading: Set dates, times and timezone
sections.body: Enter "Start Date *", "End Date *" and "Promotion Start Date *" as MM/DD/YYYY (for example 09/14/2025), or click the calendar icon. The promotion start date is when promotion for the event begins. Then fill in "Start Time *", "End Time *" and pick a "Timezone *" from the "Select timezone" list. Dates must be today or later. The end date cannot be before the start date. The promotion start date cannot be after the event start date. The start time must be in the future, and the end time must be after the start time.

sections.heading: Add location, capacity and admission type
sections.body: Optionally fill in "Location", "Directions to Venue" (up to 580 characters) and "Capacity". Choose an "Admission Type *" from the "Select admission type" list: "Free" or "Ticketed". The "Registration Required", "Sports Event", "Competition Event" and "Featured Event" checkboxes are also available. If you turn on "Competition Event", a message says competition mode is enabled. It tells you to set up the catalog, settings and results in the admin competitions section, using the "Competitions" and "Competition settings" buttons.

sections.heading: Guest options and priority rankings
sections.body: Use the checkboxes "Allow Guests", "Require Guest Approval" and "Enable Guest Pricing" to control guests. Set "Max Guests Per Attendee" as well. When guests are allowed, that number must be greater than 0. You can also fill in "Featured Event Priority Ranking" and "Live Event Priority Ranking".

sections.heading: Make an event recurring
sections.body: Tick "Make this event recurring" to repeat the event. 1) Choose a "Recurrence Pattern *". One option is "Biweekly (Every 2 weeks)". 2) For weekly patterns, pick one or more days under "On days of week *" (Sunday to Saturday). For monthly patterns, set "On day of month *" with a day number or "Last day of month". 3) Choose an "End Condition *": "End on date" or "End after occurrences". With "End on date", set the "End Date *" (maximum 5 years from the start date). With "End after occurrences", enter a number from 1 to 1000. A preview lists the first 10 occurrences, and more may exist depending on your end condition.

sections.heading: Configure payments
sections.body: Under "Payment Configuration", choose a "Payment Flow Mode *". "Stripe Only" sends all payments through Stripe checkout. "Manual Only (Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, etc.)" uses fee-free methods such as Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, Cash or Check. "Hybrid (Both Stripe and Manual)" lets users choose. The "Enable Manual Payment" checkbox ("Manual Payment Enabled") is available when you pick "Manual Only" or "Hybrid". It is switched on automatically for fundraiser and charity events.

sections.heading: Fundraiser, charity and Givebutter
sections.body: Under "Fundraiser & Charity Configuration", tick "Is Fundraiser Event" or "Is Charity Event". Then "Zero-Fee Payment Provider" is set to Givebutter automatically. If you tick "Use Zero-Fee Provider", you must choose a provider from "Select provider". The "Givebutter Campaign ID" field is optional. If you leave it empty, the default campaign ID from your Givebutter provider configuration is used. A specific campaign ID per event is recommended for better tracking and reporting. To find it, open the campaign in your Givebutter dashboard, go to Settings, then Advanced, and copy the Campaign ID. You can also copy it from the campaign URL.

sections.heading: Use an external registration or ticket link
sections.body: To send people to an outside vendor such as Zeffy, tick "Use external registration URL" or "Use external ticket purchase URL". Then enter the full address in "External registration URL *" or "External ticket URL *". The Register or Buy Tickets button then opens that link in a new browser tab. For the ticket link, set Admission type to "Ticketed".

sections.heading: Email header image and From email
sections.body: In "Email Header Image", upload a picture for the top of ticket confirmation emails. 1) Click the upload area or drag an image onto it. 2) Wait for "Upload successful!". The image must be JPEG, PNG or GIF and no larger than 10MB. Once uploaded, click the image to change it. Under "From Email Field:", search and pick a verified, active address from the list. You can remove your choice with the clear button. If the list is empty, you will see a message to contact Admin to add from email addresses. Choosing a from email is validated, so enter a valid address if asked.

sections.heading: Create the event, or copy an existing one
sections.body: When the form is ready, click "Create Event". The page shows "Please wait while we create your event...". On success it says your event was created and sends you to manage events. If the form was pre-filled from another event, the button reads "Create Event (Copy)". All fields are pre-populated, the start date is set to today and the end date to tomorrow, so review and update them first. If creation fails, you will see a message about missing or invalid fields, invalid data format, a recurrence settings problem, or a database error. Check the fields and try again.

sections.heading: Reset or cancel the form
sections.body: Use "Reset" ("Reset Form") to clear your entries and start over. Use "Cancel" to leave without creating the event. Nothing is created until you click "Create Event".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Manage Events page (Admin > Manage Events) lets you create, edit, and manage all events for this tenant (website). At the top you will find a "Back to Admin" link and a "Create Event" button. Below them is a "Search Events" form, a switch between "Future Events" and "Past Events", and the event list with page controls ("Previous", "Next"). There is also a set of event section tiles with a search box, where you can open tools such as media, tickets, performers, sponsors, and the agenda. While data loads you will see "Loading events...".

sections.heading: Create a new event
sections.body: Click the "Create Event" button near the top of the page to start a new event. The "Create New Event" tile ("Start a new event" / "Create and publish an event") also opens event creation. If the list is empty, a "Create New Event" button is shown there as well. To start from an existing event, use the copy button in that event's row (see the copy section).

sections.heading: Search, filter, and sort events
sections.body: Use the "Search Events" form. 1) Type in the "Event ID" box to find an event by its ID, or use the "Search By" options: "Title", "Caption", "Start Date", or "End Date". 2) Pick "Admission": "All", "Free", or "Paid". 3) Choose a "Sort" order: "Date (Earliest)", "Date (Latest)", "Title (A-Z)", "Title (Z-A)", "ID (Newest)", or "ID (Oldest)". Click "Clear" (Clear search form) to reset the form. The small clear button on the event ID box ("Clear event search") clears just that search. If nothing matches, you will see "No events found" and "No events match your current search criteria."

sections.heading: Switch between future and past events
sections.body: Use the switch above the list to move between "Future Events" and "Past Events" (button labels "Show Future Events" and "Show Past Events"). If an event you expect is missing, check that you are on the right side of the switch. Messages such as "No future events created." or "There are no events listed yet." remind you to use this switch.

sections.heading: Read the event list
sections.body: Each row shows the columns "Event Info" (title and "Event ID:"), "Type", "Dates", "Active", "Edit/View", "Delete Actions", "Media", "Upload", "Calendar", "Tickets", and "Competitions". "Type" shows whether the event is a "Parent Event" or a "Child Event" in a recurrence series. Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to change pages; the footer shows "Showing" and the page number. A tip on the page says to click "View" in the Edit/View column to see full event details, and to click the × button to close the dialog.

sections.heading: View, edit, or copy an event
sections.body: In the "Edit/View" column, use the view button ("View event details") to see the "Event Details" dialog, and the edit button ("Edit event details") to change an event. The copy button ("Copy this event to create a new one", shown as "Copy event") starts a new event based on the existing one, which saves time for similar events. Close the details dialog with the × or "Close" button.

sections.heading: Activate or deactivate an event
sections.body: The "Active" column shows the status and offers "Activate" or "Deactivate". 1) Click "Deactivate event (soft delete)" or "Activate event" in the event's row. 2) Read the confirmation ("Confirm Deactivate Event" or "Confirm Activate Event") and click to confirm, or choose "Cancel". Deactivated events are hidden from public view but can be reactivated later; activated events are visible to the public and available for registration. If an event is already active or inactive, the matching button is unavailable. For a single occurrence in a recurrence series, only that occurrence changes; for a parent event, the message explains the effect on the series. Success messages appear when done.

sections.heading: Permanently delete an event
sections.body: In the "Delete Actions" column, the "Hard Delete" button ("Permanently delete event (hard delete)") removes an event for good. 1) Click "Hard Delete" in the row. 2) Read the warning in "Confirm Permanent Delete": all event data, registrations, and related information will be permanently removed and this cannot be undone. 3) Click "Permanently Delete" to continue, or "Cancel" to stop. If you only want to hide an event, use "Deactivate" instead.

sections.heading: Open an event's media, calendar, tickets, and competitions
sections.body: The row buttons open the tools for each event. "Media" ("List Media files") shows the event's media files, and "Upload" ("Upload Media Files") adds more. "Calendar" ("View Calendar") shows the event calendar. "Tickets" ("Manage Ticket Types") lets you manage ticket types, and "Competitions" ("Manage Competitions") manages competitions.

sections.heading: Use the event section tiles
sections.body: The tiles give quick links to related tools. Examples include "Event Analytics Dashboard", "Manage Usage", "Communication Center", "Manage Media Files", "Manage Ticket Types", "Manage Discount Codes", "Manage Tickets", "Check-In Analytics", "Sales Analytics", "Manual Payments" (Zelle, Venmo, and other offline payments), "Featured Performers", "Event Contacts", "Event Sponsors", "Event Emails", "Program Directors", and "Event Day Agenda". To find one, type in the search box ("Search event tools by name, such as performers, sponsors, or agenda."). Click a tile to open that tool.

sections.heading: Messages and troubleshooting
sections.body: If the list does not appear, you may see "Failed to load data" or "Failed to fetch child events:"; try reloading the page. If activation fails you will see "Failed to activate event. Please try again.", and a failed cancel or delete shows "Failed to cancel event" or "Delete Failed". Wait while progress messages such as "Please wait while we activate this event..." finish before doing anything else. Success messages include "The event has been activated successfully." and "The event has been marked as inactive successfully."

sections.heading: What this page is for and where things are
sections.body: Manage Users (/admin/manage-usage) lists the people (member profiles) for the selected organization. Here you can change a person's role, approval status, and contact details. This is the member list, not a sports squad. At the top you will find the "Search" box with a "Search by field" picker, status and role filters ("All Statuses" and "All Roles"), the "Bulk Upload User List" button, and the "Download Bulk Upload Template File" button. The list has the columns "Name", "Contact", "Joined", and "Actions", with "Previous" and "Next" page buttons below it. A small help icon opens "Organization admin registration and promotion", a short guide on promoting someone to admin.

sections.heading: Search and filter the user list
sections.body: 1) Pick a field in "Search by field": "First Name", "Last Name", "Email", or "Phone". 2) Type in the search box and search. 3) To narrow the list further, use the status filter ("All Statuses", "Active", "Inactive", "Pending Approval", "Suspended", "Banned", "Rejected", "Approved") and the role filter ("All Roles" or a specific role). Use "Clear user search" to reset the search. If nothing matches you will see "No users found"; if the organization has no profiles yet you will see "No users for this tenant". Use "Previous Page" and "Next Page" to move through pages; the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed.

sections.heading: Edit a user's details
sections.body: 1) Find the person and click the "Edit User" (pencil) action in their row under "Actions". 2) In the "Edit User" window, change contact details such as "First Name", "Last Name", "Email", "Phone", "Address Line 1", "Address Line 2", "City", "State", "Zip Code", and "Country". 3) There is also an "India related details" part with "Family Name", "City/Town", "District", and "Educational Institution", plus "Profile Image URL" and "Notes". 4) Click "Save Changes". Use "Cancel" or the close button to leave without saving. For a normal Google or email signup, leave the email and names as they are.

sections.heading: Change a role or status
sections.body: 1) Open "Edit User" on the person's row. 2) Under "Role" choose from "Select Role" (options include Admin, Organizer, Volunteer, Member, and, where shown, Gas Station Admin and Gas Station Manager). 3) Under "Status" choose from "Select Status": ACTIVE, INACTIVE, PENDING APPROVAL, SUSPENDED, BANNED, REJECTED, or APPROVED. 4) Click "Save Changes". Member is the default role. Only a Super Admin can promote someone to SUPER_ADMIN or change an existing SUPER_ADMIN user. For gas station organizations, use Gas Station Admin or Gas Station Manager, with locations assigned under Gas Station → Location access. After a role change, ask the person to sign out and sign back in so their Admin menu refreshes.

sections.heading: Promote someone to organization admin
sections.body: The person must first register or sign in on that organization's own website (satellite site), so a profile exists with the right tenant ID. Signing up only on the hub creates a hub profile, not an organization-admin profile, and promoting it will not make them admin of the organization. Then: 1) Open Manage Users and select the organization. 2) Search by email and, if you see the "Tenant ID" filter, set it to the website they should administer. 3) Click "Edit User", set "Role" to ADMIN and "Status" to ACTIVE or APPROVED. 4) Click "Save Changes". 5) Ask them to sign out and sign back in, then open adwiiseagent.ai/admin and pick their organization. If they registered on the wrong site, they need to sign in once on the correct organization site.

sections.heading: Approve or reject a user
sections.body: People awaiting approval show a status of Pending Approval. In their row under "Actions", click "Approve User" to approve them, or "Reject User" to reject them. You can filter by "Pending Approval" in the status filter to see who is waiting. If something goes wrong you will see a message starting with "Approve failed" or "Reject failed". If you see "Admin profile not loaded. Please refresh and try again.", refresh the page and repeat. You can also set the status yourself from "Edit User".

sections.heading: Bulk upload a user list
sections.body: 1) Click "Download Bulk Upload Template File" to get the spreadsheet template. 2) Fill it in. 3) Click "Bulk Upload User List" and choose your file; only .xlsx files are accepted. 4) Wait for "Bulk upload successful!" If it fails you will see "Bulk upload failed:" followed by the reason. Only a Super Admin can create or assign SUPER_ADMIN through bulk upload.

sections.heading: Rules and common messages
sections.body: Only a Super Admin can promote a user to SUPER_ADMIN or change a SUPER_ADMIN user; other admins will see a message saying so. Edits are saved only when you click "Save Changes"; "Cancel" discards them. If you see "Unable to verify current user role before update. Please try again.", try the action again. "Failed to update user profile" or "Failed to update user" means the save did not go through. "Failed to fetch users:" means the list could not load; refresh the page. "Selected user record missing id." means that row cannot be edited.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Manual Payments lists payment requests that skipped the card form, such as Zelle or Venmo. The page says "Manual / offline payment requests for events in this tenant." The main list is titled "Manual Payment Requests" and has a search box, status and method filters, and a date range selector. Pick an event first: the "Getting Started" message asks you to enter an Event ID above to view requests and summaries. Each row has a "Previous Page" and "Next Page" pager below the list. Opening a payment (the "View" button) takes you to its detail page, which you reach from the list by the "View Details" action.

sections.heading: Choose an event and date range
sections.body: Payments are shown for one event at a time. Use the event search ("Search Events") to find an event: pick what to search by ("Title", "Caption", "Start Date", "End Date"), set "Admission" to "All", "Free" or "Paid", and choose a "Sort" order such as "Date (Earliest)" or "Title (A-Z)". Then select the event from the results. Use the date range selector to narrow results by typing dates in the "From:" and "To:" boxes (mm/dd/yyyy) or by clicking a shortcut such as "Last 7 Days", "Last 30 Days", "Last 90 Days", "Last 6 Months", "Last Year" or "All Time". The start date must be before or equal to the end date.

sections.heading: Search and filter payments
sections.body: In the "Manual Payment Requests" list, type in the box "Search by ID, handle, or instructions..." to find a payment. Click the clear button ("Clear payment search") to empty the search. Use the status dropdown ("All Statuses", "Requested", "Received", "Voided", "Cancelled") and the method dropdown ("All Methods", "Zelle", "Venmo", "Cash App", "Cash", "Check", "Other") to narrow the list. The list columns are "Method", "Amount", "Handle", "Status", "Created" and "Actions". If nothing matches you will see "No payments found". Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; the list shows which items are being shown and the "Page" number.

sections.heading: Act on a payment from the list
sections.body: Each row has action buttons in the "Actions" column. 1) Click "View" ("View Details") to open the payment's detail page. 2) Click "Mark Received" ("Mark as Received") to confirm the money arrived. 3) Click "Cancel Payment" to cancel it; you are asked "Enter cancellation reason (optional):". 4) Click "Proof" ("View Proof of Payment") to see the proof, if the payment has one. Which buttons appear can depend on the payment's status and your access.

sections.heading: View a payment's details
sections.body: The detail page opens from the list and has a "Back to Manual Payments" link at the top. It reads "Review or update this manual payment request." It shows "Current Status", "Received At" and "Void/Cancel Reason" and sections for "Payment Details" ("Amount Due", "Payment Method", "Payment Handle", "Payment Instructions"), "Requester Information" ("Email", "Name", "Phone") and "Additional Information" ("Ticket Transaction ID", "Proof of Payment" with a "View Proof" link, "Created At", "Last Updated"). If the payment cannot be found you will see "Payment not found".

sections.heading: Edit a payment
sections.body: 1) On the detail page, click "Edit Payment". 2) Change the fields you need: the amount, the payment method ("Select Payment Method" offers Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash, Check, Wire Transfer, ACH and Other), the handle (for example @username, phone number, email), instructions or notes, and the requester's email, name and phone. 3) Save your changes. Click "Cancel" to stop editing. The amount must be greater than zero, the payment method is required, and the email must be valid, otherwise an error is shown.

sections.heading: Change a payment's status
sections.body: On the detail page, use "Change Status" to update the payment. The buttons are "Mark as Received", "Reset to Requested", "Void Payment" and "Cancel Payment". Each one asks you to confirm, for example "Are you sure you want to mark this payment as RECEIVED?". Confirm to apply the change right away. If it fails you will see "Failed to update status".

sections.heading: Run the summary batch job
sections.body: The "Manual Payment Summary Batch Job" panel builds summary data for analytics and reporting. If the summary is empty you see "No Summary Records Found"; otherwise "Summary Records Available" with a "Summary Breakdown" by "Payment Method", "Status", "Total Amount", "Transaction Count" and "Snapshot Date", plus totals for "Received", "Pending" and "Voided/Cancelled". To run it: 1) Click "Trigger Manual Payment Summary Batch Job". 2) Optionally enter a Tenant ID; leave it empty to process all tenants. 3) Optionally tick "Force update (reprocess transactions that already have summary data)". 4) Click "Trigger Batch Job". If no date range is set, all dates are processed. The job runs in the background and shows "Batch job started successfully!" with the "Job ID:", "Status:", "Estimated Records:" and "Estimated Completion:".

sections.heading: Rules and common messages
sections.body: The start date must be before or equal to the end date. A payment needs a payment method and an amount greater than zero, and a valid email address if you enter one. Status changes and the batch job start only after you confirm. Common messages: "Failed to load manual payments" or "Failed to load payment" mean the data did not load, so try again. "You do not have permission to trigger this batch job." means your account cannot run it. For "Authentication error. Please refresh the page and try again.", refresh the page. For server errors, wait a few moments and retry, then contact support if the problem continues.

sections.heading: Media Management overview
sections.body: Media Management (/admin/media) lists the images and files used by events and pages. The page is titled "Manage Media Files" and has a search area ("Search Media"), the media list, and paging buttons ("Previous" and "Next") at the bottom. Each row has actions to go to the image, edit it, or delete it, and there is an "Upload New Media" button. Clicking Edit on a row opens a quick edit window; a separate full edit page is at /admin/media/[id]/edit and is titled "Edit Media File". Public photo albums shown on the gallery page are managed under Gallery Albums (/admin/gallery/albums), not here. Navigation links such as "Admin Home", "Manage Events" and "Manage Users [Usage]" appear at the top.

sections.heading: Upload new media
sections.body: To add a file, click "Upload New Media" on the Media Management page. Use clear file names and prefer common image formats such as PNG, JPG or WEBP. Event-specific media can also be managed from the event's own media screens after you open the event. For public photo albums on the gallery page, use Gallery Albums instead.

sections.heading: Search and filter the media list
sections.body: To find media by name, type in the "Search by Title" box (placeholder "Enter media title to search..."). Use the clear button ("Clear media search") to empty the search. To jump to a specific item, use "Go to Serial #" and enter a number; it must be 1 or greater, otherwise you will see "Please enter a valid serial number (1 or greater)". Tick "Event Flyers Only" to show only event flyers. If nothing matches, the list shows "No media found." Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; the list shows which page you are on and how many items are shown.

sections.heading: Preview an image
sections.body: Mouse over an image in the list to see its full details in a tooltip. Click the × button ("Close tooltip") to close it. If you see the message that tooltips are temporarily disabled, wait a moment before hovering over images again. The "Go to Image" row action takes you to the image itself.

sections.heading: Edit media from the list
sections.body: 1) Click the "Edit Media" action on a row. 2) Change the text fields: "Title", "Description" and "Alt Text". 3) Optionally set "Start Displaying From Date"; leave it empty to display immediately, or set a future date to schedule when it starts being displayed. 4) Optionally fill in "Featured Video URL". 5) If the image is used in the homepage hero slider, set "Home Page Hero Display Duration" in "Minutes" and "Seconds"; leave empty to use the default of 8 seconds. 6) Under "Media Properties", tick the options that apply, then click "Save Changes". Click "Cancel" to close without saving. If saving fails you will see "Failed to update media".

sections.heading: Media properties (checkboxes)
sections.body: Media Properties are checkboxes that control how a file is used. The list edit window offers: "Public", "Event Flyer", "Official Doc", "Hero Image", "Active Hero", "Featured Video", "Home Page Hero", "Featured Event Image" and "Live Event Image". The full edit page offers "Event Flyer", "Event Management Official Document", "Hero Image", "Active Hero Image", "Featured Event Image", "Live Event Image" and "Public". Tick the ones that apply and click "Save Changes" for them to take effect.

sections.heading: Use the full Edit Media File page
sections.body: The page at /admin/media/[id]/edit shows read-only details for one file: "Media File ID", "Event ID", "Media Type", "Storage Type", "File Size", "Created At" and "Updated At". Below, under "Edit Media File", you can change "Title", "Description", "Alt Text", "Display Order" and "Start Displaying From Date", and tick the property checkboxes. Click "Save Changes" to save. While opening you may see "Loading media file..."; if the file does not exist you will see "Media file not found." Errors appear as "Failed to load media file" or "Failed to update media file".

sections.heading: Delete media
sections.body: 1) Click the "Delete Media" action on the row. 2) A "Confirm Deletion" window asks "Are you sure you want to delete this media item:" followed by the item name, and warns "This action cannot be undone." 3) Click "Confirm Delete" to remove it, or "Cancel" to keep it. If deletion fails you will see "Failed to delete media".

sections.heading: Rules and messages
sections.body: Changes in the edit window or edit page are saved only when you click "Save Changes"; "Cancel" discards them. Deleting is permanent once confirmed. Leaving "Start Displaying From Date" empty shows the media immediately, and an empty hero display duration uses the 8-second default. "Go to Serial #" requires a number of 1 or greater. While the list is loading you see "Loading media..."; if it cannot load you see "Failed to load media files" or "Failed to fetch media files".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Membership Plans (Admin > Membership > Plans) is where you create, edit and manage the plans people can buy for this tenant (website): prices, benefits and public visibility. The page header says "Create, edit, and manage all membership plans in the system." The main button is "Create Plan", and "Back to Admin" takes you back to the admin home. Existing plans appear in a list with the columns "Plan Name", "Plan Code", "Type", "Billing", "Price", "Status" and "Actions". This screen does not list who has subscribed; people who buy or are assigned plans appear on Membership Subscriptions (/admin/membership/subscriptions).

sections.heading: Create a plan
sections.body: 1) Click "Create Plan" at the top of the page. If no plans exist yet, the list shows "No membership plans found." and a "Create Your First Plan" button instead. 2) Fill in the form (see the field guide section). 3) Save the plan. If something is missing or invalid, a "Validation Error" message tells you what to fix. Use "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Plan form fields
sections.body: "Plan Name" is the display name and must be unique (for example Basic Plan, Premium Plan). "Plan Code" is a unique identifier used in integrations, such as basic_monthly. "Description" is free text. "Plan Type" offers "Subscription", "One Time" and "Freemium". "Billing Interval" offers "Monthly", "Quarterly" and "Yearly". Also set "Price", "Currency" and "Trial Days". "Max Events Per Month" and "Max Attendees Per Event" are limits; leave them empty for unlimited. "Features JSON" holds the plan's benefits as structured text, for example {"feature1": true, "feature2": "value"}. The "Active" option controls whether the plan is active.

sections.heading: Required fields and rules
sections.body: "Plan Name" is required and must be unique. "Plan Code" is required, must be unique, at least 4 characters, and may contain only letters, numbers, underscores and hyphens. "Price" is required. Subscription plans must have a price greater than zero, with a minimum price of $0.60. "Features JSON" must be valid; if there is a syntax error you will see "Invalid JSON format. Please check your syntax." and you must fix it before saving.

sections.heading: Stripe Product ID and Price ID
sections.body: "Stripe Product ID" and "Stripe Price ID" are shown on the form but cannot be edited. They are created automatically by Stripe when the plan is created. Until then the form shows "(Auto-generated)" or "Not yet created by Stripe API", and the plan details show "(Not yet created)".

sections.heading: View plan details
sections.body: Hover over a plan name in the first column of the list to open a tooltip dialog with detailed information. It shows description, plan type, billing interval, price, currency, trial days, status, max events and attendees ("Unlimited" when empty), Stripe IDs, and "Created At" and "Updated At" dates. Close it with "Close tooltip".

sections.heading: Edit a plan or change its status
sections.body: In the "Actions" column, click the "Edit" icon on a plan's row to open the form with its current values, change what you need, and save. The "Status" column shows whether each plan is active or inactive. If a status change fails you will see "Failed to update plan status", and a failed save shows "Failed to save plan".

sections.heading: Delete a plan
sections.body: In the "Actions" column, click the "Delete" icon on the plan's row to remove it. If it cannot be removed you will see "Failed to delete plan". Check the plan name carefully before deleting.

sections.heading: Browse many plans
sections.body: When there are more plans than fit on one page, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom of the list to move between pages. The footer shows the current "Page" and a "Showing" count. If nothing matches, you will see "No plans found".

sections.heading: Create Test Plans button
sections.body: If you see the "Create Test Plans" button, it creates two testing plans: Plan 2 ($0.70) and Plan 3 ($0.80). While it works it shows "Creating test plans...". Use it only for testing, not for real offers.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Membership Subscriptions page (under Membership in the admin area) shows membership subscriptions for this tenant: who is active, pending, or canceled. The main part of the page is the "User Subscriptions" list, with the note "View and manage all user subscriptions in the system." Above the list is a "Filter by Status:" drop-down. Each row has "View Details" and "Cancel Subscription" buttons in the "Actions" column. Use "Back to Admin" to return to the main admin area. Plans themselves are created on the Membership Plans page, not here.

sections.heading: Reading the subscriptions list
sections.body: The list has these columns: "User", "Email", "Plan", "Status", "Period Start", "Period End", and "Actions". Use it to check a person's plan and where they are in their current billing period. If nothing matches, the page shows "No subscriptions found." If the list cannot be loaded, you will see "Failed to load subscriptions".

sections.heading: Filtering by status
sections.body: Use the "Filter by Status:" drop-down above the list to show only certain subscriptions. 1) Open the drop-down. 2) Choose one of: "All Statuses", "Active", "Trial", "Cancelled", "Past Due", "Expired", or "Suspended". 3) The list shows only subscriptions with that status. Choose "All Statuses" to see everyone again.

sections.heading: Moving between pages
sections.body: When there are many subscriptions, the list is split into pages. Use the "Previous" and "Next" buttons below the list to move between pages.

sections.heading: Viewing subscription details
sections.body: 1) Find the person in the list. 2) Click the "View Details" button in the "Actions" column. 3) A "Subscription Details" window opens. It shows the "Cancel at Period End" setting, the "Current Period", and the "Trial Period" with "Trial Start" and "Trial End". It also shows "Cancellation Details" ("Cancelled At" and "Cancellation Reason"), "Stripe Information" ("Subscription ID" and "Customer ID"), and "Timestamps" ("Created At" and "Updated At"). Click "Close" (or the close icon) when you are done. If the details cannot be loaded, you will see "Failed to load subscription details".

sections.heading: Cancelling a subscription
sections.body: 1) Find the subscription in the list. 2) Click "Cancel Subscription" in the "Actions" column. 3) A "Confirm Cancellation" window asks: "Are you sure you want to cancel this subscription? This action will change the status to CANCELLED." 4) Confirm to continue; the button shows "Processing..." while it works. 5) When it succeeds you will see "Subscription Cancelled" with the message "The subscription has been successfully cancelled." Choose "Cancel" in the confirmation window if you change your mind. If it does not work, the page shows "Failed to cancel subscription". The cancellation is recorded with the reason "Cancelled by admin".

sections.heading: Rules and messages to know
sections.body: Cancelling changes the subscription status to CANCELLED, so check the person and plan before you confirm. Filtering and paging only change what you see and do not change any subscription. If you see "Failed to load subscriptions" or "Failed to fetch subscriptions:", the list could not be retrieved; try reloading the page. The message "API base URL not configured" can also appear when the system is not set up to load this data.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "News advertisements" page lets you turn the advertisements on a tenant's news page on or off. The page shows the text "News page advertisement slots and master switch for this tenant." It has two parts: the "Master switch" and the "Ad slots" table. A "Back to admin home" link takes you back to the main admin page. You must pick a tenant first, because the page says "Select a tenant to change news advertisements." if none is selected.

sections.heading: Choose a tenant and load the switches
sections.body: The settings belong to one tenant (website) at a time. 1) Select a tenant. 2) Wait while "Loading news advertisement switches..." is shown. 3) The master switch and the ad slots table then appear for that tenant. If nothing is selected, you only see "Select a tenant to change news advertisements."

sections.heading: Use the master switch
sections.body: The "Master switch" turns all news advertisements on or off for the tenant. When it is on, the page says "Advertisements are allowed on the news page. Use the table to hide a single slot." When it is off, it says "Every news advertisement is off. Slot switches stay hidden until this is turned on." Turning it off hides every slot, whatever each slot is set to.

sections.heading: Show or hide a single ad slot
sections.body: The "Ad slots" section lists "One row for each advertisement already on the news page." The table has the columns "Position", "Status" and "Visibility". A position can read "Between sections". Use the control in the "Visibility" column to show or hide that one advertisement. Slot switches only appear once the master switch is on.

sections.heading: Saving and when changes appear
sections.body: After you change a switch, a message tells you the result. "Saved. The news page will show this the next time it loads." means the change worked. Visitors see it the next time the news page loads, not instantly on pages already open. If saving fails you see "Could not save news advertisement switches."

sections.heading: Error messages and what they mean
sections.body: "Could not load news advertisement settings for this tenant." and "This tenant has no settings row for news advertisements." mean the tenant's settings could not be found or read. "Could not load the advertisements from the news page." means the list of slots could not be fetched. "The switch was saved, but the news page did not accept the change. Restart Strapi if this is the first time the visibility field is used." means your setting was stored, but the news page did not update. "Strapi is not configured, so the news page cannot be updated." means the connection to the news page is not set up. If these messages keep appearing, contact whoever manages your system setup.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: "Newsletter Email Management" (the Newsletter Emails page) is where you create, edit and send email templates for promotions and newsletters. The main list, called "Email Templates", shows each template's name, event, subject and created date, with a row of action icons for editing, duplicating, sending and deleting. At the top of the page you will find the "Email History" and "Create New Template" buttons. Opening a template to edit takes you to its own page, where "Back to templates" returns you to the list. Hover over a template name in the list to see a popup with its details.

sections.heading: Search and filter the template list
sections.body: Above the list you can narrow templates down. 1) Use "Filter by Event" to pick one event, or leave it on "All Events". 2) Use "Status" to choose "All", "Active" or "Inactive". 3) Type in the "Search" box ("Search by name or subject...") to find a template by its promotion name or title. Use the clear button ("Clear template search") to empty the search box. If nothing matches you will see "No templates match your filters". Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages; the footer shows the page number and a "Showing" count.

sections.heading: See template details
sections.body: Hover over a template name in the list to open a "Template Details" popup. It shows the template name, subject, event ID, status, promotion code, whether a header and footer image are set, created and updated dates, and a "Body HTML Preview". Use the close button ("Close tooltip") to dismiss it.

sections.heading: Create a new template
sections.body: 1) Click "Create New Template" at the top of the page. 2) Fill in "Template Name" (for example, Summer Sale 2024) and "Email Subject". 3) Choose the from email address (required; see the from email rules section). 4) Optionally pick a "Discount Code (Optional)", or leave it on "None". If the event has no discount codes you will see a message saying so. 5) Enter "Email Body HTML" and, if needed, "Email Footer HTML". Click "Click to see example HTML" to view a sample and use "Copy to editor" to copy it into the body. 6) Tick or untick "Template is active", then click "Create Template" (or "Cancel" to leave). After saving you are redirected. Header and footer images can only be added after the template is created, by editing it.

sections.heading: From email address rules
sections.body: The from email is chosen from a searchable list ("Search email addresses...") of active addresses from your tenant configuration; one may be marked "Default", and you can clear your choice with "Clear selection". The address must be registered and verified with AWS SES (Amazon Simple Email Service). If your domain is verified in SES, any valid address on that domain can be used. You cannot send an email where the "From" and "To" addresses are the same, and Hotmail accounts do not work as the From address. If the list is empty you will see a message to contact your admin to add from email addresses. If you leave it blank you will see "Please enter from email address". The email logo and footer can be set under Tenant Settings → Customization.

sections.heading: Edit an existing template
sections.body: 1) In the template list, click the "Edit" icon on the row (right-click it to open in a new tab). 2) On "Edit Newsletter Email Template", change the name, subject, from email, discount code, body HTML, footer HTML or the "Template is active" setting. 3) Click "Update Template". You will see a saving message, then a success message and a redirect to the list. "Cancel" leaves without saving. If the template cannot be found you will see "This template is no longer available" or "This template could not be loaded"; refresh the page or go back and open it again.

sections.heading: Upload header and footer images
sections.body: On the edit page, use the "Header Image" and "Footer Image" sections. 1) Click the area to upload, or drag and drop an image onto it ("Drop image here"). 2) A preview appears. Images must be PNG, JPG or GIF up to 5MB. Uploads and removals are saved straight away (you will see "Header image uploaded and saved successfully!" or the footer equivalent), without needing "Update Template". Use the remove option on the preview to delete an image. Under the footer image, tick "Add site footer" to insert your homepage-style footer (tenant name, contact, links) at about 600 px email width when the template is saved or sent; you can use it together with a footer banner image.

sections.heading: Send a test email
sections.body: Always test before sending to subscribers. 1) In the template row, click the "Send Test" icon. 2) In the "Send Test Email" window, check the "Template Name" and type an address in "Recipient Email Address" ("Enter email address"). 3) Click "Confirm & Send". An invalid address shows "Please enter a valid email address". When it works you will see "Send Successfully!". Sometimes the first email may take a minute or two to arrive. Remember the From and To addresses cannot be the same.

sections.heading: Send to event attendees or all subscribed members
sections.body: Two send icons are in each template row. "Send Bulk" sends the email to the event attendees registered for the event (or pertinent to that event only); a "Send Bulk Email" confirmation window asks you to confirm using the template. "Send to All Members" (also titled "Send to Subscribed Members") is a global email to members who subscribed to receive emails; its window is titled "Send to All Subscribed Members". In either window click "Confirm & Send" to proceed or "Cancel" to stop. These sends cannot be undone, so send a test first.

sections.heading: Duplicate or delete a template
sections.body: To copy a template, click the "Duplicate" icon on its row; you will see "Template duplicated successfully!". To remove one, click the "Delete" icon, then confirm in the "Delete Template" window. Deleting is permanent and cannot be undone. Click "Cancel" to keep the template.

sections.heading: Check email history
sections.body: Click "Email History" at the top of the page to see emails that were sent. You can filter by "Event" (or "All Events"), by "Status" ("All Statuses", "Sent", "Failed", "Bounced"), and by "Start Date" and "End Date". The table lists "Recipient", "Subject" and "Sent At", and marks test emails as "Test Email". Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. If nothing matches you will see "No emails found".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Official document categories" page lets you manage the category slugs (folder names) that official documents are filed under. These slugs are used for bulk upload and year bundles on the official documents pages. The page shows a table of categories with the columns "Tenant ID", "Sort", "Active", "Slug", "Display name", "Description" and "Actions". Above the table you have a Tenant ID search filter and an "Add category" button. Below the table are "Previous" and "Next" page buttons and a "Showing" count. There is also a link or heading labelled "Official documents (upload)" that relates to the upload side.

sections.heading: Filter categories by Tenant ID
sections.body: A tenant is one website, identified by its Tenant ID. Categories are listed per tenant. 1) Enter or choose a Tenant ID in the search filter (the placeholder looks like "tenant_…"). 2) The list then shows the categories for that tenant. Until you select one, the list shows "(all tenants — select Tenant ID to filter)". While the list is fetching you will see "Loading…". If nothing matches, the table shows "No categories".

sections.heading: Add a category
sections.body: 1) Click "Add category". 2) In the form, fill in "Tenant ID *", "Slug *" and "Display name *" (all required). The slug placeholder suggests a style like "e.g. parish-council". 3) Optionally add a description and a "Sort order". 4) Save the form. If you leave out the slug or display name you will see "Slug and display name are required." If no tenant is chosen you will see "Select a Tenant ID in the search filter (or enter one on the form)." Add, edit and delete use the selected tenant, or the tenant entered on the form.

sections.heading: Edit a category
sections.body: 1) Find the category in the table. 2) Click the pencil-style "Edit" button in the "Actions" column (its label is "Edit category"). 3) The "Edit category" form opens. Change the details and save, or click "Cancel" to close without saving. Slugs should stay stable once documents reference them, so avoid changing a slug that is already in use. If a row shows "This row has no id — it cannot be edited (fallback data).", it is from the built-in list and cannot be edited.

sections.heading: Delete a category
sections.body: 1) Find the category in the table. 2) Click the "Delete" button in the "Actions" column (its label is "Delete category"). 3) A confirmation titled "Delete category?" appears. 4) Confirm to remove it, or click "Cancel" to keep it. Be careful with categories that documents already use, since slugs should stay stable once documents reference them.

sections.heading: Browse pages and read the table
sections.body: When there are many categories, use the "Previous" and "Next" buttons under the table to move between pages. The page indicator shows "Page" and the "Showing" text tells you how many rows are displayed. The "Sort" column shows each category's sort order, and "Active" shows whether the category is active. "Slug" is the stable folder name used by uploads and year bundles, and "Display name" is the friendly name.

sections.heading: Fallback list and error messages
sections.body: If the categories service cannot be reached, the page shows a "Fallback list" of built-in slugs, with the message "Could not reach the categories API; showing built-in slug list." Fallback rows are not real records and cannot be edited. You may also see "Categories API is not available." or "Failed to load." Try again later or reload the page if you see these.

sections.heading: Rules and limits
sections.body: "Tenant ID *", "Slug *" and "Display name *" are required when creating a category. "Sort order" and the description are optional. Categories belong to a tenant (website), and the slugs are used by uploads and year bundles for that tenant. Keep slugs stable once documents reference them. Add, edit and delete use the tenant selected in the filter or entered on the form.

sections.heading: What this page is for and where things are
sections.body: Official Documents is the library for official files such as bylaws or notices that appear in the public documents (downloads) area of a website. The page is described as the official documents library for a tenant (one website): upload, categorize, and publish. From top to bottom you will find the bulk upload area ("Upload batch"), the "Add one file…" quick upload, the "Year bundle cover" section, a "Browse categories (list)" panel with "Refresh categories", and the "Tenant official documents" list with search, filters, and row actions. Pick the website with the "Tenant ID" fields before you upload or list documents.

sections.heading: Choose which website (tenant) you are working on
sections.body: Documents belong to a tenant, which is one website of your organization. In the "Tenant official documents" section, select a "Tenant ID" (placeholder "tenant_…") to list, open or download, edit, and delete documents for that website. The upload forms also have their own "Tenant ID" fields ("Tenant ID for upload" and "Tenant ID for quick add"). If no Tenant ID is selected, uploads go to the default tenant set up for the dashboard. If you see the message "Select a Tenant ID in the search filters", choose one in the filters first.

sections.heading: Upload many files at once (bulk upload)
sections.body: Use the bulk upload area to add several files or a whole folder in one batch. 1) Check the "Tenant ID". 2) Choose a "Category (slug)" from "Select category", or type a category slug such as photos or financial-statements. 3) Enter the "Year". 4) Optionally fill "Title prefix (optional)" and "Description (optional)". 5) Tick "Public (visible on downloads when data-driven mode is on)" if the files should be visible on the public downloads page. 6) Under "Files", click "Choose files" to select several files, or "Upload folder" to take every file in a folder (a flat file list). 7) Click "Upload batch". The same title prefix, description, and public setting apply to the batch.

sections.heading: Add a card thumbnail to a batch
sections.body: Under "Card thumbnail (optional, image only)", click "Choose thumbnail" to pick an image. It is applied to every file in the batch and is used as the preview for PDF and Office files on the public downloads page. Only image files are accepted. The "Recommended thumbnail size" note says to use JPG or PNG at 360 px wide × 225 px tall (a 16:10 shape) so it stays sharp on high-resolution screens; on desktop the download cards show about three per row.

sections.heading: Add a single file
sections.body: Use "Add one file…" when you only have one document. It uploads a single file to the tenant library the same way bulk upload does. 1) Select the "Tenant ID" ("Tenant ID for quick add"). 2) Choose the category and fill the optional title prefix, description, and card thumbnail. 3) Under "File", choose the file. 4) Confirm the upload. If you see "Choose a file." or "Select a category.", fill in that missing item and try again.

sections.heading: Browse and refresh categories
sections.body: The "Browse categories (list)" panel shows the document categories available for your tenant, and "Refresh categories" reloads them. If the category service cannot be reached, the page shows a built-in "Category list (fallback)" of slugs instead, with the message "Could not reach the categories API; showing built-in slug list." Categories from this fallback list have no database ID, so they cannot be used for year bundles. If the category choices look empty or out of date, click "Refresh categories".

sections.heading: Create a year bundle and set its cover image
sections.body: A year bundle groups a category's documents for one calendar year and can have a cover image. 1) Use "Create year bundle" with the category and "Year" (optionally a title prefix, description, and public setting). 2) In "Year bundle cover", check the "Category id" and "Year", then pick the "Bundle" (or "none — create below"). 3) Under "Cover image (from uploads)", choose an image already uploaded for that same category and year, or "No cover". 4) Click "Save cover".
