You will see "Create a year bundle first." if none exists yet. If no images are found, upload images with the same category and year, refresh the list, then choose one.

sections.heading: Search and filter the document list
sections.body: The "Tenant official documents" list shows Title, Public, Link, and Actions columns. 1) Select a "Tenant ID". 2) In "Search documents", choose a search field: "Title", "Description", "Media ID", or "File type". 3) Type the search term. 4) Set "Public visibility" to "All", "Public only", or "Private only". 5) Click "Search" (or "Apply" in Filters). Click "Clear" to reset. If nothing matches you will see "No documents found. Upload above or adjust filters." Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; "Page" and "Showing" tell you where you are.

sections.heading: Open, download, or edit a document
sections.body: In each list row, the link ("Open / Download") opens or downloads the file. The pencil button ("Edit document") opens the "Edit official document" window, where you can change the Title and Description. You can also manage the card thumbnail there: use "Replace thumbnail" or "Upload thumbnail" to choose a new image, or "Cancel" to close without changes. Updates and thumbnail uploads use the tenant selected in the filter or the document's own tenant. A title is required, so you will see "Title is required." if it is left blank.

sections.heading: Delete a document
sections.body: 1) Find the document in the "Tenant official documents" list. 2) Click the trash button ("Delete document") in the Actions column. 3) In the "Delete document?" confirmation, read the message: it removes the library entry for that document and cannot be undone. 4) Confirm to delete, or cancel to keep it.

sections.heading: Required fields and rules
sections.body: Messages you may see: "Select a category.", "Select or enter a category slug.", "Enter a valid year.", "Select at least one file.", "Choose a file.", and "Title is required.". Thumbnails must be images. Year bundles need a category with a numeric ID loaded from the category service, so use loaded categories rather than the fallback list. Public documents only show on the downloads page when the "Public" option is ticked and data-driven mode is on. Deleting a document cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Onboarding Requests lists new customer applications for a website (a tenant). Approving a request creates the tenant, its settings, email addresses, satellite domain and admin access in one step. The list is at the Onboarding Requests page; it has a search box, a "Add Request Manually" button, a "Review request" action on each row, and "Previous" / "Next" page buttons. Clicking a request opens its review screen, and "Add Request Manually" opens the "Add onboarding request" form. This area is for the platform super admin. The site type chosen on the request decides which tools the tenant sees.

sections.heading: Search and browse requests
sections.body: On the list, type in the search box (placeholder "Organization, email, domain, tenant id, organization id, or ONB- code"). You can search by organization, email, domain, tenant ID, organization ID or an ONB- code. Use "Clear search" to empty the box. If nothing matches you will see "No requests match this filter."; if there are none at all, "No requests found". Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to change pages; the footer shows the page and "Showing" count. Requests entered by an admin are marked "(manual)". Tenant IDs are saved to tenant settings only after approval.

sections.heading: Add a request manually
sections.body: 1) On the list, click "Add Request Manually". 2) Select an existing organization first; if you can't, create it under Organizations first, because contact and address details live there. The organization must have a contact email, otherwise you'll be told to update it under Organizations and select it again. 3) Enter the "Name prefix (you supply) *"; the sequence number is generated automatically and the "Generated Tenant ID:" appears. 4) Fill in the requested domain, site type, domain ownership, branding and optional subscription details. 5) Click "Save request". The request stays PENDING until you approve it on the review screen.

sections.heading: Request fields and logo
sections.body: Required fields are marked with *: "Site type *", "Domain ownership *", "Requested domain" (for example www.example.org) and "Contact email". Other fields include contact first/last name and phone, address lines, city, state/province, ZIP/postal code, country, "Primary color" (for example #1E40AF) and "Secondary color" (for example #F59E0B), "Tenant / site description" and "Customer notes". Tick "Wants online payments (tickets / donations)" if relevant. Choosing a domain ownership option shows matching DNS guidance and registrar details. The description applies to this website tenant only, not to the organization record.

sections.heading: Upload a tenant logo
sections.body: Under "Tenant logo (optional)", the logo is used for satellite sign-in branding and tenant settings. 1) Generate a Tenant ID (name prefix) first; until then upload is disabled. 2) Click to upload or drag an image onto "Drop image here", or paste a link into "Logo URL". Accepted: PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, max 10MB. 3) Check the "Tenant logo preview". Use "Remove logo" to clear it. Errors you may see: "Please select an image file", "File size must be less than 10MB", "Failed to upload logo".

sections.heading: Optional subscription details
sections.body: When adding a request you can set subscription details: "Subscription Plan" (Basic, Professional or Enterprise), "Subscription Status" (Active, Inactive, Suspended or Cancelled), "Subscription Start Date", "Subscription End Date", "Monthly Fee (USD)" and "Stripe Customer ID". All are optional. If these can't be saved after approval, you'll see a message to update them on Tenant Settings.

sections.heading: Review and edit a request
sections.body: Click "Review request" on a row to open the review screen. It shows "Request details" (including Source, Submitted, Reviewed, Submitter IP and Reviewer comments) and a "Provisioning" section. Change values, then click "Save changes"; "Changes saved." confirms. If fields are invalid you'll see "Fix the highlighted request fields first." Use "Back to onboarding requests" to return. If a request was deleted you'll see "This onboarding request is no longer available"; if it fails to load, refresh the page or go back to the list.

sections.heading: Approve and create the tenant
sections.body: In "Provisioning", set the "Tenant ID prefix" (letters, numbers and underscores only, ending with a letter; hyphens are not allowed), plus satellite key and hostname (both required). Optional fields: "Display name", "Contact email (site)" (defaults to contact email), "Info email", "Copy admins from tenant" and "Reviewer comments (internal)". Use "Check availability" to see "Available" or "Already in use". Option "Copy platform ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN profiles" and "Email the customer about the decision" are available. Click approve, then confirm "Approve and create tenant?". If any step fails, nothing is created. If an attempt failed, a note appears and you can fix values and use "Retry approval". After success, "Approval successful" lists Tenant ID, Satellite key, Hostname, No-reply email and Admins copied.

sections.heading: After approval: next steps and copy tools
sections.body: The success panel offers "View Organization", "Edit Tenant Settings" and "Satellite Domains" links, plus "Remaining manual steps" that depend on the domain ownership chosen (Route 53 / Amplify DNS guidance). Use "Copy instructions" to copy organization details and the remaining manual steps, "Copy org details" for the organization database details, and "Copy Cursor prompt" for the frontend clone prompt and satellite environment checklist. Some warnings may say site-type presets or default hero/logo were not applied; set them in Tenant Settings. Afterwards, promote the customer's first ADMIN from Manage Users once they register on their satellite.

sections.heading: Reject a request
sections.body: 1) Open the request and click "Reject". 2) In "Reason for rejecting", type a reason; it is required. 3) Choose whether to "Email the customer about the decision": if on, the reason is emailed to the customer; if off, the customer will not be emailed. 4) Click "Reject request" to confirm, or "Keep request" to cancel. "Request rejected." confirms the result.

sections.heading: What the Billing pages are for
sections.body: Billing (/admin/billing) shows platform billing: what an organization or website owes for the software platform. This is not ticket or event revenue. The main page lists tenant IDs, and each tenant (website) has its own billing page at /admin/billing/[tenantId]. The page explains that paid admin tools are locked until a platform fee is paid, and that the site itself stays online. If the list is empty, select an organization on Admin Home to list its tenant IDs.

sections.heading: Open a tenant's billing page
sections.body: On the Billing page, find the "Tenant IDs" list with the note "Choose a tenant to open its billing page." 1) Look for the website in the "Tenant ID" column. 2) Click "Open billing" in that row. 3) If the list has several pages, use "Previous" and "Next". The list shows "Loading tenant IDs..." while it loads, and "This organization has no tenant IDs yet." if there are none. If it fails you will see "Could not load tenant IDs."

sections.heading: Review billing status and settings
sections.body: On a tenant's page, the "Platform billing" panel shows "Status" and these settings: "Catalog plan" (or "No catalog plan"), "Custom fee USD (blank uses the catalog)", "Review-by date (reminder only)", "Grace days" and the "Charge switch". A review-by date is a reminder only and does not start a charge. Unpaid grace locks paid admin tools and leaves the site online. Saved changes show "Billing saved." If something fails you may see "Could not save" or "Request failed".

sections.heading: Turn charging on or off
sections.body: The "Charge switch" controls whether this tenant can be charged. Use the button "Turn charging on" or "Turn charging off" (also shown as "Turn the charge switch on" or "Turn the charge switch off"). When the switch is off, the page says "Switch is off. Stripe is not called." Turning the switch on does not charge the card by itself; once charging is allowed, use a pay link. If you see a message that only a platform super-admin can change platform billing, your account cannot make this change.

sections.heading: Pay the platform fee
sections.body: Use "Pay monthly" or "Pay once" to open Stripe Checkout, where you can pay with a card or a US bank account. Bank debit appears when ACH Direct Debit is active on the Stripe account. Use "Payment methods" to manage how you pay. Paid admin tools unlock once the platform fee is paid.

sections.heading: Location count and included locations
sections.body: The "Locations counted in the location fee" list shows which locations count toward the fee, with "Include this location" or "Remove this location" actions, and "Not included" for those left out. A custom flat fee uses quantity 1; otherwise the count is the active locations marked included. Including or removing a location saves the choice only ("Location inclusion saved."). To change the Stripe quantity, click "Update location count" afterward. If you see no include or remove buttons, the page says to ask the platform team. A failure shows "Could not update the location".

sections.heading: Cancel a subscription
sections.body: Two cancel options appear: "Cancel at period end" and "Cancel now". Cancel at period end shows "The subscription will cancel at the end of the period." Cancel now shows "Canceled now. The card is Complimentary. Pay monthly starts a new subscription." To subscribe again after canceling, use "Pay monthly".

sections.heading: Free, demo and organization-covered websites
sections.body: Some tenants show special messages instead of normal charging. If the plan is free or demo, the charge switch stays off and Stripe is not called. If the website is covered by its organization, the organization subscription is the one that is paid and canceled, shown in the "Organization subscription" section. If a tenant is covered by an organization portfolio charge, clear that portfolio fee before charging the tenant on its own.

sections.heading: View and filter charges
sections.body: The "Charges" table lists platform charges recorded for the website. Filter with "Fee" ("All fees", "Event site", "Retail locations"), "Status" ("All statuses" or a specific status) and "From" (a start date). Use "Open in charge search" to look at charges in charge search, and "Change history" to see past changes. A note "This invoice was paid later." marks late-paid invoices. Messages: "Loading charges…", "No charges match these filters.", "No platform charges are recorded for this website yet." or "Charges could not be loaded."

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: "Platform billing plans" is the fee catalog used to charge tenants (websites). It lists catalog prices for event sites and retail shops. These are not ticket prices and not membership plans. The page has an "Add plan" button, a list of plans with columns such as Name, Product, Billing, Interval, Price, Visibility and Stripe price, and an "Edit" action on each row. Count badges at the top show how many plans are "Event site", "Retail", "Published" and "Hidden". Use "Back to Platform Billing" to return to the main billing page. Changing platform billing is for platform super admins only.

sections.heading: Reading the plan list
sections.body: Each row shows the plan's name, its product ("Event site" or "Retail"), whether billing is recurring or one-time, the interval, the price, whether it is published or hidden, and the Stripe price. If nothing has been created yet, the list says "No plans yet". The badges at the top count plans by product and by visibility, so you can see at a glance how many are published and how many are hidden. If the list is long, use the "Previous" and "Next" page buttons; the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed with them.

sections.heading: Adding a plan
sections.body: 1) Click "Add plan". 2) Fill in "Name", "Code", "Product" and "List price (USD)". 3) Choose "Billing" ("Recurring or one-time", "Recurring only" or "One-time only"). 4) Optionally add a "Stripe price id" and a "Feature summary". 5) Save. You will see "The plan was added." The new plan appears in the list. Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Choosing a product and shop pack
sections.body: "Product" can be "Event site" or "Retail". For a retail plan you can also choose a "Shop pack" such as gas station, liquor store, or Dunkin; this is optional. Leave the shop pack empty ("All retail packs") to use the price for every shop pack. The product option may also show as "Retail (saved as gas station)".

sections.heading: Editing a plan
sections.body: 1) Find the plan in the list. 2) Click "Edit" on its row. 3) Change the fields you need, such as name, price, billing type, Stripe price id or feature summary. 4) Save. You will see "The plan was updated." A "Saved" indicator confirms the change. Click "Cancel" to leave without saving.

sections.heading: Publishing or hiding a plan
sections.body: In the plan form, the published option controls visibility. Published plans are available to assign; hidden plans stay off the tenant catalog until you assign one. The "Visibility" column and the "Published" and "Hidden" badges show the current state. Edit the plan to change it.

sections.heading: Rules and access
sections.body: Only a platform super admin can change platform billing; otherwise you may see "Only a platform super-admin can change platform billing" or "Admin access required". If you are signed out you will see "Sign in required". "Billing" lets you pick recurring only, one-time only, or either. "List price (USD)" is the price in US dollars. Plans save when you save the form, not as you type.

sections.heading: Poll Management overview
sections.body: The Poll Management page (Admin Panel > Management > Polls, at /admin/polls) is where you create and manage interactive polls for your events for this tenant (website). The main area is a list titled "Polls" with a search box ("Search polls...") and a "Create Poll" button. Each poll in the list shows its status ("Active", "Inactive", "Scheduled" or "Ended") and details such as "Start Date:", "End Date:", "Max Responses:", "Multiple Choices:" and "Anonymous:". Each row has three actions: "View Poll", "Edit Poll" and "Delete Poll". Responses are collected on the public site.

sections.heading: Create a new poll
sections.body: Click "Create Poll" (or "Create Your First Poll" if no polls exist yet) to open the "Create New Poll" form. 1) Fill in the "Poll Details" section: "Poll Title *", optional "Description", "Start Date *" and optional "End Date". 2) Add your choices under "Poll Options". 3) Set the options under "Poll Settings". 4) Save the poll. When it works you see "Poll Created Successfully!" and the poll is available for voting. If something goes wrong you see "Failed to Create Poll" and can try again. Use "Cancel" to close the form without creating anything.

sections.heading: Add and remove answer options
sections.body: In the "Poll Options" section ("Add the choices for your poll"), click "Add Option" to add another answer choice. To remove a choice, use the "Delete Option" button next to it. A poll needs at least 2 options, otherwise the form shows "At least 2 poll options are required".

sections.heading: Poll settings
sections.body: The "Poll Settings" section controls how people interact with the poll. "Active" makes the poll available for voting. "Anonymous Voting" lets users vote without revealing their identity. "Multiple Choices" lets users select more than one option. "Max Responses Per User" sets how many responses each user can give. "Results Visible To" lets you choose "All Users", "Voters Only" or "Admins Only".

sections.heading: Required fields and validation
sections.body: The form checks your entries before saving. "Poll Title *" is required ("Poll title is required"). "Start Date *" is required ("Start date is required"). If you set an "End Date", it must be after the start date ("End date must be after start date"). You need at least 2 options. "Max Responses Per User" must be at least 1. Description and End Date are optional.

sections.heading: View a poll and its results
sections.body: Click "View Poll" on a poll row to open its details window. It shows the status ("Active", "Inactive", "Scheduled" or "Ended"), a "Poll Information" section (description, dates, max responses, multiple choices, anonymous, results visible), "Poll Options & Results" and "Recent Responses". Click "Close" when you are done. If responses cannot be loaded you see an error message about fetching poll responses.

sections.heading: Edit a poll
sections.body: Click "Edit Poll" on a poll row to open the "Edit Poll" form ("Update poll settings and options"). Change the details, options or settings, then save. You see "Poll Updated Successfully!" when the changes are saved. If the poll cannot be loaded you see "Failed to Load Poll", and if saving fails you see "Failed to Update Poll".

sections.heading: Delete a poll
sections.body: Click "Delete Poll" on a poll row, then confirm by clicking "Delete" in the confirmation. The poll is permanently removed and you see "Poll Deleted Successfully!". If it fails you see "Failed to Delete Poll".

sections.heading: Search the poll list
sections.body: Type in the "Search polls..." box above the list to narrow the polls shown. Click "Clear search" to show all polls again. If nothing matches, the list shows "No polls found matching your search." If you have no polls yet, it shows "No polls created yet."

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Profile Site page (/admin/profile-site, titled "Personal profile tenants") manages a personal or hybrid profile website: writings, projects, services and contact blocks. Pick a tenant (one website) first, then work on its "Personal Profile Site" details. The page has a profile form with a "Save Profile" button, content lists (Writings / Portfolio, Achievements, Affiliations, Projects / Case Studies, Professional Services, Family, Media / Talks / Downloads) and a "Profile audience" panel for contacts. Lists use a "+ Add" button and "Edit" and "Delete" links on each row.

sections.heading: Choose which tenant to manage
sections.body: Before anything shows, you need to select a website tenant. The page says "Select a tenant to manage — or type a Tenant ID in the blue bar at the top". 1) Wait for "Loading tenants…" to finish. 2) Click "Select →" next to the tenant you want. Alternatively, type the Tenant ID in the blue bar at the top of the dashboard. A tenant is one website, so the ID picks a website, not an organization.

sections.heading: Edit the profile details
sections.body: In the "Personal Profile Site" section, fill in the profile fields and click "Save Profile". The fields are: Tagline, Headline, Public slug, Contact email, "Booking URL (Calendly etc.)", Location, "Profile image URL", LinkedIn, X / Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Website, "CV document URL" and "Bio (markdown)". There are also checkboxes for "Enable contact form" and "Published". "Display name" is required, and if it is empty you will see "Display name is required". After saving you will see "Profile saved.", or "Save failed." if something went wrong.

sections.heading: Add, edit or delete list items
sections.body: Each content list works the same way. 1) Click "+ Add" to open the form for a new entry. 2) Fill in the fields and save, or click "Cancel" to close the form without adding. 3) To change an entry, click "Edit" on its row. 4) To remove an entry, click "Delete" on its row. An empty list shows "No entries." Fields marked required must be filled in before you can save.

sections.heading: Writings / Portfolio
sections.body: The list shows Title, Type, Publication, Status and Order for each piece. When adding or editing, fill in Title (required), Type, URL slug, External URL, Publication, Featured image URL, Excerpt, Body (full article), Published date, Status and Display order. Type can be Original, Republished or External link. Status can be Draft, Published or Archived. Use the Display order number to control where the piece appears.

sections.heading: Achievements, Affiliations and Family
sections.body: Achievements list Category, Issuer and Date. Fields are Category (Award, Honor, Speaking, Education or Other), Issuer, Date, Description, URL, Image URL and a "Featured" checkbox. Affiliations list Organization, Role, From and To. Fields are Organization (required), Role, Start date, End date and Logo URL. Family lists Name, Relationship and Role. Fields are Display name (required), Relationship, "Role / title" and Photo URL.

sections.heading: Projects, Professional Services and Media
sections.body: Projects / Case Studies have Your role, Summary, Cover image URL, Project URL, a Featured checkbox and an "Outcome metrics JSON" field. Professional Services show a From price and an Active status. Their fields are Category, Starting price, Price unit, Currency, CTA label, CTA URL and an Active checkbox. Media / Talks / Downloads show Kind, File type and Downloadable. Their fields are Media kind, "File / media URL" (required), File type, and the checkboxes "Downloadable" and "Requires email".

sections.heading: Manage profile audience contacts
sections.body: The "Profile audience" panel lists contacts for the selected tenant. It is separate from member email subscriptions. The table shows Email, Name, Source, Status and Actions, with "Previous" and "Next" buttons to page through. To find someone, type in the "Search email…" box. To add a contact, click "Add contact", fill in Email (required), First name and Last name, then click "Save". Use "Edit" or "Delete" on a row to change or remove a contact. Deleting asks "Delete this contact?" first.

sections.heading: Import contacts from a CSV file
sections.body: Click "Import CSV" in the "Profile audience" panel and choose a .csv file to add many contacts at once. If it does not work, you will see "CSV import failed." Only .csv files are accepted.

sections.heading: Send a newsletter to the audience
sections.body: 1) In the "Profile audience" panel, enter the "Newsletter template ID". 2) Click "Send to audience". 3) You will see "Send to profile audience started." when it begins. If the ID is not valid, you will see "Enter a valid promotion email template ID." Click "Cancel" to close without sending.

sections.heading: Required fields and messages
sections.body: Required fields are: Display name for the profile, Title for a writing, Organization for an affiliation, Display name for a family member, "File / media URL" for a media item, and Email for a contact. Image, document and link fields take web addresses (URLs) as text, not uploaded files. Messages you may see include "Profile saved.", "Save failed.", "Contact saved.", "Failed to save contact.", "Contact deleted." and "Failed to delete contact."

sections.heading: Overview of Promotion Emails
sections.body: The Promotion Emails page (titled "Promotional Emails for Events") is where you manage email templates for events and send them. The main list is called "Email Templates" and has a "Filter by Event" box, a "Status" filter, and a search box. At the top you will find the "Create New Template" and "Email History" buttons. Each template row has action icons for editing, duplicating, testing and sending, and deleting. Opening a template (the Edit icon) takes you to its own edit page, titled "Edit Promotion Email Template", where you can use "Back to Promotion Emails" or "Back to templates" to return.

sections.heading: Find and filter templates
sections.body: In the "Email Templates" list, use "Filter by Event" to show templates for one event, or keep "All Events". Use "Status" to choose "All", "Active" or "Inactive". Type in the search box ("Search by name or subject...") to find a template by its name or subject, and use the clear button ("Clear template search") to reset it. The list shows "Template Name", "Event", "Subject" and "Created". Hover over a template name to see a popup with "Template Details" such as subject, event ID, status, promotion code, header and footer images, dates, and a body preview. Long lists are split into pages; use "Previous" and "Next". If nothing matches, you see "No templates match your filters".

sections.heading: Create a new template
sections.body: 1) Click "Create New Template". 2) Fill in "Template Name" (for example, Summer Sale 2024) and "Email Subject". 3) Choose the event, since you will be asked "Please select an event" if you skip it. 4) Pick a from email address from the list of verified addresses. 5) Optionally choose a "Discount Code (Optional)" or leave it as "None". 6) Enter the "Email Body HTML" and, if needed, the "Email Footer HTML". Click "Click to see example HTML" for a sample. 7) Leave "Template is active" ticked if you want it active, then click "Create Template". After it saves you are redirected back to the list. Header and footer images can only be added after the template is created, by editing it. If the chosen event has no discount codes, you will see a note to create one in the event's discount codes section.

sections.heading: From email rules
sections.body: The from email must be registered and verified with AWS SES (Amazon Simple Email Service). The from-email box lets you search and select from the active verified addresses set up for your tenant; one may be marked "Default". If the list is empty, you will see a message asking you to contact your admin to add from email addresses. If your domain is verified in SES, any valid address on that domain can be used. You cannot send an email where the From and To addresses are the same, and Hotmail accounts do not work as the From address. You will see "Please enter from email address" or "Please enter a valid email address" if the field is missing or incorrect.

sections.heading: Edit a template
sections.body: 1) In the template list, click the Edit icon on the template row (right-click it to open in a new tab). 2) Change the "Template Name", "Email Subject", "Discount Code (Optional)", body HTML, footer HTML, or the "Template is active" box. 3) Click "Update Template". You will see a saving message and are then redirected to the promotion emails list. Click "Cancel" to leave without saving. If the page says "This template could not be loaded" or "This template is no longer available", refresh the page or go back to the template list and open it again.

sections.heading: Upload header and footer images
sections.body: On a template's edit page, the "Header Image" and "Footer Image" sections accept image files (PNG, JPG, GIF up to 5MB). 1) Click the upload area or drag and drop an image onto it. 2) A preview appears and the image is uploaded and saved right away, with a success message. 3) To remove an image, use the remove option on the preview; it is also removed immediately. If you drop something that is not an image, you see "Please drop a valid image file". In the footer section you can also tick "Add site footer" to insert your homepage-style footer (tenant name, contact, links) when the template is saved or sent. You can use both footer image and site footer together. The email logo and footer can also be set in Tenant Settings → Customization.

sections.heading: Duplicate or delete a template
sections.body: To copy a template, click the Duplicate icon on its row; you see "Template duplicated successfully!" when done. To remove a template, click the Delete icon. A "Delete Template" window asks "Are you sure you want to delete this template?" and warns that it is permanent and cannot be undone. Click the delete confirmation to proceed, or "Cancel" to keep it.

sections.heading: Send test, bulk, or member emails
sections.body: Each template row has three send icons. "Send Test" sends a test email so you can check the contents: enter the address in the "Recipient Email Address" box ("Enter email address") and click "Send Test Email"; a valid email is required. "Send Bulk" sends to the event attendees registered for that event. "Send to Subscribed Members" (shown as "Send to All Members" in the guide) is a global email to all members who subscribed to receive emails. For both bulk options a confirmation window appears; click "Confirm & Send" to continue or "Cancel" to stop. These sends cannot be undone. You will see "Send Successfully!" when it works, and the first email may take a minute or two to arrive.

sections.heading: View email history
sections.body: Click "Email History" at the top of the page to see emails that were sent. Filter by "Event" (or "All Events"), "Status" ("Sent", "Failed", "Bounced", or "All Statuses"), and by "Start Date" and "End Date". The table shows "Recipient", "Subject", "Sent At", and marks test emails as "Test Email". Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. If nothing matches, you see "No emails found". Click the close button to leave the history.

sections.heading: What the QR Scanner page is for
sections.body: The QR Scanner page (/admin/qr-scanner) is titled "QR Code Scanner" with the line "Scan QR codes to verify and check in tickets". Use it at the door to scan a ticket QR code and mark that person checked in for this tenant (website). The page shows your camera view, a "Switch Camera" button, and an "Instructions:" list. After a scan, the result appears with the ticket details and a "Valid Ticket" or "Invalid Ticket" message. For arrival numbers compared with ticket buyers, use Check-in Analytics. For revenue totals, use Sales Analytics.

sections.heading: Scan a ticket at the door
sections.body: 1) Open the QR Scanner page and allow camera access if your browser asks. 2) Point your camera at the QR code on the ticket. 3) Make sure the code is clearly visible and well lit. 4) Wait while the page shows "Scanning..."; it detects and verifies the code automatically, so you don't need to press a button. While it checks, you will see "Verifying QR code...".

sections.heading: What a valid ticket shows
sections.body: When the ticket is good, the page shows "Valid Ticket" and the ticket details: "Transaction ID:", "Event ID:", "Email:", "Name:", "Quantity:", "Status:" and "Check-In Status:". It then shows "Redirecting to check-in page..." and takes you to the check-in page, where the person is checked in. Valid tickets redirect to the check-in page automatically.

sections.heading: If a ticket is invalid or verification fails
sections.body: An invalid ticket shows "Invalid Ticket" with the message "This ticket cannot be checked in." If the check itself did not work, you will see "Verification failed" or "Failed to verify QR code. Please try again." Under "Error", read the message and try again. To scan the next ticket, click "Scan Another QR Code".

sections.heading: Scan another QR code
sections.body: After a result or an error is shown, click "Scan Another QR Code" to clear it and return to scanning. Use this between guests so the camera is ready for the next ticket.

sections.heading: Switch between front and back cameras
sections.body: Click "Switch Camera" (shown on the scanner as "Switch" in some views) to toggle between the front and back cameras of your device. Try this if the picture is hard to use, or if you see a message that camera constraints are not supported. Switching cameras or using a different device is the suggested fix for that message.

sections.heading: Fix camera permission problems
sections.body: If you see "Camera Permission Denied" or a message that camera access was denied, your browser is blocking the camera. To fix it: 1) Click the lock icon in your browser's address bar. 2) Select "Allow" for camera permissions. 3) Reload this page. The page's instructions and messages all tell you to enable camera access in your browser settings and reload.

sections.heading: Other camera messages
sections.body: "Camera device not found" or "No camera found" means the device has no working camera, so check that it has one. "Camera is already in use by another application" means you should close other apps using the camera. If scanning fails to start, you may see "Failed to start scanning:" followed by a reason. Trying "Switch Camera", reloading, or using a different device can help.

sections.heading: Overview of the check-in page
sections.body: This page opens for one ticket purchase (transaction) of an event, usually after scanning the buyer's ticket QR code. It shows the purchase details and lets you record how many guests have checked in. The page has a "Transaction Summary" section, a "Ticket Breakdown" table, and a check-in form with the "Update Check-In" button. After a successful check-in you can use "Scan Another QR Code" to continue with the next guest.

sections.heading: Read the Transaction Summary
sections.body: The "Transaction Summary" section shows the details of the purchase. It lists "Name", "Amount Paid", "Date of Purchase", "Check-In Status", "Number of Guests Checked In" and "Check-In Time". Use it to confirm the buyer and see whether anyone from this purchase has already checked in.

sections.heading: Review the Ticket Breakdown
sections.body: The "Ticket Breakdown" table lists what was bought in this purchase. Each row shows the "Ticket Type", "Quantity", "Price Per Unit" and "Total". Use it to see how many guests the purchase covers before you enter a check-in number.

sections.heading: Check in guests
sections.body: To check guests in: 1) Open the page by scanning the QR code or using the transaction link. 2) In the check-in form, enter the count in "Number of People Checking In". 3) Click "Update Check-In". While saving, the button shows "Updating...". When it works, you see "Check-In Successful!" and the message "Check-in status updated successfully."

sections.heading: When check-in is already done
sections.body: If the purchase has already been fully checked in, the form shows "Check-in is done". You can compare this with "Check-In Status", "Number of Guests Checked In" and "Check-In Time" in the summary above.

sections.heading: Scan another QR code
sections.body: After a successful check-in, click "Scan Another QR Code" to go on to the next guest's ticket.

sections.heading: Copy or open the event address
sections.body: Where an event address is shown, you can use "Copy address" to copy it. "Copied!" confirms it worked. Use "Open in Google Maps" to see the location on a map. If copying fails, a "Failed to copy location:" message appears.

sections.heading: Errors and not-found messages
sections.body: If the page shows "Check-In Not Found", no ticket or check-in record was found for this QR code or transaction. Check the QR code or transaction link and try again. The page may also say "An error occurred while loading check-in details. Please try again later." If saving fails, you see "Error" and "Failed to update check-in. Please try again." Try again, and if it keeps happening, contact event support.

sections.heading: What the Retail pages are for
sections.body: Retail covers shops and stores such as gas stations, liquor stores, Dunkin', 7-Eleven, restaurants and clinics. The main page, /admin/retail, shows the "Retail morning brief": action cards for one store on one date. Retail tool tiles lead to the sub-pages: "Locations" (stores in this organization), "Compare stores", "Assign managers", plus pages for uploading a day of register and fuel files and for retail integrations. If the page asks you to pick a website first, use the tenant picker ("Select a tenant to manage") or type a Tenant ID in the blue bar at the top. A search box on the tools page lets you find tools by name, such as morning brief, locations, or managers.

sections.heading: Read the morning brief
sections.body: On the "Retail morning brief" page, 1) pick a "Brief date", 2) pick a "Store" from the list. The list shows only stores you are allowed to see for this tenant, and gallons appear only for a gas station. The brief is one date and one store; day numbers come from the register and, for gas packs, the fuel controller. A tile that has nothing shows "No data for this day". If you see "You do not have a retail role for this tenant.", your account has no retail access for that tenant. Use "Refresh brief" to rebuild the cards for the chosen store and date; it usually takes under a minute, so wait until it finishes. If it fails you will see "Refresh failed. Try again in a moment."

sections.heading: Work with cards and ask questions
sections.body: The "Morning action list" shows recommendation cards with an estimated impact ("est. impact"). Each card has the buttons "Accept", "Dismiss", "Done" and "Ask about this". A chain-level card compares stores across the chain for the brief date. In the "Ask about this brief" box, type a question or tap a suggestion such as "What's driving today's top card?", "How much is in-store sales?", "Which card has the biggest estimated impact?" or "How did fuel gallons look today?". "Ask about this" on a card fills the question for you. The answer usually takes a few seconds; if there is none you see "No answer yet for this brief." This box answers questions about the brief data and is separate from the Admin Help chat.

sections.heading: Upload a store day from files
sections.body: On the upload page ("Upload day"), save one store's day from files. 1) Choose the "Store". 2) Choose the "Business date". 3) Under "Register file" click "Choose register file". 4) For a gas station also click "Choose fuel file" under "Fuel file". 5) Click "Upload and save" and wait until the day is saved. Only CSV files are accepted. Uploading the same date again overwrites that day, and the result then says "This date was overwritten." A success shows "Day saved". "Example files" are provided; they stay dated 2026-07-08, and the business date you choose becomes the day that is saved.

sections.heading: Upload messages and what they mean
sections.body: Before uploading you must fill in everything required, or you will see "Choose a store.", "Choose a business date.", "Choose a register file." or, for a gas station, "Choose a fuel file for a gas station." If the upload fails you see "The day was not uploaded." Other messages can appear saying the day result was incomplete, or that the day was accepted but not posted to the retail tables; these point to a setup problem on the service side, so share the exact message with your platform team. The page also notes that files were stored on the engine host, and that cloud uploads use the S3 feature store.

sections.heading: View and edit locations
sections.body: The "Retail locations" page lists stores with the columns Tenant, Pack, Name, Code, Brand, Region, City, State, Dispensers and Active. If none exist you see "No locations for this tenant." To change a store, use "Edit location" on its row, update the details and click "Save" (or "Cancel"). Options include "Open 24 hours", "Active", "Counted in the location fee", "Car wash", "Lottery" and "Food service". Pack choices are Gas station, Liquor store, Dunkin, 7-Eleven, Restaurant and Clinic. "Name, code, and tenant are required." The page states: "To add or remove a location, contact the platform team. You can edit the details of the locations listed here." If you also see the "Add location" or "Delete location" buttons, they work like the other row actions.

sections.heading: Manage retail integrations
sections.body: "Retail integrations" connects a store's systems, such as payment and inventory. The list shows Store, System, Provider, Connection, Credentials ref, Config JSON, Mode and Credentials. To add one, click "Add integration", 1) "Choose a store", 2) fill in the details, 3) tick "Enabled" if it should be active, 4) click "Save". The credentials reference field gives examples like demo-pos-loc3 or an arn:aws:secretsmanager value. Use "Edit integration" on a row to change it, or "Delete integration" to remove it. "Cancel" closes the form without saving. If saving fails you see "The integration was not saved."

sections.heading: Compare stores
sections.body: "Compare stores" shows stores side by side for a date range. 1) Choose the start date in "From" and an end date. 2) Review the table: Store, Pack, Sales, Labor, Waste, Expected profit, Actual profit, Gallons and Fuel margin. If a date is missing you see "Choose a start date and an end date."

sections.heading: Assign store and regional managers
sections.body: Open "Assign managers" to see "Retail assignments". Owners assign a store manager to stores and a regional manager to region names. Only an owner or admin can assign retail managers. 1) For each store, choose a "Store manager" and click "Save stores"; you will see "Store assignments saved." or "Store assignments were not saved." 2) For each "Regional manager", type their regions in "Regions, separated by commas" and click "Save regions"; you will see "Region assignments saved." or "Region assignments were not saved." A store with a blank region stays off the regional list. If no one is available you see that there is no profile with the store manager or regional manager role for this tenant.

sections.heading: Rules and what saves when
sections.body: Uploads accept CSV files only, and a gas station needs both a register file and a fuel file. Re-uploading a date overwrites that day. On locations and integrations, changes are kept only after you click "Save"; "Cancel" discards them. On the managers page, store and region assignments are saved with their own buttons: "Save stores" and "Save regions". A location needs a name, code and tenant. Retail access can be limited to users with retail profiles even if they are not full admins. Long lists use "Previous" and "Next" page buttons.

sections.heading: What the Roster catalogs page is for
sections.body: "Roster catalogs" holds the dropdown lists that squads use: sports, achievement categories, and team types. The main page (under "What these catalogs control") shows one block for each catalog, with a manage button: "Manage sports categories", "Manage achievement categories" and "Manage team types". Each manage page lets you search, move between pages, add, edit, and remove rows. Use "Back to Roster catalogs" on a manage page to return to the main page. Rows are added for the selected organization.

sections.heading: Sports catalog
sections.body: The sports catalog lists Olympic sports and other widely played sports, including pickleball, padel, cricket, and kabaddi. They show as checkboxes on a squad member. A shared sport is available to every tenant (website). Open it with "Manage sports categories" on the main page. When you edit a row, the save button reads "Update sport".

sections.heading: Achievement categories catalog
sections.body: Achievement categories cover award, honor, trophy, and any category you add for a squad member. Open the list with "Manage achievement categories". Use "Add category" to create a new one; when editing, the save button reads "Update category".

sections.heading: Team types catalog
sections.body: Team types are used by squad groups. Sports and music stay available to every tenant. Open the list with "Manage team types". Use "Add team type" to create one; when editing, the save button reads "Update team type".

sections.heading: Search and move between pages
sections.body: On a manage page, type in the "Search by name or code" box to filter the rows. If nothing matches, you see "[No rows match your search]". Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; the current "Page" number and a "Showing" count appear with them. A page with no rows shows "No rows on this page."

sections.heading: Add or edit a row
sections.body: 1) On a manage page, use the add button ("Add category" or "Add team type") or choose "Edit" on a row. 2) Fill in "Code" and "Label". Both are required, otherwise you see "Code and label are required". 3) Set "Sort order" to control the order in the list, and tick "Active" to keep the row in use. 4) Save with the update/add button; a "Saved" message confirms it, and "Could not save" means it failed. Use "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Shared rows and rows for one tenant
sections.body: The list has a "Scope" column showing whether a row is "Shared". Shared rows apply to every organization. A row saved for the selected tenant is visible only there. The option "Shared with every tenant" makes a row shared. Only a platform super admin can change a shared catalog row; otherwise you get the message "Only a platform super admin can change a shared catalog row".

sections.heading: Deactivate or remove a row
sections.body: In the list, the row actions are "Edit", "Deactivate", and "Remove" (under the "Actions" column). "Deactivate" turns off a row; the "Active" column shows its state. "Remove" deletes the row; if it fails you see "Remove failed". Shared rows can only be changed by a platform super admin.

sections.heading: Columns and rules
sections.body: The list columns are "Code", "Label", "Order", "Scope", "Active", and "Actions". "Code" and "Label" are required when saving. "Sort order" sets where a row appears. Changes to a row take effect when you save it. Shared rows can be changed only by a platform super admin.

sections.heading: What the Sales Analytics page is for
sections.body: The Sales Analytics page (Admin > Sales Analytics) lets you view and analyze ticket sales for your events. It shows ticket sales metrics and transaction history for events in this tenant (website). Start by choosing an event with the "Search Events" panel and optionally a date range. After that, the page shows summary cards, charts and breakdowns, and a "Sales Transactions" list. Until you pick an event, a "Getting Started" message asks you to enter an Event ID to view sales analytics and reports. A batch job button for Stripe fees and tax is also on this page.

sections.heading: Choose an event to analyze
sections.body: Use the "Search Events" panel to find an event. 1) Pick an option in "Search By" (for example "Title", "Caption", "Start Date" or "End Date"). 2) Type your search. 3) Narrow results with "Admission" ("All", "Free" or "Paid"). 4) Change the order with "Sort": "Date (Earliest)", "Date (Latest)", "Title (A-Z)", "Title (Z-A)", "ID (Newest)" or "ID (Oldest)". 5) Select the event from the results. While searching you may see "Loading events...". If nothing matches you will see "No events found matching your search criteria.", and before you search the panel says "Enter search criteria to find events."

sections.heading: Filter by date range
sections.body: Use the date range selector to limit the sales shown. You can type dates in the "From:" and "To:" boxes (format mm/dd/yyyy) or click a quick button: "Last 7 Days", "Last 30 Days", "Last 90 Days", "Last 6 Months", "Last Year" or "All Time". The start date must be before or equal to the end date, otherwise you will see "Start date must be before or equal to end date".

sections.heading: Read the summary cards and charts
sections.body: After an event loads, cards show "Total Revenue", "Gross Revenue", "Net Revenue", "Avg Ticket Price", "Total Transactions", "Total Discounts", "Total Refunds" and "Platform Fees". Another card, "Net Revenue Before Tax", is described as "After Stripe fees, before tax". Below are "Revenue by Payment Method" and trend views: "Sales Trends by Day", "Sales Trends by Week", "Sales Trends by Month" and "Sales by Hour". While data loads you will see "Loading sales analytics...".

sections.heading: Manual payment breakdown
sections.body: If the event has manual payments, the "Manual Payment Status Breakdown" section appears. It breaks down manual payment transactions (Zelle, Venmo, Cash, etc.) by status. Manual payment types such as "Wire Transfer" and "Other Manual Payment" may appear in the payment method figures.

sections.heading: Search and browse transactions
sections.body: The "Sales Transactions" list shows "Transaction ID", "Name", "Email", "Quantity", "Gross Amount", "Discount", "Final Amount", "Platform Fee", "Payment Method" and "Purchase Date". To find a buyer, type in the search box ("Search by name, email, or ID..."). Click the clear button ("Clear sales search") to reset it. If nothing matches, you will see "No transactions found". Use "Previous" and "Next" ("Previous Page" and "Next Page") to move between pages. The "Showing" text tells you which rows you are viewing.

sections.heading: Export sales to CSV or Excel
sections.body: Use the "CSV" button ("Export to CSV") or the "Excel" button ("Export to Excel") near the "Sales Transactions" list to download the sales data as a file. Choose your event and date range first so the export covers what you want. The page refers to the result as a "Sales Report".

sections.heading: Trigger the Stripe Fees and Tax Update batch job
sections.body: This batch job retrieves missing Stripe fee and tax data from Stripe and updates transaction records. It runs in the background. 1) Click the "Trigger Stripe Fees and Tax Update Batch Job" button. 2) In "Batch Job Options", optionally enter a Tenant ID (leave it empty to process all tenants). 3) Optionally tick "Force update (reprocess transactions that already have Stripe fee data)". 4) Click "Trigger Batch Job"; the button shows "Starting Batch Job..." while it works. On success you see "Batch job started successfully!" with the Job ID, Status, Estimated Records and Estimated Completion. If no date range is chosen, the note says no date filter applies and all dates are processed.

sections.heading: Manual payment events and the batch job
sections.body: If the event is set up for manual payments, you see a "Manual Payment Event Detected" notice. The batch job is only applicable to Stripe payments, and manual payments (Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, etc.) have no Stripe fees. If the event also has Stripe payments, you can still trigger the batch job to update Stripe fee data for those transactions.

sections.heading: Common messages and problems
sections.body: "Failed to load sales metrics" or "Failed to load sales data" means the figures could not be loaded; try again. "Request timed out. Please try again." means the request took too long. For the batch job, "Invalid date range" means the start date is after the end date. "Authentication failed. Please refresh the page and try again." means you should reload the page. "You do not have permission to trigger this batch job." means your account is not allowed to run it. For service or server errors, try again later or contact support.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Satellite Domains" page (Admin → Satellite Domains) lets you manage the custom public web addresses that sign in through this hub, along with their branding. A satellite domain is a tenant's custom public URL that runs the same app as the primary domain, and each one is linked to a Tenant ID (the website). The page shows a searchable list with the columns "Key", "Display Name", "Hostname", "Tenant ID" and "Status". The "Add Domain" button opens the form to create one, and each row has edit and delete actions. A help icon opens the setup guidelines. The page is for platform super admins only.

sections.heading: Recommended setup order
sections.body: Login and sign-up on a custom URL need a satellite domain record, so register the hostname here or sign-in on that URL will not work correctly. The recommended order is: 1) Create the company organization (CRM). 2) Go to Onboarding → Add Request and enter the Tenant ID, hostname, branding and portfolio. 3) Approve the onboarding. 4) Register the Satellite Domain here with the Satellite Key, Domain URL (including the scheme), Hostname, Tenant ID and Enabled. 5) Configure DNS. 6) Configure the Clerk satellite domain on the primary. The Tenant ID must match the one in Tenant Settings and the organization. The primary domain must stay deployed for satellite sign-in to work.

sections.heading: Search and browse the list
sections.body: Type in the search box ("Search by name, key, hostname, or tenant...") to narrow the list by display name, key, hostname or tenant. Use the clear button ("Clear domain search") to reset it. Some column headers, such as Key, Display Name and Tenant ID, are sortable. At the bottom, "Previous" and "Next" move between pages, and the page shows which page you are on and a "Showing ... satellite domains" count. If nothing matches you see "No satellite domains found".

sections.heading: Add a satellite domain
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Domain" (the "Add Satellite Domain" button). 2) Under "Core Configuration", fill the required fields "Satellite Key *" (for example mosc-temp), "Display Name *", "Domain URL *" and "Hostname *" (for example www.mosc-temp.com). 3) Enter the "Tenant ID" of the website this domain belongs to, and use the "Enabled" setting to turn it on or off. 4) Fill in any optional branding, contact and auth page settings. 5) Click "Create Domain". You see "Satellite domain created successfully" when it saves. Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Required fields and messages
sections.body: Satellite Key, Display Name, Domain URL and Hostname are required. If one is empty you will see "Satellite Key is required", "Display Name is required", "Domain URL is required" or "Hostname is required". Include the scheme in the Domain URL. If the list cannot load you see "Failed to load satellite domains". Success messages appear after you create, update or delete a domain.

sections.heading: Branding, logo and colors
sections.body: In the form, the "Branding" section has "Organization Name", "Full Name" and "Tagline". Under "Logo", choose "Logo Type" as "Text" or "Image", enter a "Logo URL", and set "Logo Primary Color" and "Logo Secondary Color". "Theme Colors" has "Primary Color", "Hover Color" and "Active Color" (for example #9333ea). If a Tenant ID is filled in, a panel "Tenant settings logo (same Tenant ID)" shows the logo from Tenant Management settings. Use "Copy" to copy its URL, or "Use for satellite" to fill the Logo URL field. The message "Logo URL applied — save to persist" reminds you to save the domain afterward. If no logo exists yet, upload one under Tenant Management → Customization and come back.

sections.heading: Contact, social and auth page options
sections.body: "Contact Information" holds "Address", "Phone", "Toll Free" and "Email". The social links section (optional) has "Facebook", "Twitter / X", "LinkedIn" and "YouTube"; skip it if you don't need social icons, and you can add or edit them anytime. "Auth Page Display" has "Show on Auth Header" and "Show on Auth Footer" to control what appears on the sign-in pages of the satellite site.

sections.heading: Edit a satellite domain
sections.body: 1) Find the domain in the list. 2) Click the edit action ("Edit Satellite Domain") on its row. 3) Change the fields you need. 4) Click "Update Domain". You see "Satellite domain updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving. Keep the Tenant ID matching Tenant Settings and the organization.

sections.heading: Turn a domain on or off
sections.body: The "Status" column shows whether each domain is enabled. Click the status in the row to switch it: the hover text says "Click to disable" or "Click to enable". You can also use the "Enabled" setting in the edit form and click "Update Domain".

sections.heading: Delete a satellite domain
sections.body: 1) Click the delete action ("Delete Satellite Domain") on the row. 2) In the confirmation, click "Delete". You see "Satellite domain deleted successfully". Once the hostname is no longer registered, sign-in on that custom URL will not work correctly, so delete only when you are sure.

sections.heading: What the School site page is for
sections.body: The "School site" page (Admin > School) is where you manage the content of a school website (tenant): staff, departments, facilities, activities, pages, merit highlights, and fee invoices. Each of these has its own tab: "Staff", "Departments", "Facilities", "Activities", "Pages", "Highlights", and "Fee invoices". Each tab shows a list of records with an Edit and a Delete icon on each row. Under the list are "Previous" and "Next" buttons with the current "Page" number. Use "Back to Admin" to return to the main admin area.

sections.heading: Browse records and move between pages
sections.body: 1) Click a tab to see its records. 2) Wait while "Loading…" is shown. 3) Use "Next" and "Previous" (also the arrow buttons labelled "Next Page" and "Previous Page") to move through long lists. If a tab has nothing to show, you will see "No records on this page." Lower priority or sort numbers appear first in the lists.

sections.heading: Add or edit a record
sections.body: To change an existing record, click the Edit (pencil) icon on its row. A form opens with the fields for that tab, and you can leave it without saving by clicking "Cancel". A new or edited row is saved on the tab you are working in. If you see an add button on a tab, use it to start a new record with the same kind of form. Fields marked as required must be filled in before the record can be saved.

sections.heading: Staff tab: teachers and other people
sections.body: Staff holds teachers and all other school people. Required fields are "Category" (Administration, Teaching, or Supporting), "Stage" (All stages, KG, LP, UP, HS, or HSS), "First name", and "Last name". Optional fields include "Designation", "Qualification", "Subject", "Class teacher of", "Department id", "Email", "Phone", "Profile image URL", "Bio", "Priority order", and the "Active" checkbox. A teacher's email and phone are stored on the staff row. Do not enter teachers on the Executive Committee, which is for public officers, not school staff.

sections.heading: Departments and Facilities
sections.body: On the "Departments" tab, "Name" and "Slug" are required. You can also fill in "Summary", "Body", "Image URL", "Head staff id" (the staff record of the department head), and "Sort order". Facilities are managed on their own "Facilities" tab, and you edit and delete rows the same way as on other tabs.

sections.heading: Activities, Pages, and Highlights
sections.body: On the "Activities" tab, choose a "Kind": Club, Sport, or Program. On the "Pages" tab, which is used for content such as a principal message, "Title" is required. On the "Highlights" tab (merit names), "Person name" is required, and you can add a "Subtitle" and an "Academic year". Open a row's Edit icon to change any of these.

sections.heading: Fee invoices
sections.body: The "Fee invoices" tab lists invoices for the school. Choose a "Fee kind": Admission, Tuition, Transport, or Other. You can record "Student name", "Class", "Payer name", "Payer email", and "Payer phone" on the invoice itself. "Amount due" and "Currency" are required, and you can set a "Due date". "Status" can be Draft, Open, Paid, or Void.

sections.heading: Delete a record
sections.body: 1) Find the row on its tab. 2) Click the Delete (bin) icon. 3) When "Delete this record?" appears, confirm. If something goes wrong you will see "Delete failed", and the record is still in the list. If you only want to hide a staff row from the public pages, consider clearing its "Active" checkbox instead of deleting it.

sections.heading: Required fields, ordering, and active rows
sections.body: Required fields differ by tab: Staff needs Category, Stage, First name and Last name; Departments need Name and Slug; Pages need Title; Highlights need Person name; Fee invoices need Amount due and Currency. Lower "Priority order" or "Sort order" numbers appear first. Inactive rows stay in admin and can be left off the public school pages.

sections.heading: If something does not load
sections.body: If a tab shows "Could not load records", try switching to another tab and back, or reload the page. If a list seems empty, check that you are on the right page number; "No records on this page." means that page has nothing. If you cannot reach the page you want, use "Back to Admin" and open School site again.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Squads" page (Admin dashboard, Squads) is where you create squads and put people on them. It has a "Create squad" area for adding a new squad, and an "Assign a person to squads" area for choosing a member and saving which squads they belong to. Use the "Admin home" link to go back to the main admin dashboard. These are membership links only. They do not change the person's roster profile.

sections.heading: Create a squad
sections.body: Use the "Create squad" area to add a new squad. 1) Type the squad's name in the "Squad name" box. 2) Type a group label in the "Category (Kids, Over 40)" box, for example Kids or Over 40. 3) Click "Create squad". The new squad can then be used when you assign people to squads.

sections.heading: Assign a person to squads
sections.body: Use the "Assign a person to squads" section to set which squads one person belongs to. 1) Open "Choose a member" and pick the person. 2) Select the squads they should be on. 3) Click "Save memberships" to store your choices. Your changes are not kept until you click "Save memberships".

sections.heading: Putting one player on more than one squad
sections.body: A single player can be on more than one squad. For example, someone can be in a squad with the category Kids and also in another squad. Choose the person once under "Choose a member", select every squad they belong to, then click "Save memberships". Each squad is a separate membership link for that person.

sections.heading: What membership does and does not change
sections.body: Squad membership is only the link between a person and a squad. It is not the roster profile itself, so saving memberships does not edit the person's profile details. To change who is on a squad, choose the member again under "Choose a member", adjust their squads, and click "Save memberships". The page can also remove a membership link, so only keep the squads a person should actually belong to.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Squad groups page (titled "Team groups") is where you manage the squads and bands shown on the homepage carousel, such as First XI, Under-16 or Choir. Each group has its own roster members. The page shows a searchable list of groups with columns "Name", "Type", "Order", "Active", "Tenant" and "Actions". Above the list are search, status and sort controls and an "Add group" button. People are added to groups on the Squad roster page.

sections.heading: Filter by tenant
sections.body: Under the page heading there is a Tenant ID typeahead. Use it to show groups for one website (tenant) of an organization. It is optional: if you leave it empty, the page uses your default tenant context. A Tenant ID picks a website, not the whole organization.

sections.heading: Search, filter and sort the list
sections.body: Type in "Search team groups" and choose what to search with "Search by": "Name", "Slug", "Team type" or "Group ID". Use "Status" to show "All", "Active only" or "Inactive only" groups. Use "Sort" to order by "Order (low first)", "Order (high first)", "Name (A–Z)", "Name (Z–A)" or "Type (A–Z)". While the list updates you may see "Refreshing…". If nothing matches, you will see "No team groups found. Create one or adjust filters."

sections.heading: Create a group
sections.body: 1) Click "Add group" above the list. 2) In the "New team group" form, fill in "Name *" and choose "Team type *". 3) Optionally fill in "Display order", "Category label", "URL slug", "Section label", "Headline", "Description", "CTA label" and "CTA href". 4) Tick or untick "Active on site" to control whether the group is shown. 5) Click "Create group". Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Form fields and rules
sections.body: "Name *" is required; if it is empty you will see "Name is required". The name field suggests examples like "Kids, Over 40, Over 50". "Team type *" is required and is chosen from a list; if the list cannot be loaded you will see "Could not load team types". The type list is shown as SPORTS / MUSIC / OTHER in the page. "Display order" sets where the group appears, "Category label", "Section label", "Headline", "Description", "CTA label" and "CTA href" are optional text for how the group is presented on the site.

sections.heading: Edit a group
sections.body: 1) Find the group in the list. 2) Click "Edit" in the "Actions" column. 3) Change the details in the "Edit team group" form. 4) Save your changes, or click "Cancel" to leave without saving. To hide a group from the site without deleting it, untick "Active on site".

sections.heading: See the members of a group
sections.body: Use the "Members" action in the "Actions" column to see the people in a group. The form for an existing group also has a "View all players" button. To add people to a group, use the Squad roster page and pick the group there.

sections.heading: Delete a group
sections.body: 1) Click "Delete" in the "Actions" column of the group. 2) A "Delete team group?" confirmation appears and warns that all members in this group will be removed. 3) Confirm to delete, or click "Cancel" to keep the group. If you only want to hide the group, edit it and untick "Active on site" instead.

sections.heading: Paging and error messages
sections.body: Use "Previous" and "Next" below the list to move between pages; the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed. If the list cannot load you may see "Failed to fetch team groups:" followed by a reason, including a message that the fetch timed out after 15 seconds. Creating, updating or deleting can also show an error message if the action fails. In that case, try again or adjust your filters.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Team roster members" page lists the people inside your squads, such as players or band members. Each member has a name, sports, skills, achievements and a portrait, and belongs to a team group. At the top you will find search and filter controls, then a list with the columns "Name", "Group", "Role", "Order", "Tenant" and "Actions". The "Add member" button opens a blank form, and "Manage groups" takes you to the team groups. Paging buttons ("Previous", "Next") sit under the list.

sections.heading: Search and filter the roster
sections.body: Use "Search roster members" to look people up. 1) Pick a field in "Search by": "First name", "Last name", "Email", "Position", "Instrument" or "Member ID". 2) Type your search text. 3) Narrow the list with "Team group" (default "All groups") and "Status" ("All", "Active only" or "Inactive only"). "Refreshing…" shows while the list reloads. If nothing matches, you will see "No members found".

sections.heading: Filter by website (Tenant ID)
sections.body: The page description mentions a Tenant ID typeahead that filters the roster by website tenant. It is optional. If you leave it empty, the page uses your default tenant context. The "Tenant" column in the list shows which website each member belongs to. A tenant is one website, and one organization can own many tenants.

sections.heading: Sort and move between pages
sections.body: Use "Sort" to choose the order: "Priority (low first)", "Priority (high first)", "Last name (A–Z)" or "First name (A–Z)". The list is split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" under the list to move between them. The page number and a "Showing" count tell you where you are.

sections.heading: Add a new member
sections.body: 1) Click "Add member" to open the "New roster member" form. 2) Choose a "Team group *"; the name in brackets is the group type, such as football or music. 3) Fill in "First name *" and "Last name *". 4) Complete any other fields you need. 5) Click "Create member". If the team group or either name is missing, you will see "Team group is required" or "First and last name are required". Use "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Member details on the form
sections.body: Optional fields include "Title", "Priority order", "Jersey number", "Position", "Instrument", "Vocal role", "Lineup subtitle", "Email", "Role", "Biography", "Nationality", "Date of birth", "Preferred foot" and "Height (cm)". "Priority order" is a whole number, and lower numbers appear first. "Jersey number" is for football and should be a whole number. "User profile ID (optional)" is only for a player who already has a site account. "Biography" is the public bio. Leave a field blank if you do not have the information.

sections.heading: Sports, season and career, and coach
sections.body: Under "Sports categories", tick every sport the member plays; more than one can be selected. Each ticked sport gets its own section, except football, which uses "Season and career". There you can enter "Season label", "Pass accuracy %", "Shot accuracy %", "Top speed (km/h)", "Career appearances", "Career goals" and "Career assists", and leave any number blank if unknown. You can also enter "Coach name", "Coach email" and "Coach phone". If no sports are listed, you will see "No active sports yet. Add them under Roster catalogs."

sections.heading: Achievements and skills
sections.body: In "Achievements", click "+ Add achievement" to add one card per award. Fill in the title, the "Date", the "Category" (choose from the list, or "Select a category") and a "Description". Every achievement needs a category, or you will see "Each achievement needs a category". If a category is missing, add it under Roster catalogs. Click "Remove achievement" to delete a card. Under "Skills / expertise", click "+ Add skill" and type one skill per box, for example Free kicks. Blank boxes are ignored.

sections.heading: Portrait and public visibility
sections.body: Under "Portrait image", upload a clear head-and-shoulders photo in JPG or PNG format, with the face fully visible. The "Active on roster" checkbox controls whether the member shows on the public roster. Untick it to hide the member without deleting the profile. Members hidden this way appear under "Inactive only" in the "Status" filter.

sections.heading: Edit or delete a member
sections.body: To change a member, click "Edit" in the "Actions" column. This opens the "Edit roster member" form. Change what you need and save it. To remove a member, click "Delete". A "Delete member?" confirmation appears. Confirm to delete, or click "Cancel" to keep them. To hide someone without losing their profile, untick "Active on roster" instead.

sections.heading: Error messages
sections.body: If the list cannot load, you will see "Failed to fetch team members:" followed by a reason. A fetch can also fail if it takes longer than 15 seconds. On the form, "Could not load sports catalogs" and "Could not load achievements" mean those parts did not load. Try again, or reload the page. Messages that start with "Error creating team member", "Error updating team member" or "Error deleting team member" mean that action did not complete.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Tenant Email Addresses" page lets you configure the verified "From" email addresses for this tenant (website), sorted by type such as info, sales, support or noreply. These addresses are used when the platform sends emails. They are official sender or contact addresses, not a one-off campaign. At the top you will find the "Add Email Address" button and a search box. Below is a list of addresses with paging at the bottom ("Previous", "Page", "Next") and a count line starting with "Showing". Each row has actions to view details, edit and delete. The page also has an "Email configuration guide" note explaining the From, Copy-To and Reply-To fields.

sections.heading: Add an email address
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Email Address". 2) In the "Add Tenant Email Address" window, choose the "Email Type" (INFO, SALES, TICKETS, CONTACT, SUPPORT, MARKETING, NOREPLY or ADMIN). 3) Enter the "From" email address, which is required. 4) Optionally fill in "Copy-To", "Reply-To", "Display Name" (for example Customer Support or Sales Team) and "Description". 5) Set "Active" and "Default for this type" as needed. 6) Click "Create Email Address". A message confirms "Email address created successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: From, Copy-To and Reply-To
sections.body: "From (required)" is the address emails are sent from. "Copy-To (optional)" sends a duplicate of outbound messages to that address, for example a manager CC'd on contact form submissions; leave it empty if no extra copy is needed. "Reply-To (optional)" is where replies go, for example support@yourorg.org. Copy-To and Reply-To, if provided, must each differ from the From address. The page notes that you should contact the platform administrator to add or verify sender addresses in AWS SES before use.

sections.heading: Active, Default and Display Name
sections.body: "Active" marks whether the address is turned on for use. "Default for this type" marks the address as the default for its email type. "Display Name" is a friendly name for the address, such as Customer Support or Sales Team. "Description" is an optional note about how the address is used. These are set in the add and edit windows and saved when you click "Create Email Address" or "Save Changes".

sections.heading: Search and browse the list
sections.body: Type in the search box ("Search by email, display name, or type...") and click "Search" to filter the list. Use the clear button ("Clear email search") to remove the search. The list shows columns including type, "From Email Address", "Copy-To Address", "Reply-To Address", "Display Name", "Active" and "Default". Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. If nothing matches, you see "No email addresses match your search."; if none exist yet, "No tenant email addresses configured yet."

sections.heading: View full details
sections.body: Hover over a row ("Hover for full email address details") or use the "View details" action to see a details panel. It shows ID, Tenant ID, Type, From Email, Copy-To, Reply-To, Display Name, Active, Default, Description, Created At and Updated At. Close the panel with the "Close" button.

sections.heading: Edit an email address
sections.body: 1) Find the address in the list. 2) Click "Edit email address" in its row. 3) In the "Edit Tenant Email Address" window, change the fields you need. 4) Click "Save Changes". A message confirms "Email address updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Delete an email address
sections.body: 1) Click "Delete email address" in the row of the address you want to remove. 2) The "Delete Tenant Email Address" window asks you to confirm and warns that this action cannot be undone. 3) Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to keep it. A message confirms "Email address deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Rules and error messages
sections.body: The email address and the email type are required. Copy-To and Reply-To must differ from the From address when provided. A tenant cannot have the same From address twice for the same email type; if you try, you are told to edit the existing address or use a different From address or type. Other messages you may see are "Failed to load tenant email addresses", "Failed to create email address" and "Failed to update email address". Changes are saved when you click "Create Email Address", "Save Changes" or "Delete".

sections.heading: Overview of Tenant Organizations
sections.body: An organization is the client (a company, institution, or person) that signs up. It can own many website tenant IDs. The main page, "Tenant Organizations", lists organizations with the columns "Organization Name", "Tenant IDs", "Website / Domain", "Contact Email", "Organization charge", "Status" and "Actions". Above the list you will find the search box, the status filters, the "Create New" button, and a button for creating a website Tenant ID through onboarding. Click an organization to open its detail page, which has "Organization Details", a tenant ID list, billing scope, "Actions" and "Suspension". Related pages are New Organization, Edit Organization, Search organizations, and the move pages.

sections.heading: Find organizations in the list
sections.body: On the "Tenant Organizations" page, type in the box "Search by organization name, tenant ID, or domain..." to narrow the list. Use the status drop-down ("All Statuses", "Active", "Inactive", "Suspended") and the second filter ("All Organizations", "Active Only", "Inactive Only"). If nothing matches you will see "No organizations found". Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to change pages; the footer shows "Page" and "Showing" counts. Hover over a row to see full organization details in a pop-up, and click the × button to close it.

sections.heading: Advanced search and export
sections.body: Open "Search organizations" (the search button at the top of the list, or the /search page) to filter by any combination of fields.
