Fields are "Organization name", "Domain", "Contact email", "Contact person", "Phone", "City", "State", "ZIP", "Country", "Website URL" and "Website tenant ID", plus the drop-downs "Site type", "Subscription status" and an active/inactive choice. Each text field matches anywhere in the value. 1) Fill in the filters. 2) Click "Search". 3) Use "Previous" and "Next" to page through results. Click "Clear" to reset the filters. "Export results" downloads every match, and "Export all organizations" downloads the full table; if nothing matched, the file only has the column headers.

sections.heading: Create a new organization
sections.body: 1) On the "Tenant Organizations" page click "Create New". 2) Fill in "Organization Name *", "Contact Email *", "Contact Phone *" and "Contact person name *", and the address fields (address line 1, city, state / province, ZIP / postal code and country are required). 3) Optionally add "Domain" (leave it empty if there is none yet), "Description", "Website URL", and a "Monthly charge (USD)". 4) Click "Create Organization". The name must be unique, and the domain must not already be registered. This creates only the organization; the website tenant ID is added later through onboarding.

sections.heading: Form rules and limits
sections.body: Required fields are marked with *: organization name, contact email, contact phone and contact person name, plus address line 1, city, state / province, ZIP / postal code and country. Organization name and contact person name must be under 255 characters, phone under 50, address lines 255 or less, ZIP 20 or less and country 100 or less. The email must be valid. You will see messages such as "An organization with this name already exists." or "This domain is already registered." if there is a clash. The "Active Organization" checkbox controls status; inactive organizations cannot be used for new events or registrations. The "Monthly charge (USD)" covers every tenant ID under the organization; an amount above 0.00 turns the charge on, and 0.00 leaves it off.

sections.heading: Edit an organization
sections.body: 1) Open the organization from the list. 2) Click "Edit Organization" (or use the edit action in the list row). 3) Change the company information, contact or address fields. 4) Click "Update Organization". After saving you are sent back to the organization page. Tenant ID, domain hostnames and branding are not edited here; they stay in Onboarding and tenant settings. Use "Cancel" to leave without saving.

sections.heading: Read the organization page
sections.body: The organization page shows "Organization Details": "Status", "Database ID (PK)", "Organization Name", "Contact Email", "Contact Phone", "Contact person name", "Website URL", "Address", "Created At" and "Updated At". It also shows the "Organization monthly charge", which is one charge for the whole organization; tenant IDs under it are complimentary and not billed on their own. The "Tenant IDs" list shows each website with its "Tenant ID" and "Status", with "View" and "Edit" in the "Settings" column. If the organization has none you will see "No tenant IDs yet". If the link is wrong you will see "This organization is no longer available"; use "Back to Organizations".

sections.heading: Set the billing scope
sections.body: The billing scope card on the organization page lets you choose "Bill the organization once" or "Bill each website separately". 1) Choose an option. 2) For one subscription, enter a "Monthly amount" greater than zero; for separate billing, enter zero or more. 3) Click "Save billing scope". The organization needs at least one website tenant before it can be billed as one subscription. When billed separately, each website stays complimentary until its own charge switch is turned on. "Open billing area" takes you to billing.

sections.heading: Move tenant IDs between organizations
sections.body: There are two ways. To move one tenant ID into an organization: 1) Click "Move a tenant ID to this organization" on the organization page, or pick the receiving organization on the move page and continue. 2) Type the tenant ID and click "Look up tenant ID". 3) Click "Move to this organization". To move between two organizations, click "Move tenant IDs between two organizations", choose two different organizations, and drag a tenant ID onto the other column or use "Move to the other organization". Dropping a tenant ID onto the organization it already belongs to does nothing, and you cannot move one that is already on the organization.

sections.heading: Suspend websites or dashboards
sections.body: The "Suspension" section on the organization page can turn off the public websites, the dashboards, or both for every tenant ID in the organization, for example after missed payments. 1) Open the suspension dialog. 2) Switch on "Turn off the public website" and/or "Turn off dashboard access". 3) Optionally add an "Internal note (optional)", visible only to super admins. 4) Save. Nothing is deleted, and turning a switch off brings access back. The Billing page stays open for tenant admins. In the tenant ID list, "Suspend" on a row affects just that site. The hub you are signed in to cannot be suspended from here. "See everything that is suspended" shows the full overview.

sections.heading: Make inactive or cascade delete
sections.body: If you see the options in the row actions, you can "Make inactive" or "Cascade Delete". Making inactive keeps the organization, its tenant settings, email addresses, satellite domains and onboarding requests, and you can make it active again. Cascade delete removes the organization and related tenant settings, tenant email addresses and satellite domains; websites that belong to it become their own organizations. It cannot be undone, although onboarding requests, user profiles and events are kept. 1) Click the cascade delete action. 2) Type the organization name to confirm. 3) Click "Cascade delete now". Choose "Keep organization" or "Make inactive instead" to avoid deleting.

sections.heading: Create a website tenant ID
sections.body: A new organization does not include a website tenant ID. After the organization exists, use "Create Tenant ID via onboarding" on the list, or "Onboard a tenant ID" on the organization page, to go to Onboarding and start a new request. There you set the tenant ID, hostname or domain, branding and portfolio membership. A tenant ID can use only lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. For a custom domain, also register it under Satellite Domains so sign-in and branding work on that URL.

sections.heading: What this page is for and where things are
sections.body: The "Suspend sites and dashboards" page lets you turn off a tenant ID's public website, its admin and retail dashboards, or both. Nothing is deleted. The page has an organization picker (labelled "Organization", starting at "All organizations"), a search box, a "Tenant IDs" list with the columns "Tenant ID", "Organization", "Status" and "Change", and a "Currently suspended" summary. Use "Back to Admin Dashboard" to leave. This is for platform super admins only. If the suspended list cannot load, you see a message asking you to refresh the page.

sections.heading: Find a tenant ID
sections.body: The "Tenant IDs" list shows every tenant ID until you pick an organization. To search, 1) type in the box "Search by tenant ID" 2) click "Search" (the magnifier button). Click "Clear" or "Clear search" to reset it. While the list loads you see "Loading tenant IDs...", and if nothing matches you see "No tenant IDs match." Use "Previous" and "Next" under the list to move between pages.

sections.heading: Work on one organization
sections.body: Use the "Organization" picker to choose an organization. The list then shows only that organization and its tenant IDs. You can also click "Show only this organization" on a row to narrow the list to that row's organization. Choose "All organizations" to see everything again. When an organization is selected, a hint tells you to use "Suspend all" to turn off every tenant ID it owns at once.

sections.heading: Suspend one tenant ID
sections.body: To turn off a single website (tenant ID), 1) find its row in the "Tenant IDs" list 2) click the button in the "Change" column, which says "Suspend" (or "Suspended: change" if it is already suspended) 3) in the window, tick "Turn off the public website" and/or "Turn off dashboard access" 4) optionally add an "Internal note (optional)" 5) save. The window shows what it applies to under "This applies to". The "Status" column shows "Live", "Website off" or "Dashboard off".

sections.heading: Suspend a whole organization
sections.body: To turn off every tenant ID an organization owns at once, 1) pick the organization in the "Organization" picker 2) click "Suspend all" 3) choose the switches "Turn off the public website" and/or "Turn off dashboard access" 4) add an optional note and save. The dialog's "By organization" wording shows it covers all of that organization's tenant IDs. The "Currently suspended" area also lists "Organizations (every tenant ID they own)" that are suspended this way.

sections.heading: What each option does
sections.body: "Turn off the public website": visitors see a page saying the site is temporarily unavailable, and sign-in still works. "Turn off dashboard access": tenant admins and retail users see a notice in place of the admin and retail dashboards, while the Billing page stays open so they can pay. "Internal note (optional)" is seen only by super admins, not by visitors or tenant admins. Use a note such as "For example: two missed monthly payments" to record the reason. Platform super admins are never locked out.

sections.heading: Bring a site back (re-enable)
sections.body: To restore access, 1) open the same tenant ID row or organization by clicking "Suspended: change" (or the organization's change button) 2) turn the switches off again 3) save. Nothing was deleted, so everything returns as it was. Use "Cancel" to close the window without changing anything. Changes reach live sites within about a minute.

sections.heading: See what is currently suspended
sections.body: The "Currently suspended" section lists suspended items along with their "Note". If nothing is suspended it says "Nothing is suspended right now." Organizations suspended as a whole appear under "Organizations (every tenant ID they own)". Click the change button on an entry to adjust or lift it.

sections.heading: Limits and error messages
sections.body: The hub you are signed in to cannot be suspended: its own tenant ID, and any organization that owns it, cannot be suspended from here. Platform super admins are never locked out. Changes are saved only when you save in the window, and "The suspension could not be saved." appears if saving fails. Other messages you may see include "Could not load that tenant ID", "Could not load organizations", "Could not load tenant IDs" and "That organization no longer exists." If saving reports the backend did not save the suspension, the suspension settings have to be deployed on the backend first.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Test CRUD Operations" page (Admin Dashboard > Tenant Management > Test CRUD Operations) lets you test Create, Read, Update and Delete operations for tenant management. It is a platform test screen, not a customer workflow. The page has a "Test Controls" panel with four buttons, a "Test Results" area with the tabs "All Tests", "Organizations" and "Settings", and a "Test Logs" area that shows progress. The breadcrumb at the top lets you go back to "Admin Dashboard" or "Tenant Management".

sections.heading: Run all tests
sections.body: Use this to check organization and settings operations in one go. 1) Open the "Test Controls" panel. 2) Click "Run All Tests". 3) While it runs, the page shows "Running tests..." and "Please wait while the tests are running. Check the logs below for progress." The log starts with "Starting comprehensive CRUD operations test..." and ends with "All tests passed!" or "Some tests failed".

sections.heading: Test organizations only
sections.body: Click "Test Organizations Only" in "Test Controls" to run only the organization checks. The log starts with "Starting organization CRUD tests..." and ends with "Organization tests passed!" or "Organization tests failed". The test uses a sample record named "Test Organization" with the description "A test organization for CRUD testing", country "United States". The test later changes its description to "Updated test organization description". If a created organization comes back without an ID, the test reports "Created organization missing ID".

sections.heading: Test settings only
sections.body: Click "Test Settings Only" in "Test Controls" to run only the website settings checks. The log starts with "Starting settings CRUD tests..." and ends with "Settings tests passed!" or "Settings tests failed". If the created settings come back without an ID, the test reports "Created settings missing ID". Settings errors, such as settings already existing for a tenant, a missing required database column, or a tenant not belonging to your organization, may also appear in the log.

sections.heading: Read the results and logs
sections.body: Results appear under "Test Results", which has the tabs "All Tests", "Organizations" and "Settings". Click a tab to see results for that group. The "Test Logs" area shows step-by-step output. Before any test is run it says "No logs yet. Run a test to see the output."

sections.heading: Clear results
sections.body: Click "Clear Results" in "Test Controls" to remove the current results and logs from the page. After clearing, the "Test Logs" area goes back to showing "No logs yet. Run a test to see the output." Use it before a new run if you want a clean view.

sections.heading: Things to know
sections.body: This is a platform test screen, so use it only for testing. The tests create and change sample records through the same actions the settings pages use. Wait for "Running tests..." to finish before reading the final result. If a test fails, check "Test Logs" for the message.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Use the Test Stripe page to run a test card payment in Stripe and confirm checkout works before a real ticket sale. The main page is titled "Test Stripe Integration" and is at /admin/test-stripe. It has a "Test Amount (USD)" field, a "Test Card Numbers" reference list, and a "Test Stripe Payment" button. After a successful payment you land on a confirmation page at /admin/test-stripe/success titled "Test Payment Successful!".

sections.heading: Run a test payment
sections.body: The page creates a test checkout session and sends you to Stripe's payment page. 1) Open the Test Stripe page. 2) Enter an amount in the "Test Amount (USD)" field. 3) Click "Test Stripe Payment". 4) While the button shows "Creating Checkout Session...", wait to be redirected to Stripe. 5) On Stripe's page, enter one of the test card numbers and finish the payment.

sections.heading: Choosing the test amount
sections.body: The "Test Amount (USD)" field is in US dollars. The hint under it says "Enter an amount between $0.01 and $999.99". Use a minimal amount for testing.

sections.heading: Test card numbers and card details
sections.body: The "Test Card Numbers" box lists cards for different outcomes: "Success:", "Decline:", "Insufficient Funds:", "Expired Card:" and "Incorrect CVC:". Pick the one for the result you want to check and enter it on Stripe's payment page. The page says to use any future expiry date and any 3-digit CVC for testing.

sections.heading: After a successful payment
sections.body: When the payment completes, the "Test Payment Successful!" page says "Your test Stripe transaction was completed successfully." Under "Transaction Details" you see the "Session ID:" and the "Status:", which shows "Completed". Click "Test Another Payment" to run another test. Click "Back to Admin" to return to the admin area. The "Admin Home" link is also on this page.

sections.heading: Canceled payments and error messages
sections.body: If you leave Stripe's page without paying, the test page shows "Payment was canceled." You can click "Test Stripe Payment" to try again. Other messages you may see are "Failed to create test checkout session", "No checkout URL received" and "An error occurred during checkout". These mean the checkout could not start. Try again, and check your Stripe setup if it keeps happening.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Tournaments are seasons or cups for a sports-team website. The Tournaments tile appears only when the organization's site type is a sports team. The list page shows a table with the columns "Menu label", "Title", "Year", "Status", "In menu" and "Actions", plus a "New tournament" button and a search and filter area. If you see "Select a tenant to manage tournaments.", pick a tenant (website) first. Each row has an "Edit tournament" action and a "Delete tournament" action. If nothing has been added you will see "No tournaments yet."

sections.heading: Create a new tournament
sections.body: 1) Choose a sports team tenant, since the page shows "Select a sports team tenant before creating a tournament." if none is selected. 2) On the Tournaments list, click "New tournament". 3) Fill in the form, at minimum the title and the "Short label (menu item, unique)". 4) Click "Save tournament". While saving you see "Please wait while the tournament is saved.", then "Tournament saved. Returning to the list." and you are taken back to the list. Click "Cancel" to leave without saving.

sections.heading: Tournament form fields
sections.body: The form includes: "Short label (menu item, unique)", "Year (optional)", "Welcome text", "Details text", "Age group label", "Chief guest name", "Chief guest image", "Fixtures image", "Registration email", "External results URL (Tournify)", "External results link label" and "Legacy page URL". It also has a "Status" selection and a "Published" option. A title and a slug are also checked when you save. Fill in only what applies to your tournament; fields marked optional can be left blank.

sections.heading: Edit a tournament
sections.body: 1) On the Tournaments list, click the "Edit tournament" action (pencil) in the row. 2) Change the fields you need. 3) Click "Save tournament"; a "Saved Successfully!" message confirms it and you return to the list. If the tournament cannot be found you will see "Tournament not found." Use "Cancel" to leave without saving changes.

sections.heading: Upload images
sections.body: The "Chief guest image" and "Fixtures image" fields each have an "Upload image" button. Until you upload, the field shows "No image uploaded yet", and a "Clear" button removes the current image. Upload stores the image and puts its URL on this tournament, but you must still click "Save tournament" to keep it. Accepted types are PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP, and the file must be under 10MB. You may see "Please select an image file", "File size must be less than 10MB", "Select a tenant before uploading an image" or "Image upload failed" if something is wrong.

sections.heading: Show a tournament in the header menu
sections.body: Tick the option that reads "Show this tournament in the header. The short label is the menu item. Saving with this checked turns it off for every other tournament of this tenant." Only one tournament per tenant can be in the header at a time. If another tournament is already shown, you may see "Another tournament is already shown in the header. Save again so this one replaces it." and should click save again. The "In menu" column on the list shows which tournament is in the menu.

sections.heading: Status and publishing
sections.body: Use the "Status" selection to mark a tournament as "Upcoming", "In progress" or "Completed". The "Published" option controls whether the tournament is published. The list shows each tournament's status in the "Status" column. Changes take effect when you click "Save tournament".

sections.heading: Search and filter the list
sections.body: Use the "Search tournaments" area above the table. 1) Under "Search by", choose "Tournament name", "Menu label" or "Year". 2) Type in the box labelled "Type to search". 3) Optionally set "Shown in header" to "All", "Enabled" or "Not enabled". 4) Optionally set "Status" to "Upcoming", "In progress", "Completed", "Published" or "Not published". 5) Click "Apply". Click "Clear" to reset the filters.

sections.heading: Delete a tournament
sections.body: 1) On the Tournaments list, find the tournament's row. 2) Click the "Delete tournament" action in the "Actions" column. 3) Follow any confirmation that appears. If it does not work you will see "Delete failed".

sections.heading: Rules and error messages
sections.body: The short label is required and must be 40 characters or fewer, and it must be unique. The title is required. The slug may contain only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. If saving fails you will see "Save failed. Please try again." Images are saved only after you click "Save tournament", even though the upload itself happens immediately.

sections.heading: What the WhatsApp pages are for
sections.body: The WhatsApp pages let you send WhatsApp messages to many recipients for this tenant (website) and monitor how they perform. There are two pages. "WhatsApp Bulk Messaging" (/admin/whatsapp/bulk-messaging) is where you write and send a campaign; it shows the cards "Messages Sent Today", "Delivery Rate", "Active Recipients" and "Campaigns This Month", plus "Settings" and "Analytics" options. "WhatsApp Dashboard" (/admin/whatsapp/dashboard) is where you monitor results, with the tabs "Analytics", "Message History", "Delivery Status" and "Usage Alerts". If something goes wrong, a "WhatsApp Integration Error" screen may appear with "Try Again" and "Go to Admin" buttons.

sections.heading: Send a bulk message: the steps
sections.body: Sending a campaign is a guided flow with a progress bar at the top. The steps are 1) "Compose Message", 2) "Select Recipients", 3) "Schedule (Optional)", 4) "Review & Send" and 5) "Sending Messages". Use "Continue" to move forward and "Previous" to go back. When the campaign finishes you see "Messages sent successfully!" and can open the delivery report.

sections.heading: Write your message or use a template
sections.body: In "Compose Your Message", 1) choose a "Message Type": "Transactional" or "Marketing". Transactional messages can be sent anytime, while marketing messages have restrictions. 2) To use a template, turn on "Use Message Template" and pick one under "Select Template" ("Choose a template..."); the examples are Welcome Message, Event Reminder, Payment Confirmation and Newsletter. Only approved templates can be selected. 3) Otherwise type in "Message Content" ("Type your WhatsApp message here..."). 4) If the template has "Template Variables", fill them in. The "Message Preview" box shows how it will look, and "Clear" resets the form. Click "Continue to Recipients" when done.

sections.heading: Add recipients manually or by CSV
sections.body: In "Select Recipients", use "Add Recipients" and choose "Add Individual" or "Upload CSV". For one person, fill in "Phone Number *" (required), optionally "Name (Optional)" and "Email (Optional)", then click "Add Recipient" (or "Cancel"). For a file, upload a .csv with the columns phone,name,email where phone is required, for example +1234567890,John Doe,john@example.com. If the list is empty, click "Add Your First Recipient". Phone numbers must be in a valid format such as +1234567890.

sections.heading: Search and clear the recipient list
sections.body: Once recipients are added, use the "Search recipients..." box to find someone in the list. If nothing matches you see "No recipients match your search"; try different search terms. "Clear All" removes all recipients from the list. When the list is ready, a "Ready to Send" note appears (large campaigns may take time to process) and you click "Continue to Preview".

sections.heading: Schedule messages or send now
sections.body: The "Schedule Messages (Optional)" step lets you send at a specific time or send immediately. In the composer, "Schedule Message (Optional)" says "Leave empty to send immediately". So to send now, leave the schedule empty; to send later, set the date and time. The chosen time appears as "Scheduled:" in the review summary.

sections.heading: Preview and validate before sending
sections.body: "Preview & Validate" lets you review your message and recipients. Switch the preview between "Mobile" and "Desktop" and use "Preview with Recipient:" to see it for a specific person. "Campaign Summary" shows message details (type, characters, template, schedule), recipient counts ("Total Recipients:", "With Names:") and "Estimates" for cost and time. If there are problems an "Issues Found" box lists them, such as missing message content, no recipients, invalid phone numbers, a message over 4096 characters, or more than 1000 marketing recipients in a day. Click "Edit Message" to go back, or "Confirm & Continue" to send; you must confirm before messages are sent.

sections.heading: Watch and stop sending
sections.body: "Sending Progress" shows the live counts "Sent", "Delivered", "Failed" and "Remaining", the "Delivery Rate", "Estimated Time Remaining" and "Recent Activity". Messages are sent at a rate that complies with WhatsApp's messaging policies. To halt the campaign, click "Stop" and confirm; stopping cannot be undone. When it ends you see "Sending Complete" and can view the delivery report.

sections.heading: Read the delivery report and retry failures
sections.body: After a campaign, "Delivery Report" shows "Total Sent", "Delivered", "Failed", "Success Rate", a "Performance Summary" and a "Campaign Overview". The "All Messages" list shows each recipient, phone, status and time. The "Failed Messages" list shows the reason (for example "Invalid phone number format") and a "Retry" button for each message; if none failed you see "No Failed Messages". Click "Export Report" to download the report, or "Start New Campaign" to begin again.

sections.heading: Use the WhatsApp Dashboard and date range
sections.body: The "WhatsApp Dashboard" shows summary cards: "Total Messages", "Delivery Rate", "Active Campaigns" and "Failed Messages". Under "Date Range:" pick a "Start date" and "End date", or use the quick buttons "Last 7 days", "Last 30 days" or "Last 3 months". Switch between the tabs "Analytics", "Message History", "Delivery Status" and "Usage Alerts". If data cannot load you see "Failed to load analytics".

sections.heading: Analytics and exporting data
sections.body: The "Analytics" tab shows an "Analytics Overview" (total, sent, delivered and failed messages, plus delivery, success and read rates), "Message Trends" with "Daily Volume", and a "Delivery Status" breakdown. If the chosen period has no data you see "No data available for selected period". Under "Data Export", click "Export CSV" to download the data. The "Export PDF" button is shown, but the page notes that PDF export is still to be implemented.

sections.heading: Search, filter and export message history
sections.body: On the "Message History" tab, type in the search box ("Search messages by content, recipient, or ID...") and pick a status from the filter: "All Statuses", "Sent", "Delivered", "Read" or "Failed". The list "Recent Messages" shows recipient, message content, status and sent time; use "Previous" and "Next" to page through. Click "View" on a row to open "Message Details" with status timeline, template and campaign, and error details if it failed. For failed messages, "Retry Send" tries again. "Export CSV" downloads the messages.

sections.heading: Track delivery status in real time
sections.body: The "Delivery Status" tab ("Real-time Delivery Status") shows counts for total, sent, delivered, read and failed messages and a "Message Status Grid" with message ID, recipient, status, sent and last updated times. Use "Filter by Status" (All Statuses, Sent, Delivered, Read, Failed, Pending) or tick "Show failed messages only". "Auto-refresh" updates the list every 30 seconds, and "Refresh" updates it right away. In a row, click "Details" to open "Message Details" or "Retry" to resend a failed message; "Close" shuts the details.

sections.heading: Review alerts and set thresholds
sections.body: The "Usage Alerts" tab ("Usage Alerts & Monitoring") shows alert counts ("Total Alerts", "Active Alerts", "Critical", "Action Required") and usage figures for messages against the monthly limit, estimated cost against the monthly budget, and failure rate against its threshold. Narrow the list with "Filter by Category" (Usage, Cost, Performance, Quota, Delivery) and "Filter by Severity" (High, Medium, Low); "Clear Filters" resets them. On an alert use "Resolve" or "Dismiss". To change settings, click "Alert Settings", set "Usage Threshold (%)", "Cost Threshold (%)" and "Failure Rate Threshold (%)", turn on "Enable Email Notifications" or "Enable SMS Notifications", choose "Notification Frequency" (Immediate, Daily Summary or Weekly Summary), then click "Save Settings" or "Cancel".

sections.heading: Limits and rules to know
sections.body: Message content is required and cannot exceed 4096 characters. At least one recipient is required, and every recipient needs a valid phone number (for example +1234567890). Marketing messages are limited to 1000 recipients per day, and transactional messages can be sent anytime. Only approved templates can be selected. CSV uploads must be .csv files with the columns phone,name,email, and only phone is required. Stopping a campaign in progress cannot be undone.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "WhatsApp Settings" page (/admin/whatsapp-settings) is where you set up the WhatsApp integration for your organization. At the top are two action buttons, "Send Messages" and "Analytics". Below them, the "WhatsApp Integration Statistics" area shows four figures: "Integration Status", "Templates", "Messages Sent" and "Delivery Rate". Under that is the "WhatsApp Integration Settings" section, which holds the integration credentials and templates for this tenant (website). While the form loads you see "Loading WhatsApp settings form...".

sections.heading: Reading the integration statistics
sections.body: The "WhatsApp Integration Statistics" area gives a quick health check. "Integration Status" shows "Not Configured" until the integration is set up. "Templates" shows how many message templates you have (0 at the moment on a new setup). "Messages Sent" shows how many messages have gone out. "Delivery Rate" shows "Delivery rate not available" when there is no data yet.

sections.heading: Configure the WhatsApp integration
sections.body: In the "WhatsApp Integration Settings" section you will find the "WhatsApp Integration" card with the text "Configure your WhatsApp Business API settings". 1) Open the "WhatsApp Settings" page. 2) Scroll to the "WhatsApp Integration Setup" panel. 3) Click "Configure Integration" to start the configuration process. Note that the panel currently says "This is a simplified version to test the basic page structure.", so the full form may not be available yet.

sections.heading: Send messages
sections.body: Click "Send Messages" near the top of the page to go to the bulk messaging screen, where you can send WhatsApp messages. The button is described as navigating to the bulk messaging interface.

sections.heading: View analytics
sections.body: Click "Analytics" near the top of the page to see WhatsApp messaging analytics and performance metrics. Use it to review how your messages are performing.

sections.heading: If an error appears
sections.body: If something goes wrong, a "WhatsApp Integration Error" panel appears with the message "Something went wrong with the WhatsApp integration". It may show a "Suggestion:" and a "Technical Details" section with Error Code, Category, Severity, Timestamp and Context. 1) Click "Try Again" to retry. 2) Or click "Go to Admin" to leave the page. Smaller error messages may also offer "Retry" or "Dismiss". If the problem persists, contact support and include the error details shown.
